title: Placebo and dollar-matched audit of LVRL's anchored frontier critic on released V-curves
statement: Re-run LVRL's value-critic prompt (frontier model, k = 3 sibling summaries, group pass rate, stated outcome, endpoint anchors applied after prediction) on the 107 failed SWE-bench Verified trajectories whose Monte-Carlo prefix-value curves 2610.17633 released (47 + 60 curves, about 331 executed continuations each, 8 base runs per task supplying mu_G and siblings), and score each arm's largest predicted value drop by the share of the run's measured loss it captures (2610.17633's value-captured score VC_k), stratified by trajectory third, plus per-curve Spearman with V-hat. Arms: the base critic (3 repeats), the same critic with k = 0 siblings (LVRL's own unanswered anchors-vs-siblings split), a placebo critic told the wrong outcome and shown another task's siblings, the critic's marginal-matched shuffle (CWGT's control), the random-step expectation (GRPO's uniform split, also what the anchors alone produce), the linear-decay estimator V_lin(t) = p(x)(1 - t/T), a dollar-matched Monte-Carlo arm (K = 4 continuations subsampled from the released continuations, costing what one frontier call costs), the policy's own forward self-estimate (P('yes') to 'will this run succeed?' at each prefix), and the outcome-conditioned log-ratio from the open-weight policy Qwen3.6-27B as a replication of CWGT on a second environment. Zero environment compute: the ground truth is already executed.
claim: On long-horizon SWE failures the frontier critic locates lost value better than a uniform split only in the final third of a trajectory, that advantage disappears when the stated outcome is wrong, and four fresh continuations at the same dollars track the executable step value more closely than the critic; what LVRL pays for is outcome-reading, not step-reading.
trick: Take failed agent runs whose step-by-step success odds were already measured by replay, ask the frontier critic where the run was lost, lie to it about the ending, and price four fresh continuations at the same dollars; see which answer moves and which tracks the truth.
why_now: 2610.17633 (2026-10-13) released code, curves and labels for 36,296 executed continuations on SWE-bench Verified; LVRL (2026-10-11) published the exact critic prompt and its own 44% / 78% / 88% early / middle / late sign-agreement numbers with no placebo or shuffle, and states in its limitations that separating the free anchors from the paid siblings and distilling the critic are future work; CWGT 2608.19760 (Aug 2026) fixed the audit protocol (marginal-matched shuffle, pre-registered plan) but graded only judge scores, log-ratios and confidence, on ALFWorld.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): on the released curves compute VC_2 for the oracle step t* and for a uniformly random step with a bootstrap over continuations; the instrument has resolution only if the oracle-vs-random gap is significant across the pooled 107 curves; also confirm the release carries per-continuation outcomes and at least 15 probed steps per curve (else regenerate K = 8 screening curves for 20 trajectories, ~2,000 continuations, ~25 GPU-hours). Step 1 (about $550 in API calls: 107 trajectories x 6 critic calls at 50-150k input tokens each, plus 432 sibling summaries; about 10 GPU-hours for log-ratio and self-estimate scoring with Qwen3.6-27B; 5 days): run all arms, report VC_2 and Spearman by trajectory third with bootstrap intervals, the base critic's own repeat spread, and the split-half Spearman of V-hat as the ceiling.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Step 0: the oracle's and the random step's VC_2 intervals overlap on 107 curves, so about 331 continuations per curve cannot separate a perfect localizer from chance; the ruler is dead at $0. Step 1 kills the claim if the base critic's VC_2 beats both its shuffle and the random expectation in the first third AND the placebo arm leaves the predicted largest drop unchanged in most trajectories AND the critic's median per-curve Spearman is within 0.05 of the dollar-matched K = 4 MC arm: the critic then reads step evidence as well as running the policy does, LVRL's framing stands, and the result is a one-paragraph confirmation.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment: first third, base critic inside its shuffle's interval (consistent with LVRL's own 44%), Spearman ~0.5 against ~0.4 for linear decay and ~0.7 for K = 4 MC (ceiling ~0.85 from split halves); final third, VC_2 two to three times the random expectation; the wrong-outcome placebo moves the predicted largest drop in more than 60% of trajectories and the final-third advantage collapses to the shuffle level; the k = 0 arm is indistinguishable from k = 3; the policy self-estimate is indistinguishable from linear decay.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: LVRL section 4.4 reads the critic as tracking 'semantic progress' and calls it policy-aware; the 26 in-context or frozen LLM value-critic recipes for agents in the 12-month arXiv window treat the per-step guess as step evidence and treat Monte-Carlo continuations as unaffordable at training time; CWGT found outcome conditioning adds no causal information for log-ratios (partial correlation -0.004) and left anchored frontier critics unaudited.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the critic beats its shuffle, survives the placebo and matches MC early, a frontier model carries forward-looking value on long-horizon SWE runs: the cheap forward estimator 2610.17633 asks for and the distillation target LVRL's limitation asks for, usable by restart controllers. If it does not, the endpoint anchors plus a uniform split (plain GRPO) are an equal credit signal at $0 for the first two thirds, credit recipes should spend the critic budget on continuations at a few anchors, and every LLM-critic paper owes a placebo arm and a dollar-matched MC arm.

identifiability: V(h_t) is random given the frozen agent's sampling temperature (0.70, top-p 0.80) and the remaining step budget B - t; SWE containers are deterministic given actions, so there is no luck term after an action and drops are decisions; the standard error of V-hat (~0.09 at K = 32) is reported as the split-half ceiling. The critic's output is random given the API's own sampling; temperature 0 through an API is not deterministic, so the base arm runs 3 times and its spread is reported. The graded quantity is a property of the (critic prompt, agent policy, budget) triple, not of the task; the shrinking-budget confound of 2610.17633 (31% of continuations exhaust the budget) is inherited and stated. All estimators are graded on failed runs only, where V falls from p(x) to 0, which is why the linear-decay control is mandatory.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: the audit grades a recipe labs ship and runs on released data; solo suffices for the SWE instantiation (~$550, 10 GPU-hours). A lab adds its own AppWorld replay (LVRL's 3,899-state probe data are not released), the production critic prompt and a second critic vendor. Race: CWGT's authors extending their audit to anchored critics; LVRL's authors, who left the anchors-vs-siblings separation to future work; the credit-assignment lane publishes ~3 papers/week (18 in-window hits on the credit+validation query), so the window is tight but the data advantage (curves already released) is ours only until someone else reads the release. Merged from two cards: 2610.17633 supplies the ground truth and the dollar-matched MC arm; 2610.15840 supplies the critic under audit, the placebo and the shuffle.

scorecard.target_value: Asked in print: LVRL (2610.15840) states its step credit is unreliable early (44% vs 88%), leaves separating anchors from in-context siblings to future work, and calls the frontier bill prohibitive under budget limits (card complaints 2 and 3); 2610.17633 sec. 7 says value estimators controllers need 'can be built and ranked' against its curves; CWGT's abstract: existing evaluations grade step correctness, it audits contribution, and they come apart. Who pays: training teams spending order $10k per AppWorld run on a frontier critic plus summarizer; restart or controller builders (2608.03222, 2609.38147) who need a forward prefix value.

impact_ceiling.floor: A footnote: the anchored frontier critic's localization on SWE failures sits inside its own shuffle in all thirds, or beats it only late, with a measured ranking of three estimators against a noise ceiling; requires the release to contain trajectory text and per-continuation outcomes; p = 0.5 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: A measurement paper: value-captured share and Spearman by trajectory third for the critic, k = 0, placebo, shuffle, MC and log-ratio arms, with the mechanism (outcome-reading vs step-reading) separated and the recipe consequence that anchors plus uniform split equal the critic for the first two thirds at $0; requires step 0 to show resolution and the 60 second-agent curves to replicate; p = 0.35 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The critic survives placebo, beats shuffle early and matches MC: first replay-graded evidence that frontier models carry forward value on long-horizon agent runs, which makes a distilled local critic a sound target and changes what restart controllers use; or the reverse, 'Spearman with executable V' becomes the reported validation for step-credit claims adopted by one training group; requires curves from a second scaffold (~100 GPU-hours); p = 0.15 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan route (Odysseus, EasyPPO) and any RL group: a ground-truth grade of the lane's most expensive credit signal, usable as a baseline table; the uniform/shuffle/placebo/MC arms become required controls. Industry: anyone paying frontier API for critics. Jacob's edge: the instrument's statistics (binomial noise at 331 continuations, bootstrap over curves, placebo design, attenuation by noisy ground truth) is a physics-trained fit; computer engineering: zero (no systems component); L5: zero.
scorecard.kill_probe: Step 0: oracle-vs-random VC_2 gap on the released curves, $0, 1 day, dead if intervals overlap. Step 1: critic plus controls and the dollar-matched MC arm, about $550 API and 10 GPU-hours, 5 days; claim dead if the critic beats its shuffle in the first third, holds under placebo and matches MC within 0.05 Spearman.

neighbors.title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay
neighbors.trick: Re-execute the policy's own alternative action at each step and roll forward; the outcome shift is the step's contribution, and every credit signal is graded against it beside its own shuffled copy.
neighbors.difference: Audits an outcome-aware per-step correctness judge, a hindsight log-ratio and policy confidence on ALFWorld (Qwen2.5-7B); no anchored sibling-conditioned frontier value critic, no wrong-outcome placebo, no dollar-matched MC arm, no SWE.

neighbors.title: Executable Prefix Values for Locating Agent Failures
neighbors.trick: Restart the agent from reconstructed states of its own failed run and count how often it still succeeds; where that number falls is where the run was lost.
neighbors.difference: Supplies the ground truth; grades judges, a human and fixed rules by value captured (Table 32 already holds the random-step, step-1, first-edit rows: cite, do not re-run); grades no value estimator.

neighbors.title: LLM Value Functions for Credit Assignment in Agentic RL (LVRL)
neighbors.trick: Ask a frozen frontier model for the value of every step, pin the first to the group pass rate and the last to the observed outcome, and train on the differences.
neighbors.difference: The critic under audit; its own MC check is 114 hand-thresholded AppWorld events with sign agreement, no shuffle, no placebo, no correlation; anchors and siblings ablated jointly; no code or labels released.

neighbors.title: Last Step Matters: Early Uncertainty Cannot Predict Failure in Long-Horizon Agents
neighbors.trick: Score verbal confidence and perplexity at each stage of a run against the final outcome; they separate failures at the end (AUROC 0.85) and not at mid-run (under 0.60 at 50% progress).
neighbors.difference: Forward uncertainty on deep-research tasks, no executed value and no critic; makes the candidate's self-estimate arm a replication row.

neighbors.title: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents
neighbors.trick: Train per-step verbalized confidence against the episode's realized outcome using the GRPO group as labels; AUROC rises from chance to 0.68-0.85.
neighbors.difference: Trained self-estimate graded on group outcomes (ALFWorld/TextWorld/WebShop), not on executed V-curves; its depth/difficulty/foresight protocol is the one to copy.

neighbors.title: Counterfactual Rollout Replay: Forkable Environments as Free Process Rewards for Software Engineering Agents
neighbors.trick: Restore the state at a few decision points, sample one alternative action, roll it forward, and use the return difference as the step's advantage.
neighbors.difference: A training recipe on SWE-bench Verified with an equal-wall-clock comparison; occupies the consequence 'spend the budget on continuations at a few anchors'; grades no critic.

neighbors.title: RTMC: Step-Level Credit Assignment via Rollout Trees
neighbors.trick: Group rollouts that pass through the same state and use their returns as per-step values, no critic.
neighbors.difference: A free realized-sibling arm on the same benchmark; no comparison to a critic or executed V.

neighbors.title: ProAct: Agentic Lookahead in Interactive Environments (MC-Critic)
neighbors.trick: Calibrate a value estimate with lightweight environment rollouts inside PPO/GRPO on 2048 and Sokoban.
neighbors.difference: MC-calibrated critic in the training loop; no audit of a frontier critic.

neighbors.title: Retrospective In-Context Learning for Temporal Credit Assignment with Large Language Models
neighbors.trick: Have a pretrained LLM read a finished episode and write each step's advantage; train on it (BabyAI).
neighbors.difference: In-context hindsight credit precedent; the abstract names no replay ground truth.

neighbors.title: Causal Agent Replay: Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures
neighbors.trick: Intervene on one step of a run, re-execute forward under the same stochastic policy, and report the outcome shift with intervals.
neighbors.difference: Attribution tooling validated on synthetic SCMs; grades no critic.

neighbors.title: The Variance of Thought: Policy Variance, Critical Forks, and Local Credit Assignment
neighbors.trick: In a deterministic MDP policy variance Var_a Q(s,a) is the only return variance; an MC advantage estimate at a fork with success P has signal-to-noise of order sqrt(P).
neighbors.difference: Theory that prices step 0's resolution; no measurement.

neighbors.title: Fail-Fast, Restart-Smart
neighbors.trick: A 0.6B monitor trained on Qwen3.6-27B prefixes predicts failure early and triggers a fresh restart at a target false-positive rate.
neighbors.difference: A forward estimator on the same policy family; an arm to grade if released, not a competitor.

pre_window_precedents.title: VinePPO
pre_window_precedents.trick: Value networks barely beat a random baseline when comparing alternative steps; replace them with Monte-Carlo continuations (MATH/GSM8K).

pre_window_precedents.title: Math-Shepherd
pre_window_precedents.trick: Label each step by the success rate of continuations sampled from it and train a process reward model on those labels.

pre_window_precedents.title: GiGPO
pre_window_precedents.trick: Group actions that leave the same environment state and compute step advantages from their returns, with no critic.

limitation_quotes.section: 9 Limitations, and what would change our mind
limitation_quotes.quote: Every scope condition below is measured, not assumed: the audit runs in a single environment with a binary outcome, and every claim is scoped accordingly. The training-loop experiments are single-family and single-scale (Qwen2.5-7B, LoRA (low-rank adaptation), offline) ... Our audit is confined to a single environment.

Hindsight conditioning is a single outcome-injection line appended to the prompt — our addition, not HCAPO's [App. L]; judge prompt input: '3. Final Outcome: Whether the episode ended in task success or failure.'

Two policies of one family, one scaffold, one benchmark subset; V is relative to the agent and its budget (§6.9). The restart evaluation is offline and assumes a value-based policy never restarts a run that would have succeeded. Replay failures, the 31% of continuations that exhaust the shrinking budget and resampled killed runs are all counted and bounded by the controls (§6.10). The judges come from one vendor; one human annotator leaves inter-annotator agreement unmeasured.
the curve is the reference against which localizers and the value estimators controllers need can be built and ranked.

Although separating the effect of the endpoint anchors from that of the context rollouts, and varying the number of context rollouts, is left to future work, we hypothesize that performance improves with context size.

Querying a large LLM to predict step values for every trajectory during training can be prohibitive when training throughput or compute budget is constrained. Future work can investigate reducing this cost, for example, by querying the estimator only when its value signal is highly uncertain or by distilling its step-level knowledge into a smaller, learned critic.

objections.objection: The forward critic-vs-executed-continuations audit by trajectory depth is in print: Probe-and-Resume 2610.21088 (2026-10-15) grades a frontier critic at 25/50/75% depth against executed continuations on 1,111 intermediate states of 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks — pairwise accuracy 49-56% at 25% depth (chance 50%), 56-62% at 50%, 64-69% at 75%, no significant selection gain over random at 25%, decided-pairs split, best-constant row, bootstrap intervals over tasks; the record's pre-registered 'expected' result is a published finding (Gate 2B service); the kill search's 11 queries missed a 5-day-old paper because its vocabulary ('credit assignment', 'process reward', 'placebo', 'Monte Carlo') does not contain 'test-time search', 'critic', 'intermediate states', 'continuation pass rate'.
objections.evidence: 2610.21088 S3.2, S4, S5, App. F, Table 8 [full]: 'At intermediate states, the critics rank states better than chance late in the trajectory (64%-69% at 75% depth), but not early (49%-56% at 25%; Figure 2a). At 25% depth, we do not detect a statistically significant selection gain over random choice'
objections.answer: round 1: 2610.21088 grades a forward critic, the probe the hindsight anchored class; round 2: conceded that the hindsight class has no consequence and the claim's substance is what 2610.21088 reports

objections.objection: The shuffle is a degenerate null: with c_0 = mu_G and c_T = 0 fixed by anchoring and interior values permuted by a uniform sigma, interior transitions are exchangeable, so E[VC_k(argmax drop of c o sigma)] = E_{t~Unif}[VC_k(t)] — Table 32's random-step row (VC1 0.04, VC3 0.10); for Spearman against the isotonic fit any non-increasing curve has rho = 1 and the shuffle E[rho] = 0, so linear decay, the anchors alone and the critic all 'beat shuffle'. The only null separating step-reading from anchor-reading is V_lin(t) = mu_G (1 - t/T) or an outcome-blind, anchor-free critic; the headline and kills_if never test against it. Median t*/T = 0.28; 40/47 decisive steps in the first two thirds.
objections.evidence: 2610.15840 S3.2 (anchoring) [full]; 2610.17633 S4, S6.8 eq. (9), Table 9 [full]; argument; theory_tstar.py
objections.answer: conceded: the headline must read 'do not beat the linear decay between their own anchors' and kills_if must be on VC_2(critic) - VC_2(V_lin); the claim may not be changed mid-red-team

objections.objection: Per-curve Spearman on levels is shape-dominated: every audited curve is non-increasing, so under the paper's own schedule (K=8 screening every 5 steps, K=16 labels, K=32 confirmation, 24.1 points per curve) split-half Spearman is 0.90 (cliff) / 0.61 (erosion) while linear decay scores 0.78 / 0.86 and a disjoint K=4 MC arm 0.85 / 0.55 — on erosions (30/47) linear decay beats the ground truth's own split half; 'within 0.05 of MC' has no discriminating power.
objections.evidence: 2610.17633 S4 Schedule, Table 7, App. K Table 13 ('A curve has 24.1 points on average ... and costs 331 continuations'), App. W ('17 cliffs and 30 erosions'), S6.6 [full]; sys_splithalf.py
objections.answer: conceded: drop Spearman on levels; grade increments or VC_k; ceiling on increments by shape

objections.objection: 'By trajectory third' has no resolution early and is undefined late: split-half Spearman in the first third 0.24 (cliff) / 0.11 (erosion), middle 0.77 / 0.00, final undefined in 88% / 91% of curves (after the point of no return every point is 0/K by design); the claim's 'first two thirds' holds for the oracle too; VC_2 'by third' is undefined in the record.
objections.evidence: 2610.17633 S4 ('Point of no return: ... points are raised to K = 24 until the one-sided 95% Wilson upper bound on V is below 0.15') [full]; sys_thirds.py
objections.answer: conceded: restrict by-third statistics to curves the truth resolves there; report the excluded count

objections.objection: The 'dollar-matched K=4 MC arm' has no stated unit, is contaminated (subsampling the truth's K=8 screening continuations inflates Spearman +0.08 to +0.25), and matched dollars buy 11-290 continuations: one critic call at 50-150k tokens at LVRL's quoted $5/$25 per M is $0.30-0.80; the release's 123 GPU-h covered ~17,800 runs (0.0069 GPU-h per run, $0.014-0.028 at $2-4/GPU-h); Table 29 already prices 'screening at K = 4' (203 continuations, 0.30 of the drop) — a row to cite.
objections.evidence: 2610.17633 S6.6 / Table 29 [full]; release README S3 ('about 220 GPU-hours') [source]; 2610.15840 App. B.1 Table 6 [full]; sys_dollars.py
objections.answer: conceded: K_match fresh continuations at the schedule's anchors with price and unit pre-registered; cite Table 29

objections.objection: The wrong-outcome placebo is one-directional on an all-failed set: 'wrong outcome' is always 'told success'; with the terminal anchor at 1 after prediction the critic must emit a non-decreasing curve, so 'the placebo leaves the predicted largest drop unchanged in most trajectories' is false by construction and the three-way kill conjunction can never be satisfied; the arm bundles wrong outcome with another task's siblings and mu_G; no successful-run curves exist to make the lie symmetric.
objections.evidence: 2610.15840 App. C Figs. 7-8 ('Initial and terminal values are anchored after prediction') [full]; 2610.17633 S5, Tables 1, 13 [full]
objections.answer: conceded: replace by a sibling-channel arm (true outcome, other task's siblings), an outcome-blind anchor-free critic, and decoy curves if a lie is kept

objections.objection: The critic is a hindsight smoother, c_t = f(h_T, R, mu_G, siblings), not a value function (LVRL: 'a hindsight estimate rather than a true state-value function'); a hindsight reader locates t* by reading backward from the symptom; VC_k(critic) high is consistent with zero forward information, so the ceiling scenario ('a frontier model carries forward-looking value ... usable by restart controllers') does not follow; no arm runs the model on prefixes only.
objections.evidence: 2610.15840 S3.2, S4.4 [full]; 2610.17633 Def. 1, S6.4 [full]; 2608.19760 S5 ('knowing how the trajectory ended changes the score, but not toward what each step contributed') [full]
objections.answer: conceded: the forward consequence needs a prefix-only frontier arm

objections.objection: Budget is part of the state in the ground truth (V(h_t) = Pr(Y=1 | h_t, pi, budget B-t)) and absent from the critic's prompt; D_t = V_B(h_t) - V_{B-t}(h_t) is the late drop on capped runs; 31% of main-policy continuations exhaust the budget (L2 stratum 62%); the 9B set (60/107) was withdrawn by the owners from their own restart analysis ('lost under the remaining budget' and 'lost' nearly coincide).
objections.answer: conceded: primary analysis on the L0+L1 strata of both policies (~46 curves); no final-third claims except on the ten full-budget trajectories

objections.objection: The kill criterion is a one-sided conjunction of three positives and underpowered: VC_2 in [0,1] with sd ~0.25 over ~55 first-third curves from ~30 task clusters gives SE ~0.04-0.05 on a mean difference; the critic must reach VC_2 >= 0.17-0.19 (~3x the random expectation) to clear 2 SE; LVRL's own 44% early (29% zeros) sits below; any noise failure leaves the claim 'supported'.
objections.evidence: 2610.17633 Table 32, Table 9, S4 (task-level cluster bootstrap) [full]; 2610.15840 Table 10 [full]; theory_tstar.py
objections.answer: conceded: equivalence-bound design with task-cluster bootstrap; no final-third row

objections.objection: Positivity: VC_k divides by V-hat(h_0); 8/47 curves have V-hat(h_0) <= 0.18 and 6 <= 0.125 ('doomed from the start and has nothing to localize'), with SE on the VC share 0.6-2.3; the fit is read only at raised points, so a critic step in an unbisected gap is scored on K=8 points while the oracle's t* is scored on K=32 bisected points — the instrument's resolution is correlated with the oracle's answer.
objections.evidence: 2610.17633 S3 Def. 4, Table 7, App. H, Table 9 [full]; theory_tstar.py
objections.answer: conceded: exclude doomed curves; score every arm on the probed grid at achieved K

objections.objection: Regime: LVRL's critic ran on 9.0-20.4k-token AppWorld transcripts (responses truncated at 4,000 characters) and its MC check is AppWorld M=32; the audit feeds 100-step mini-swe-agent transcripts under a 131k context — a null there is 'LVRL's prompt out of its regime'; Table 10's first third is 44% same sign / 29% no change / 26% opposite, so the early deficit is conservatism (zeros), which a shuffle/VC_2 test does not measure.
objections.answer: conceded: apply LVRL's truncation, report by length tercile and the zero-prediction share

objections.objection: The k=0 arm is CWGT's judge class (an LLM told the final outcome, asked per-step credit) already at shuffle level in print: median Spearman 0.114 [0.027, 0.168] vs its marginal-matched shuffle [-0.049, 0.117]; the record counts it as a new finding.
objections.evidence: 2608.19760 Table 1, App. L [full] ('weak, possibly nonzero, yet indistinguishable from its own control')
objections.answer: conceded: k=0 is a replication row

objections.objection: One prompt, one vendor, one scaffold cannot license 'published step-credit critics': LVRL's SWE training used R2E-Gym with Qwen3-8B/32B, its MC validation is AppWorld only, and the signal is critic-dependent (Qwen3-235B 9.8% vs Opus 4.6 24.3%); CWGT scopes to one environment and justifies it by auditing methods on their own venue.
objections.answer: conceded: the headline names the triple; a second critic family moves into the solo arms

objections.objection: VC_k reduces the critic to a localizer and is blunt on erosions; the owners' restart point t_r = min{t : R-hat(x, B-t) - V(h_t) >= mu} and offline restart gain are the controller-relevant functional, shipped as analysis/restart.py, and cost $0 to apply to every arm — the incumbent ruler for estimators.
objections.evidence: 2610.17633 Def. 5, S6.5 ('Restarting at the restart point t_r (mu = 0.10) raises expected success from 0.44 to 0.57'), S7 [full]; README [source]
objections.answer: conceded: add the restart-gain row

objections.objection: The one convincing experiment — the forward frontier arm on the K=32 curves (prefix only, no outcome, at every probed anchor) beside linear decay and the restart gain — is a replication of 2610.21088 answering its own label-noise caveat (5 continuations per state, SE up to 22 points, 79% of states all-pass/all-fail); cost ~2,100 prefixes x ~50k tokens, $200-320 per repeat ($50-100 with prefix caching), three repeats $300-900, 0 GPU-h, 2 days — cheaper than the record's step 1 and the only object with a question mark left.
objections.evidence: 2610.21088 App. F, Table 8 [full]; 2610.15840 App. C [full]; 2610.17633 S4 Schedule [full]; argument
objections.answer: conceded: a different probe and a new candidate; recorded as the claim's re-open trigger

objections.objection: Known idea with new words, the fourth telling: VinePPO 2024 ('barely outperform a random baseline when comparing alternative steps'), 2608.29685 (no uncertainty signal above AUROC 0.60 at 50% progress), CWGT (judge and log-ratio at shuffle level), 2610.21088 (frontier critic at chance at 25% depth); the only arm outside that lineage is the placebo on a hindsight class with no consequence; 'every critic paper owes a shuffle and a placebo' is a reviewer request.

title: Budget loss versus state loss: the two controls executable restart skipped
statement: Using the released code and trajectories of 2610.17633, run the two controls the paper ran on 10 trajectories or not at all: (a) full-budget continuations (budget B = 100 from every anchor instead of B - t) on 40 failed trajectories stratified by whether the base run hit the step cap, giving the budget share of lost value beta_t = (V_B(h_t) - V_{B-t}(h_t)) / p(x) and the shift of the decisive step t* and restart point t_r; (b) remaining-budget screening curves on 30 successful runs from the same 2-6/8 band tasks, giving the rate at which the paper's restart rule (R(x, B - t) - V-hat(h_t) >= 0.10) fires on a run that was going to succeed. Report the restart gain net of false kills and by budget stratum.
claim: On SWE-bench Verified a large share of the value 'lost' at early steps of capped failures is budget, not state damage, and value-based restart kills a measurable fraction of winning runs, so failure-localization labels and restart gains are not well defined without stating the step budget and the false-kill rate.
trick: Give the agent a full budget from every prefix and run the restart rule on runs that were going to win, to see how much of the measured failure was the clock and how often the fix kills a success.
why_now: 2610.17633 released code, curves and labels on 2026-10-13 and names both gaps in its own limitations (budget confound, sec. 6.9-6.10, 10 trajectories; no curves for successful runs, sec. 6.5); Fail-Fast (2608.03222, 2026-08-04) already prices restart by a false-positive rate (5% / 25%) on the same policy, so the missing number has a consumer.

killing_experiment.design: Replay anchors (every 5 steps, K = 8) under full budget B = 100 for 20 capped and 20 uncapped failed trajectories across both agents (~3,200 continuations), and remaining-budget screening curves (K = 8, bisection on dips >= 0.25) for 30 successful band runs (~2,900 continuations); compute beta_t per anchor, t* and t_r under both budgets, the fraction of successful runs where the restart rule fires at any probed step, and net gain = gross offline gain - P(success) x false-kill rate x (1 - R(x, B - t)). Assumes ~100 continuations per H100-hour on a 27B FP8 vLLM instance; 26% replay loss budgeted. Pre-check: anchor states are reconstructible from the released trajectories with the released fingerprinting code.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Budget share beta is below 0.15 at every anchor on the capped stratum AND the restart rule fires on fewer than 5% of successful runs at K = 8: both controls are small, the paper's +0.13 gain and 'early innocuous read' headline stand, and the result is a one-line confirmation.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment: beta >= 0.4 at early anchors on capped failures and <= 0.1 on uncapped ones; t* moves later by a median >= 8 steps on capped runs and <= 2 on uncapped; the restart rule fires on 25-40% of successful band runs at K = 8 (standard error 0.17) and 10-20% at K = 32, cutting the net gain from +0.13 to +0.05-0.09.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Traverse (2609.17930), Who&When and the four frontier judges define 'first mistake' as a property of the transcript with no budget clause; 2610.17633 charges judge-label restarts a decoy false-positive rate but charges the value policy zero.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If beta is large on capped runs, failure-localization benchmarks must state the budget and report budget-attributable loss separately, and Fail-Fast-style monitors trained on capped runs are learning 'slow', not 'wrong'; if the false-kill rate is material, restart controllers (2608.03222, 2609.38147) must report net gain, and the EPV online result (0.39 vs 0.26) needs the winners' arm.

identifiability: V_B and V_{B-t} are both random given the continuation seeds of the agent (temperature 0.70, top-p 0.80) and are properties of (policy, scaffold, task, budget); their difference at a fixed prefix is identified because both arms restart from the same reconstructed state and differ only in the budget argument. The false-kill rate is a property of the restart rule's protocol (K, mu = 0.10, the anchor schedule) applied to the agent's own success-run distribution; it is reported at K = 8 and K = 32 because the rule fires more often at higher V-hat variance. Environment deterministic after action; successful runs are drawn from the same band tasks (p(x) in 2/8-6/8) so p(x) is matched to the failed-run sample.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a missing-control measurement on released public data, ~80 GPU-hours. The EPV authors are the natural owners and have the containers and 10 trajectories already; the re-open test is whether their v2 includes these controls (ask them). A lab would have the committed anchor images (no 26% replay loss) and the online restart harness; solo has the released code and must reconstruct states.

scorecard.target_value: 2610.17633 limitations: 'the full-budget control moved the decisive step later in all 10 trajectories checked' (sec. 6.9-6.10) and 'I have no curves for runs that would have succeeded, so I cannot measure how often a value-based restart kills a winning run' (sec. 6.5), both filed as complaint seeds this week; 2608.03222 prices restart at a target false-positive rate. Who pays: restart-controller builders, failure-localization benchmark owners (Traverse/Scout), anyone reading 'the decisive step is an early innocuous read' as a claim about agents rather than about clocks.

impact_ceiling.floor: Budget share and false-kill rate measured on 40 + 30 trajectories; a correction note the EPV and Fail-Fast papers cite. Requires anchor reconstruction to work on the released trajectories. p ~0.5 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: The net restart gain roughly halves and the early-step headline holds only on uncapped runs: a workshop paper that adds a budget clause and a winners' arm to how restart and localization results are reported. Requires both effects to appear on both agents. p ~0.3 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: 'Budget-stated failure localization' and 'net restart gain' become required reporting in Traverse-style benchmarks and controller papers; requires showing beta depends on scaffold (a second scaffold's runs, ~100 GPU-hours more). p ~0.1 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan (tau-family): moderate, attribution of failure to agent versus protocol (budget) is the lane's core; HAL (Narayanan): moderate, budget is a cost-accounting axis; evaluators (Traverse owners): direct. Industry: coding-agent products with restart or abort logic, where a false kill costs a solved task. Jacob's edge: physics side low-moderate (a two-term decomposition with a telescoping identity; competing-hazards framing), computer-engineering side low; zero for L5.
scorecard.kill_probe: ~6,100 continuations (full-budget anchors on 40 failed runs; screening curves on 30 successful runs); ~80 H100-hours, ~$250; dead if beta < 0.15 on capped runs and false-kill rate < 5%; 7 days.
scorecard.density_ownership: arXiv API, 12 months: step/turn budget + agent + failure/restart/attribution = 20 hits, none decomposing lost value into budget versus state; closest 2609.38411 (competing-hazards systematization of loss of control: check whether timeout is a competing risk there), 2607.14547 AdaTurn (budget-aware test-time scaling), 2608.03222 Fail-Fast (false-positive-rate pricing of restart). Pre-window precedents: 2512.06749 DoVer (intervene-and-rerun attribution), 2608.03222. Occupied by the card: V-curves on failed runs, judge grading, restart at t_r and t_pnr, the 10-trajectory budget control. W42 seeds adjacent: 2610.21088 Probe-and-Resume, 2610.18780 BLADE. Kill search owed.
scorecard.why_now: Code, curves and labels released 2026-10-13; the paper's own limitations name both controls; Fail-Fast on the same policy gives the false-positive-rate framing a consumer since 2026-08.
scorecard.register: Measurement (missing comparison and control arm); not a restart controller, not a new localizer, not the card's method on a new benchmark (same benchmark, two quantities the card's method did not report).

neighbors_to_check_first: 2608.03222 — Fail-Fast: restart priced by false-positive rate on Qwen3.6-27B; whether it reports the fraction of killed runs that would have succeeded

2609.38411 — competing-hazards systematization: whether budget exhaustion is treated as a competing risk to agent error

2607.14547 — AdaTurn budget-aware test-time scaling: any budget-vs-state decomposition
2512.06749 — DoVer: intervene-and-rerun attribution, the pre-window precedent for executable controls

title: Dollar-matched cold-start BabyAI: LVRL's critic bill as GRPO rollouts
statement: Reproduce LVRL's BabyAI configuration (Qwen3-4B student, G = 8, 64 environments, 150 updates, 128-step horizon, its ID/OOD level split) with plain GRPO and confirm the paper's near-zero floor, then spend LVRL's BabyAI critic-plus-summarizer bill (8,838 critic queries at $0.06-0.14 each plus an equal summarization bill, about $1-2.5k, which is 400-1,000 H100-hours at cloud prices) on rollouts of the student instead: GRPO with G = 32 (lower-bound dollar match), plus the two free step-credit incumbents the paper omitted, GiGPO anchor-state grouping (operator 1: the realized sibling value where observation-matched siblings exist, free on BabyAI's repeating grid states) and VSR prefix replay (2610.15888, which already reports BabyAI numbers). Measure ID/OOD success at 150 updates against LVRL's published 69.0 / 52.2 and log anchor-state coverage per trajectory third so the mechanism is visible.
claim: LVRL's BabyAI cold-start result is reachable without a critic by spending the same dollars on rollouts, so the paper's 'GRPO and PPO stay near 0' row measures an unmatched budget, not a credit effect.
trick: Take the money the paper paid a frontier model to guess step values, spend it on more rollouts of the student, and see whether the student learns the same.
why_now: VSR (2610.15888, Oct 2026) reports beating GRPO and GiGPO on BabyAI, so critic-free BabyAI numbers exist in a configuration different from LVRL's (Oct 2026) and nobody has placed them on one config; CWGT (Aug 2026) showed in a seven-arm pre-registered experiment that credit-rule comparisons which do not match dose measure dose, and LVRL's table matches neither dollars nor rollouts.

killing_experiment.design: Stage 1 (the probe): GRPO G = 8 floor reproduction (about 80 GPU-hours: 150 updates x 64 envs x 8 trajectories x up to 128 short-action steps with prefix caching, estimate) plus GRPO G = 32 (about 320 GPU-hours) on LVRL's exact BabyAI level set, one seed each, same eval protocol; about 400 GPU-hours, about $1k at cloud prices, 7 days on 8 GPUs. Stage 2 (lab or follow-up): GiGPO and VSR (about 80 GPU-hours each), then 3 seeds on the winning arm.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Void (protocol failure, not a result) if GRPO G = 8 reaches more than 15% ID success: the configuration does not reproduce the paper's floor and must be re-aligned before any claim. Kills the claim if GRPO G = 32 stays at or below 20% ID at 150 updates while G = 8 reproduces about 0: four times the rollouts do not lift cold-start BabyAI, so the critic's hindsight split inside all-fail groups is doing something rollout budget does not buy, and LVRL's cold-start claim stands at matched dollars. Stage 2 kills the free version if GiGPO and VSR both stay at or below 10% ID.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment: GRPO G = 32 lifts off the floor and reaches 30-50% ID at 150 updates against LVRL's 69.0 (p = 0.5), because with a base pass rate near 1% the chance that a group of 32 contains a success is about 0.27 against 0.08 for G = 8, which is enough to bootstrap on BabyAI's easy levels; GiGPO alone stays near 0 (p = 0.65), since anchor-state groups with all-zero returns carry no signal; VSR lands between.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: LVRL: all-fail groups give GRPO no signal regardless of budget, so cold start needs a critic (the BabyAI claim in the card); the credit-assignment lane's tables compare recipes at equal group size and never at equal dollars.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If G = 32 stays near 0, the frontier critic's interior values in all-fail groups are a shaped reward from a frontier model's prior that no rollout budget replaces, and the lane's default for sparse cold-start agentic RL changes to 'pay for dense shaping or use a curriculum'. If G = 32 reaches 50% or more, every LLM-critic paper owes a dollar-matched large-group arm, and the $10k-per-run recipe loses its cold-start argument.

identifiability: Success rate is random given the student's sampling temperature at training and at evaluation (LVRL's evaluation protocol, greedy or sampled, must be matched and stated); BabyAI is deterministic given seed and actions, so differences between siblings are decisions, never luck, and anchor-state matching is exact. One seed per arm in the probe with a 10-point kill threshold; LVRL's own 3-seed spread (its table's standard deviations) sets whether that threshold is far from seed noise, and is read before running.
positioning_note: Lab-contested shape by default (a recipe comparison), rescued by the definitive-comparison clause: the arms are the production default (G = 8), the strongest cheap incumbents (free branching, prefix replay) and the dollar-matched large group, which is the comparison nobody ran. The probe costs about 400 GPU-hours, over one GPU-week on a single GPU and inside the dollar equivalent of LVRL's own BabyAI critic bill; parked from the solo position (Gate 1) with re-open trigger 'access to 8 GPUs for a week, or the config shrinks to under 168 GPU-hours'. A lab also has the AppWorld version (500 updates, order $10k matched) which is out of solo reach.

verdict_by_position.solo: parked: Gate 1 (probe over one GPU-week from the solo position)

title: Hindsight-optimal switching bounds forecast-guided prefill-decode role switching
statement: Build a trace-driven discrete-event replay of agentic rollout (Frontier, 2605.21312, released at github.com/NetX-lab/Frontier, already models PD disaggregation and RL rollouts; fallback: a 300-line simulator with prefill tokens/s and decode step time calibrated on one 8-GPU node) fed by public trajectories with per-turn prompt tokens, output tokens and tool durations (SWE-agent .traj files in the swe-bench/experiments repo: each TrajectoryStep carries execution_time, query, thought, action; single-turn math lengths from public DAPO/OpenR1 rollouts) at 256-4096 concurrent trajectories, synchronous and asynchronous (staleness 2 and 8). Four arms on the same trace: (i) static PD split at the per-workload optimal ratio, (ii) Prorsa's Eq. 1 forecaster (10-s horizon, 5-s switch, in-flight cancellation), (iii) an observation-only two-threshold hysteresis rule on prefill backlog and decode KV occupancy (operations research: the Hofri-Ross two-queue server with setup time, where a threshold policy is optimal; FluidPD's 'pressure index' is the serving instance), (iv) the hindsight oracle: a dynamic program over (prefill-instance count, 10-s slot) with the switch cost, given the full arrival and length record. Measured: oracle headroom H = T_static / T_oracle - 1 and capture ratio rho_arm = (T_static - T_arm) / (T_static - T_oracle), per workload x concurrency x staleness.
claim: Oracle headroom over the per-task static split shrinks with concurrency and asynchrony (the superposition of many independent trajectory renewal processes smooths the prefill-to-decode demand ratio), so at >= 1024 concurrent trajectories in asynchronous rollout H is below 10%, and an observation-only hysteresis rule captures as much of H as the 10-s forecaster.
trick: Replay the rollout trace, compute the best switching schedule anyone could have run with perfect foresight, and ask how much of that gap a forecaster closes versus a plain backlog threshold, as the number of concurrent trajectories grows.
why_now: Prorsa (2026-10-12) is the first to report forecast error (WAPE 5.4-14.4%) for role switching without the throughput it costs; Frontier (2026-05-20) released a validated disaggregated-serving simulator with RL-rollout support (throughput error below 4% on 16 H800); FluidPD (2026-10-02) shipped the observation-only role-reassignment rule in serving, so the forecast-vs-observation-vs-oracle comparison has all three arms in print but never on one trace.

killing_experiment.design: Run the four arms on three traces (SWE-agent coding, replayed tool durations; a general-agent proxy from HAL or Toolathlon-style logs with longer tool gaps; single-turn math), each at concurrency 256, 1024, 4096, sync and async. Calibrate prefill tokens/s and decode step time per batch size once on Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8 in SGLang on one 8-GPU node (16 GPU-hours), or take Frontier's calibrated models (0 GPU-hours). Five bootstrap resamples of trajectories into batches per cell.
killing_experiment.kills_if: In at least two of three workloads at concurrency >= 1024 asynchronous, H >= 15% and the forecaster captures >= 0.8 H while the hysteresis rule captures <= 0.5 H: then forecasting is both needed and sufficient and the claim is dead (the kill result is still the first public oracle bound on role switching, citable as a footnote). Separately pre-registered non-kill: H < 5% in every cell including synchronous means switching is a dead lever and the digest says so.

preregistered_surprise.expected: H falls roughly as 1/sqrt(concurrency) in async mode (judgment: 20-40% at 256, under 10% at 1024+); in synchronous mode H stays 15-40% because the step-start prefill burst and decode-only tail are structural; hysteresis matches the forecaster within 10 points of capture ratio everywhere; the forecaster's capture ratio drops on the general-agent trace where WAPE is highest.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Dynamic PD switching driven by a demand forecast is a standing lever for agentic rollout (Prorsa: up to 1.44x over static; PEARL: PD mode and ratio must track the workload at runtime; FluidPD: 94.6 pp SLO gain in serving), and better forecasts are the path to more of it.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If H is small at scale, training-infra teams stop building forecasters for role switching and put the effort into fixing colocation interference (AInfer-PD 2609.00993) or into the synchronous-step case only; if hysteresis equals the forecaster, the forecaster is deleted from the recipe (the ConServe 'observation, not prediction' result moves from serving into RL rollout). If instead the forecaster captures most of a large H, the field gets its first oracle-normalized number for how good 10-s forecasting is, and the question becomes which of the ignored terms (output length, KV growth) closes the rest.

identifiability: Random given the trajectory record: none; the replay, the Eq. 1 forecaster (EMA alpha 0.1) and the DP oracle are deterministic functions of the trace, so all variation is from which trajectories enter which batch (bootstrap resampling over trajectories, 5 draws per cell). No LLM is sampled in the probe, so no temperature enters; the token-length and tool-duration distributions are those of the logged policy (SWE-agent with the logged model), not of an RL policy mid-training, and this is named as the first limitation. H is a property of the workload x injection protocol (sync/async, concurrency, staleness), not of the system constants beyond the switch cost and the prefill/decode speeds, which are reported as the two calibration numbers.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent. Solo: everything is trace replay plus one calibration run; the SWE-agent .traj logs and Frontier are public. A lab (Prorsa's or PEARL's authors, or any verl/ROLL/AReaL team) has the real 128-GPU stack and real rollout traces with timestamps, which no one has released; their incentive is to show the switcher, not to bound it, and the two closest papers report no oracle. The lab version is the same four arms on real traces plus a live confirmation of one cell; the solo version is the simulator study and is already a complete measurement paper.

scorecard.target_value: Prorsa itself: Section 5.5 and Appendix C report WAPE but never the throughput that forecast error costs, and no oracle is reported (card, weakest_component); FluidPD's abstract motivates observation-only role reassignment against forecasting-free autoscaling but never against an oracle. Who pays: every team running asynchronous agentic RL on verl, ROLL, AReaL or slime that must decide whether PD disaggregation with role switching is worth 6.4K lines of scheduler code.

impact_ceiling.floor: A released replay harness and the first oracle-normalized capture ratio for forecast-guided switching on one public coding trace. Requires only the simulator and the .traj parser. p = 0.7 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: The scaling result: switching headroom versus concurrency and staleness across three workloads, with the hysteresis-equals-forecaster finding; cited by rollout-engine papers as the reason to switch (or not) at a given scale. Requires the three traces and Frontier-level calibration. p = 0.35 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The rule is adopted as a pre-deployment check in a framework's docs (verl or SGLang router) and the hysteresis rule ships as the default role-switching policy; Prorsa/PEARL follow-ups report capture ratio against the oracle. Requires one framework maintainer to care and a real-trace confirmation. p = 0.1 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: L3 routes (Lloyd / Netravali / Tri Dao, systems): direct, a measurement of a rollout-engine design decision. Industry: RL infra teams choosing topology; serving teams get the RL analogue of ConServe/FluidPD. Jacob's edge: stochastic processes (superposition of renewal processes, Palm-Khintchine) supply the mechanism; computer engineering supplies the scheduling model. Zero relevance to L1, L2 (no training signal is touched), L4, L5.
scorecard.kill_probe: Replay four arms on three traces at three concurrencies, sync and async; 16 GPU-hours calibration (or 0 with Frontier), ~$60, 7 days; dead if H >= 15% and forecaster captures >= 0.8 H while hysteresis <= 0.5 H in two of three workloads at >= 1024 async.
scorecard.density_ownership: arXiv API 2026-10-19: prefill+decode+(oracle|hindsight|offline optimal)+(trace|replay|simulat) = 1 hit (NetKV 2606.03910, unrelated: decode-instance selection); prefill+(disaggregation|disaggregated)+(RL|rollout|post-training) = 7 hits, closest Prorsa and PEARL 2609.35158 (runtime PD mode/ratio selection with cost-aware switching, no oracle); (polling|switching cost|setup time|hysteresis|threshold policy)+(prefill|LLM serving) = 3 hits, none relevant. No one owns the oracle bound or the capture ratio. Pre-window precedents to name in the kill search: Hofri & Ross 1987 (two queues, setup times, threshold optimality); DistServe 2024 and Splitwise 2024 (static PD provisioning). This week's seeds: 2610.21500 (remote KV tiers for context-parallel prefill, kept) and ReFlow 2610.21640 (replay-driven decoupling) are adjacent, not overlapping. Kill search owed: 12-month window with words oracle, hindsight, regret, offline optimal, autoscaling, reconfiguration, role switch, elastic, hysteresis, threshold; quote PEARL's and FluidPD's limitation sections. Public-trace check done 2026-10-19: SWE-smith HF trajectories carry messages/instance_id/resolved/model/traj_id/patch only; SWE-agent .traj TrajectoryStep carries execution_time per step (sweagent/types.py), so per-step tool durations come from the swe-bench/experiments trajs, not from the HF dataset.

scorecard.register: Measurement with a definitive comparison (four arms, one trace, oracle-normalized). It is not a new scheduler, not a new forecaster, and not Prorsa on a new benchmark; the hysteresis arm is a control, not the contribution.

title: A prefill-decode overlap statistic predicts when disaggregation pays
statement: Define, from a rollout log alone, the overlap statistic Omega = integral over time of 1[prefill active on any engine at t] times D(t), divided by the integral of D(t), where D(t) is the number of sequences decoding at t (so Omega is the share of decode work that coincides with prefill); the colocation interference Prorsa measures (3.76-59.98% idle at the synchronized expert phase) scales with Omega, while disaggregation's cost (KV transfer plus switching) does not. Compute Omega for four workloads whose turn count and injection protocol are crossed: synchronous single-turn math, asynchronous single-turn math with continuous injection, phase-locked multi-turn (constant tool time, so turns stay aligned across the batch) and natural multi-turn (SWE-agent .traj execution_time replayed by a sleeping fake tool); then run each colocated (DP-attention 8, EP 8) and PD-disaggregated (4P+4D) on one 8-GPU node with Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8 in SGLang and measure rollout throughput. Measured: sign and size of disaggregated/colocated throughput against Omega, with Prorsa's own reversal (math 0.86-1.28, coding 2.54-4.05) as the first out-of-sample test.
claim: The sign of the disaggregation speedup is set by the temporal overlap of prefill with decode (Omega), not by turn count: asynchronously injected single-turn math gains from disaggregation and phase-locked multi-turn loses, and Omega computed from logs before deployment predicts both.
trick: Measure what fraction of decoding happens while someone else is prefilling; colocation only hurts in that fraction, so that number, read off the logs, tells you whether splitting prefill from decode will pay before you buy the second set of GPUs.
why_now: Prorsa (2026-10-12) is the first paper to publish a sign reversal of PD disaggregation across workloads on one stack (math slower, coding 2.5-4x faster) with the idle-ratio mechanism named; SGLang PD disaggregation with Mooncake transfer runs on one node since 2025 and verl supports SGLang rollout, so the four-workload test needs no cluster.

killing_experiment.design: Four workloads x two topologies x 3 repeats on one 8-GPU node (Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8, SGLang; fake tools sleep for logged execution_time); ~1 hour per cell including warm-up gives 24 node-hours = 192 GPU-hours worst case, trimmed to ~80 GPU-hours by shortening the two single-turn cells. Omega computed offline from each run's request log and, separately, predicted from the trace before the run.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Either off-diagonal cell breaks the ruler: asynchronous single-turn math does not gain from disaggregation (ratio <= 1.0) or phase-locked multi-turn does gain (ratio >= 1.1), or Omega is not monotone with the speedup across the four cells. Then turn count, not overlap, is the right rule of thumb and the ruler is dead; the kill result (an 8-GPU reproduction of Prorsa's reversal with the cause isolated) is still a citable footnote.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Omega near 0 for sync single-turn and phase-locked multi-turn (both lose, ratio 0.85-1.0), Omega above 0.6 for async single-turn and natural multi-turn (both gain, ratio 1.2-2x on one node, smaller than Prorsa's 2.5-4x because NVLink makes KV transfer nearly free); speedup monotone in Omega across the four cells (judgment).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Disaggregation pays for agentic (multi-turn) rollout and not for single-turn (Prorsa Section 5.2 attributes the reversal to continuous prefill demand in agentic tasks; PEARL says the colocate-vs-disaggregate choice 'varies with the workload' and resolves it by runtime profiling, not by a log statistic).
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the ruler holds, the colocate-versus-disaggregate decision moves from a runtime profiler or a cluster A/B to a one-line statistic on existing logs, and asynchronous single-turn RL (the common math/code RLVR case) becomes a disaggregation customer the field has written off. If it fails, PEARL-style runtime profiling is the right answer and pre-deployment statistics are not.

identifiability: Omega is a property of the workload trace crossed with the injection protocol (sync/async, concurrency), not of the policy's temperature: tool durations are replayed from logs by a sleeping fake tool and prompt/output lengths are fixed by the trace, so no LLM sampling enters the probe and repeated runs differ only by engine nondeterminism (3 repeats, report spread). Omega is computable before deployment from any log with per-turn token counts and tool durations; its value changes with concurrency and the system's prefill speed (through how long prefill is 'active'), so it is reported with both as conditioning.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent. Solo: one 8-GPU node for a day (~$250) and public logs; the small-MoE single-node setting under-represents the RDMA transfer cost Prorsa pays, which is named as the first limitation and which makes the solo result conservative on the 'disaggregation loses' side. A lab (Prorsa's authors, PEARL's, any verl team) has 128 GPUs and real traces and would run the four cells at scale in a day; their papers so far optimize the switcher rather than publish the decision rule, and PEARL resolves the same question with runtime profiling, so the lab version is a race we can enter with the ruler shape only.

scorecard.target_value: Prorsa Section 5.2 (math slower than colocation in most settings, no rule given; card complaint #1); PEARL abstract: 'the choice between colocation and disaggregation and the optimal PD ratio vary with the workload'; 2605.28302 poses 'when does each level actually pay off' for attention-FFN disaggregation. Who pays: every team provisioning rollout engines for RLVR or agentic RL, and SGLang/verl maintainers writing deployment guidance.

impact_ceiling.floor: An 8-GPU reproduction of Prorsa's sign reversal with the overlap mechanism isolated from turn count on four workloads, plus the Omega script over SWE-agent logs. Requires the node and the fake-tool replayer. p = 0.6 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: Omega adopted as the pre-deployment check in one framework's docs and used to show that asynchronous single-turn RLVR gains from disaggregation. Requires the async single-turn cell to come out positive and a maintainer to pick it up. p = 0.25 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: Omega becomes the standard workload descriptor that rollout-engine papers report alongside turn count and context length, and PD-switching papers evaluate against it. Requires confirmation at cluster scale by a lab. p = 0.08 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: L3 routes (Lloyd / Netravali / Tri Dao): direct, a ruler for a rollout-engine decision with a systems experiment. Industry: RL infra and serving teams. Jacob's edge: computer engineering (DP-attention barrier, interconnect cost model) and the Little's-law style time-integral statistic. Zero relevance to L1, L2, L4, L5.
scorecard.kill_probe: Four workloads x two topologies x 3 repeats on one 8-GPU node, ~80 GPU-hours, ~$250, 7 days; dead if either off-diagonal cell breaks the predicted sign or Omega is not monotone with the speedup.
scorecard.density_ownership: arXiv API 2026-10-19: prefill+decode+(interference|colocat)+(agent|multi-turn|rollout) = 12 hits (Prorsa, AInfer-PD 2609.00993, PPD 2603.13358 'not all prefills are equal', P-PAS 2608.15171 prefill-decode interference crossover in vLLM, PackServe 2609.33224 white-box interference latency models, 2609.34663 tool re-arrival prefill interference on NPUs); prefill+(disaggregation|disaggregated)+(when|whether|break-even|cost model|analytical) = 35 hits, closest 2605.28302 (AFD design space, 'when does each level pay off', by simulation) and 2601.21351 (one trace statistic theta governs AFD provisioning, nonparametric estimator from traces: the same ruler shape for a different decision); (data parallel attention|DP attention)+(prefill|MoE)+(idle|straggler|imbalance) = 0 hits, so the DP-attention idle mechanism is Prorsa's alone in abstracts. Occupied: Prorsa owns the idle-ratio characterization and the math/coding reversal; PEARL owns runtime colocate-vs-disaggregate selection for RL; PackServe owns interference latency models for serving. Not occupied: a pre-deployment log statistic for the sign of disaggregation in rollout, tested by crossing turn count with injection protocol. Pre-window precedents for the kill search: DistServe 2024 and Splitwise 2024 (interference as the motivation for PD split), Sarathi-Serve 2024 (chunked prefill as the colocation fix). Kill search owed: words interference, colocation, chunked prefill, break-even, provisioning, workload statistic, DP attention, expert parallel barrier; quote PEARL's and 2605.28302's limitation sections.
scorecard.why_now: Prorsa 2026-10-12 (the reversal with numbers and the named mechanism); PEARL 2026-09-28 (the question posed and answered by profiling, not by a statistic); SGLang PD disaggregation single-node since 2025; SWE-agent .traj execution_time public.
scorecard.register: Ruler (a workload statistic with a sign prediction) plus a small systems experiment. It is not a scheduler, not a switching policy, not a simulator paper, and not a reproduction of Prorsa at scale.

title: No-scaffold habit as a ruler for the sign of scaffold effects
statement: Measure each model's no-scaffold habit vector (share of runs that answer without a tool call, give-up rate, grounded-answer share, repeats, actions since last new information) from k=5 baseline runs per task, then predict the sign of each scaffold switch's accuracy effect on an unseen domain and unseen models, and score the prediction against three competitors: baseline accuracy, model size or price, and the capability-saturation rule of 2512.08296. Out-of-sample domain: MedicalHarness (2610.05778; code and data public, 83 non-browser tasks, MH-Lab switches for context policy, planning and tool exposure) on five open-weight models served locally; same-domain new models: EvoOntology's public data-agent harness on KramaBench (104 tasks) with and without the semantic layer on three open models not in the paper's seven. Every per-(model, switch, environment) effect carries its run-to-run standard error from k runs, so a sign is only scored where |effect| exceeds two standard errors, and the habit vector's intraclass correlation across runs and across two reasoning-effort settings says whether the habit belongs to the model or to the setting.
claim: A model's no-scaffold habit, measured from five baseline runs per task, predicts the sign of a scaffold's accuracy effect on an unseen domain and unseen models more often than the model's baseline accuracy does.
trick: Watch how a model behaves with no scaffold, bet on which scaffolds will help it, and count how often that bet beats simply betting on its accuracy.
why_now: MedicalHarness released code, 107 tasks and mechanism switches on 2026-10-05, giving a second domain where a harness switch can be flipped per model; the card paper (2026-10-14) published the three-habit taxonomy with its own recognition rates (73/82/87/92% from 5/10/20/50 baseline runs; 39-55% for GPT-5.4); 2610.00651 (2026-09-30) showed scaffold coverage, not task count, caps model-ranking reliability on HAL and Harbor, so a per-model predictor of scaffold effect is the missing covariate.

killing_experiment.design: Arm 1: MedicalHarness MH-Lab, 83 tasks (MedTool 32, MedMemory 23, MedPlanning 28; MedWeb dropped), five open-weight 20-35B models (e.g. Qwen3.6-27B, GLM-4.7-Flash 30B-A3B, gpt-oss-20b, Gemma-4-27B, Llama-4-Scout), baseline all-off with k=5, each of three switches on with k=3; 5 x 83 x (5 + 9) = 5,810 runs. Arm 2: EvoOntology harness on KramaBench, three new open models, layer on/off, k=3; 1,872 runs. Compute the 12 trace features per run (re-implemented from the card paper's definitions), the per-model habit vector, nearest-centroid group against the paper's three groups and a scalar p_blind (share of runs answering with no tool call). Predict the sign of each of 45 (model x switch x environment) effects plus 9 (model x benchmark) layer effects by (a) the paper's sign rule from the habit, (b) baseline accuracy above/below the median, (c) size/price rank, (d) 2512.08296's saturation rule. Score sign agreement on effects whose |effect| > 2 run-to-run standard errors. Identifiability: ICC of the habit vector across the five baseline runs; for one model, repeat baseline at two reasoning-effort or temperature settings.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Habit-based sign accuracy is within one correct sign of accuracy-based prediction on the scored effects (the taxonomy is capability saturation relabelled), OR the habit vector's across-run ICC is below 0.5 (the habit is a property of the run, not the model, and cannot be a per-model ruler), OR fewer than 15 of the 54 effects clear two standard errors (the sign is not measurable at this scale and the paper's one-run-per-cell groups were noise).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Habit ties baseline accuracy on the context-policy and tool-exposure (layer-like) switches, where both say 'strong models look, weak models do not', and beats accuracy on planning/orchestration-like switches, where premature answering is a style not a capability (the card paper: GPT-5.5 keeps 78-94% blind answering at every effort while accurate). Judgment: p=0.4 that habit beats accuracy overall; p=0.6 that ICC exceeds 0.7.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper organizes its guidance by behavior group, so it assumes the habit is the deciding information; 2512.08296 assumes capability saturation ('coordination yields diminishing returns once single-agent baselines exceed certain performance') and reports consistent architecture preferences on unseen frontier models from capability alone; 2603.29231 says memory scaffolds hurt all 10 models, i.e. no habit dependence at all.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: Habit wins: leaderboards (HAL, Harbor) add a blind-answer-share column next to accuracy, harness choice is indexed by habit, and 2512.08296's predictive model gains a behavioral covariate. Accuracy wins: the three-habit taxonomy collapses to 'scaffold the weak' and the card paper's guidance is a capability rule. ICC below 0.5: the paper's Appendix B recognition rates were the headline and 'behavior group' is a sampling artifact of one run per cell.

identifiability: The scaffold effect for (model, switch) is random given the policy's sampling at its stated temperature (open models: the served temperature, fixed and reported; the card paper left provider defaults unstated) and the task set; the environments (files, databases, EMR mock) are deterministic after the action, so there is no luck term beyond the policy's own draws. The habit vector is a property of the model-at-setting, not the model: the card paper's GPT-5.4 drops from 24% to 3% blind answers when reasoning effort rises, so the ruler is indexed by (model, effort/temperature) and the probe measures ICC across runs and across two settings for one model to say which it is.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a measurement of scaffold-model interaction on public harnesses, not a frontier post-training problem. Solo is feasible with open models and public code. What a lab has that solo lacks: the card paper's authors hold ~14,000 annotated runs across seven closed models; if those traces are released the first half of this probe is a zero-GPU re-analysis, and they are the natural owners (re-open test: ask whether traces and the 12 feature definitions are released). Dropped hints recorded here: operator 5 alone (run-to-run variance of the scaffold effect) is a service, since 2602.07150 (SD > 1.5 pp at temperature 0, 60,000 SWE-bench runs), 2608.11323 (agent main effect < 3% of variance; agent x task 7-23%) and 2610.00651 already made the one-run-per-cell point; it survives only as the two-standard-error filter inside this probe. Operator 2 (reading the habit from the first N steps of a trace) is dropped: identifying the model from a prefix is fingerprinting with a known answer, and 2610.05572 shows early run-level discrimination at 0.50-0.55 while cross-unit (model, task) information dominates; the early-prediction register is occupied (2607.06503, 2608.03222, 2608.29685, 2610.19614, 2609.25647).

scorecard.target_value: Asked in print: the card paper's Limitations ('systems that choose or adapt CETs to an agent's observed behavior' is future work; newer models 'may show behaviors beyond the three groups'); 2610.00651 ('spend evaluation budget on the sources of uncertainty that matter', scaffold coverage being the binding one); MedicalHarness ('no single harness is best across models and tasks'). Who pays: leaderboard owners (HAL, Harbor) who need a per-model covariate for scaffold effects; data-platform and harness teams choosing a scaffold per model; benchmark owners deciding how many runs per cell.

impact_ceiling.floor: A replication note: the paper's group effects clear or do not clear a measured noise floor on a second domain, with ICC numbers for the habit vector. Requires only arm 1. Judgment p=0.45.
impact_ceiling.middle: A ruler paper: the habit vector predicts the sign of scaffold effects out of sample better than accuracy on one switch family (planning/orchestration) and no better on the others, with the identifiability result (model-at-setting). Requires both arms and the two-setting check. Judgment p=0.35.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: A leaderboard column: blind-answer share and give-up rate reported per model on HAL/Harbor, and scaffold effects predicted from them across benchmarks; adopted by one leaderboard. Requires the middle result plus a HAL/Harbor re-analysis from released traces. Judgment p=0.15.

scorecard.relevance: HAL (Narayanan): direct, the column and the per-model covariate for 2610.00651's inter-scaffold reliability. Narasimhan (tau-family): moderate, tau-bench scaffold sensitivity is the same shape with a simulated user added. Evaluators: direct (how many runs per cell; which claims a one-run table supports). Industry: data-platform and agent-harness teams picking scaffolds per model. Jacob's edge: zero for theoretical physics; small for computer engineering (serving five open models locally, trace feature extraction); the statistics (variance components, ICC) are standard.
scorecard.kill_probe: Arm 1 alone (5,810 MedicalHarness runs, ~80 H100-hours, 6 days): if habit-based sign accuracy is within one sign of accuracy-based on the effects clearing 2 SE, or ICC < 0.5, dead.
scorecard.density_ownership: arXiv API 2026-10-19: scaffold/harness sensitivity query 399 total (50 returned, all in-window); run-variance agent evaluation 59; behavior-predicts-scaffold 254 (mostly off-topic). Closest, all read at abstract level: 2610.00651 (Bayesian variance decomposition, HAL/Harbor, inter-scaffold reliability), 2608.11323 (G-theory, agent x task, three estimators), 2605.23950 (harness variance decomposition protocol, position paper), 2610.05778 MedicalHarness (harness x model interaction about a quarter of variance; traces analyzed), 2602.07150 (run-to-run variance, two scaffolds), 2512.08296 (predictive model of architecture effects from capability, R^2 0.37, held-out models), 2610.10478 (base-model screens predicting post-training outcome: the analogous predictor shape). None returned uses a behavioral trace covariate to predict the sign of a harness switch out of sample; this is bounded by the search, the two closest limitation sections are unread, and this week's seeds 2610.22289 (scaffolding for ARC-AGI-3) and 2610.16757 (platform as part of the measurement) are adjacent. Kill search owed. Race window: about one scaffold-interaction paper per 3-4 weeks in this register against a 10-day probe.
scorecard.why_now: MedicalHarness release 2026-10-05 (public second domain with switches); the card paper 2026-10-14 (taxonomy plus its own recognition rates); 2610.00651 2026-09-30 (scaffold coverage caps reliability).
scorecard.register: Ruler (a measurement that grades the paper's taxonomy as a predictor), with a small recipe consequence (which column a leaderboard adds; how many runs per cell). It is not a scaffold-selection controller, not a new taxonomy, and not a new scaffold.
