title: Placebo semantic layer: does form or content stop investigators looking
statement: Add two control arms the paper did not run to the semantic-layer switch: a placebo layer with the same format and length that describes a different dataset's columns and conventions (wrong content), and a content-free layer that lists the columns with generic descriptions, alongside no layer and the true layer, on KramaBench (104 tasks) and a 100-task DataClaw subset with three open models spanning the paper's groups (two investigators, one premature answerer). Measure tool calls before the first answer, blind-answer share, grounded-answer share and accuracy per arm with k=2 runs, and attribute the layer's drop in investigation to its content (true layer only) or its form (placebo arms too).
claim: For models that investigate without a scaffold, a confident data description lowers tool use before the first answer regardless of whether its content is right, so the semantic layer's harm to investigators is a prompt-form effect, not informational substitution.
trick: Give the agent a confident data description that is wrong or empty and see whether it stops checking as much as it does with the right one.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-14) made the claim 'the semantic layer stops them from looking' with a single layer design and no content control; 2604.25149 (2026-04-28) showed the layer's single-shot gain is the same for three frontier models (+17 to +23 points), which says the content works when there is no loop; EvoOntology (2026-09-14) released a queryable layer served as a tool, giving a third form arm (layer as tool, not prompt) for free.

killing_experiment.design: Four arms (no layer; true layer; placebo wrong-dataset layer, shuffled across tasks, matched in length and format; content-free layer with column names and generic descriptions), 204 tasks, three open models served locally at a fixed stated temperature (two that investigate at baseline, one that answers blind at baseline, chosen after 50 baseline runs), k=2 runs per cell: 204 x 4 x 3 x 2 = 4,896 runs. Optional fifth arm: EvoOntology's layer served as an MCP tool. Readouts per arm: mean tool calls before first answer, blind-answer share, grounded-answer share, accuracy, each with its run-to-run standard error. Primary contrast: drop in pre-answer tool calls under the placebo arms as a fraction of the drop under the true layer, for the investigator models.
killing_experiment.kills_if: For both investigator models the placebo arms change pre-answer tool calls and blind-answer share by less than one third of the true layer's change and within two standard errors of zero: the harm is informational substitution, the form hypothesis is dead, and the result that survives is 'the agent trusts the content it is given, right or wrong' (a footnote for layer builders).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Placebo layers reproduce at least half of the true layer's drop in pre-answer tool calls for the investigator models, with accuracy falling under the wrong-content placebo and staying flat under the content-free one; for the premature answerer no arm changes tool use. Judgment: p=0.5 for the form result.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper attributes the drop to content ('the semantic layer stops them from looking' because the description substitutes for inspection); 2604.25149 attributes the single-shot gain to 'changing what the model is being asked to do', i.e. content; EvoOntology assumes a better layer is a more correct layer.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: Form dominates: every context-engineering evaluation needs a placebo-context arm (a standard control), and layers should be served as tools the agent queries rather than prompt text, giving EvoOntology's design choice its mechanism. Content dominates: the harm is substitution and the fix is a layer that states what it does not cover, and the paper's sign rule stands as stated.

identifiability: The drop in pre-answer tool calls is a property of the policy at its stated temperature; the environment (files, databases) is deterministic after the action, so every run-to-run difference is the policy's draw. The quantity depends on the model-at-setting (the card paper's GPT-5.4 blind share moves 24% to 3% with reasoning effort), so each model runs at one fixed effort/temperature, reported. k=2 runs give the standard error; the placebo content is shuffled across tasks so no task sees its own description by accident.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a control-arm measurement on public data-agent benchmarks with open models; not a frontier lab's core problem. Solo feasible with 40 GPU-hours. What a lab has that solo lacks: the card paper's harness and the closed-model investigators (Opus 5.5, GPT-5.5), where the effect was reported; open-model investigators are a proxy and the record must say so. L4 relevance is secondary (the layer is a prompt, not a lossy self-written message), so the lane is L1 scaffold sensitivity and attribution of the effect to content versus form.

scorecard.target_value: Asked in print: the card paper's Limitations (each scaffold tested in one representative design; other designs are future work) and its finding that the layer lowers investigators' tool use; 2604.25149's interpretation that the layer changes 'what the model is being asked to do'. Who pays: teams building semantic layers and data catalogs for agents (the data-platform industry), data-agent benchmark owners (KramaBench, DataClaw) deciding whether to ship descriptions, and anyone evaluating a context-engineering claim without a placebo arm.

impact_ceiling.floor: A control-arm result on two benchmarks and three open models saying how much of the layer's behavioral effect is content; cited by the next layer paper. Requires the four arms. Judgment p=0.5.
impact_ceiling.middle: A measurement with a mechanism: form explains most of the drop in investigation, content explains the accuracy change, and the layer-as-tool arm recovers investigation; a placebo-context arm becomes a standard control in context-engineering evaluations. Requires the fifth arm and one closed investigator model (about $400). Judgment p=0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: A recipe default changes: data-agent harnesses serve the layer as a queryable tool rather than prompt text, with the paper's sign rule rewritten by form; adopted by one public harness. Requires the middle result replicated on the card paper's own harness. Judgment p=0.1.

scorecard.relevance: HAL and evaluators: the placebo-context control as a standard arm for scaffold claims. Narasimhan (tau-family): low, no simulated user. Industry: direct for data-platform teams. Jacob's edge: zero for theoretical physics; small for computer engineering (serving models, building the placebo generator).
scorecard.kill_probe: Two investigator models x four arms x 104 KramaBench tasks x k=2 (1,664 runs, ~15 H100-hours, 3 days): if placebo arms move pre-answer tool calls by less than a third of the true layer's change and within 2 SE of zero, dead.
scorecard.density_ownership: arXiv API 2026-10-19: 'semantic layer' + agent 52 total (45 in window); placebo/distractor + description + tool use 48; text-to-SQL schema robustness 82. Closest, abstracts read: 2604.25149 (layer document helps three frontier models equally, single-shot, no loop), 2609.37153 ToxicBench (blind compliance with poisoned tool outputs; the trusted object is evidence, not a description), 2605.07769 (action bias: agents act when inaction is right), 2601.07226 (contextual distractors degrade reasoning models), 2608.16045 (data exploration as a first-class step), 2605.25838 (schema variants change text-to-SQL answers), 2609.15779 EvoOntology (layer as a tool). No returned paper runs a placebo or content-free description arm against agent tool use; bounded by the search, limitation sections unread, kill search owed. Occupied by the card: the true-layer effect per group. Not re-proposed: any compaction recipe (C-W42-01 killed, C-W42-02 parked).
scorecard.register: Measurement with a mechanism and a control arm, with a small recipe consequence (layer as prompt versus layer as tool). It is not a new semantic-layer design, not a prompt-injection or robustness study, and not a compaction or memory recipe.

neighbors_to_check_first: 2604.25149 — read whether any arm varies the document's content or includes a wrong document; their paired protocol is the single-shot baseline
2609.37153 — ToxicBench's 'checking versus adoption' split is the readout to borrow; check whether a schema-error arm already acts as a placebo description
2609.15779 — EvoOntology's backbone-conditional paired evaluation: whether it reports tool-use counts with and without the layer per backbone
2605.07769 — action bias as the competing mechanism: the agent acts on whatever it is given
2601.07226 — distractor effects on reasoning models: whether irrelevant context lowers tool use or only accuracy
2608.16045 — whether an explicit exploration artifact changes downstream tool use when supplied versus withheld

title: Does Source-Judged Compaction win by what it deletes or how much?
statement: Re-run the paper's AppWorld test-normal setting (168 tasks x 3 runs, OpenClaw safeguard compressor, 4,096-token window, frozen agent) with four compaction post-processors: none (Prompting), SJC's judge-gated delete, a marginal-matched random delete that removes the same number of entries per section at each boundary as a shadow judge would, and a zero-cost section-drop that deletes the Open TODOs and Pending user asks sections wholesale with no judge. Score Pass3 (fraction of tasks solved in all three runs) and Acc with across-run std, plus summary length and agent tokens per arm. The matched quantity is entries deleted per boundary per section; the second control is the cheapest deterministic incumbent.
claim: The Pass3 gain SJC reports over Prompting (+8.9 AppWorld GPT) is reproduced within noise by deleting the same number of entries chosen at random within each section, or by dropping the two plan sections without any judge, so the gain is a length-and-section effect and the provenance judge carries no information beyond it.
trick: Delete the same number of summary bullets at random, and separately delete the two plan sections outright, and see whether the provenance judge still beats both.
why_now: SJC landed 2026-10-14 with a public compressor prompt (OpenClaw commit d2f8755), public benchmark (AppWorld) and a per-section deletion census (67.7% of Open TODOs, 86.1% of Pending user asks unsourced; 13-21% of entries pruned, 30-40% at the first boundary) that makes the matched-count and section-drop arms specifiable from the paper alone; PAIR (2609.36526, 2026-09-29) and RECAP (2610.22897, 2026-10-16) show the matched-state comparison culture is active in this exact lane this month.

killing_experiment.design: Four arms x 168 AppWorld test-normal tasks x 3 sampling-only runs with the paper's GPT agent (GPT-5.6 Luna, medium effort) = 2,016 runs; judge re-implemented from the paper's appendix prompt (one calibrated yes/no request per boundary) unless code is released; random arm uses the judge in shadow mode for the count only; section-drop needs no judge. Secondary: repeat on MiniMax-M3 if the GPT result is within 3 Pass3 points either way. Assumed cost: ~20 steps x 4K input + 0.5K output tokens per run at list price, doubled for reasoning tokens.
killing_experiment.kills_if: SJC beats both the matched random arm and the section-drop arm by at least 5 Pass3 points on GPT (with 3-run std under 3 points), i.e. the judge identifies harmful entries beyond their count and section; then the paper's mechanism claim stands and this candidate is a confirming footnote.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Section-drop matches SJC within 3 Pass3 points on GPT (deletions concentrate in the two plan sections and at the first boundary); matched random deletion recovers roughly half the gain (summaries shrink 14-27%, agent tokens fall 1.3-8.0%, and shorter summaries alone help); judgment probability that SJC does not beat section-drop by 5 points: 0.6.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper's reading: the deleted entries are harmful because they are unsourced (22 of 29 failure-following entries unsourced), so a provenance judge is the right gate; no random or section-level control is in the paper.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If random matches SJC: the judge is a length regulator, and every compaction paper reporting a filtering gain owes a matched-count control (a ruler change). If section-drop matches SJC: the fix is a one-line edit to the 29 surveyed compaction prompts (stop writing TODO and pending-ask sections), a default change for harness builders, and the $0.002-per-task judge is unnecessary. If SJC wins clearly: provenance carries information beyond count and section, and the next question is the per-entry value ruler (the TRACE candidate).

identifiability: Pass3 is random given (task, arm) only through the agent's and compressor's sampling at the provider's default temperature (the paper's three runs differ only by sampling; confirm the temperature in its appendix) plus the judge's 2.1% answer flips; AppWorld's simulated apps are deterministic after the action, so there is no environment luck term. The random arm's randomness is ours and is a protocol choice, declared as such. Pass3 over 168 tasks has a binomial standard error of about 3.8 points, which bounds the resolvable gap; the 3-run std the paper reports is the within-arm noise.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: the comparison a reviewer asks for on an academic paper, run on public code and data with API dollars; nothing a frontier lab needs. The SJC/PAIR/TRACE authors are the natural owners and hold the harness; 'they have the stack' is a guess about priorities, and the re-open test is asking them whether a random or section control exists in their unpublished runs. A lab position adds nothing but the authors' own trajectories; solo is sufficient. Shares one harness with the label-vs-delete candidate (combined ~$1,000-1,150 API).

scorecard.target_value: Asked for in print by the checklist discipline of this lane rather than by a named party: PAIR (2609.36526) states that whole-trajectory full-vs-compressed comparisons 'cannot isolate individual compressions and are confounded by agent stochasticity', and SJC's own appendix reports provenance and correctness independent (92.2% vs 90.6% correct; AUROC 0.444), which is the open question of what the gate is actually selecting. Who pays: harness builders choosing a compaction prompt (OpenHands, SWE-agent, Pi, Claude Code-style structured summaries) and compaction-paper authors who need the control.

impact_ceiling.floor: A confirming footnote that SJC's judge carries information beyond length and section; requires the four-arm run; probability 0.4 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: A short measurement note showing a matched-count or section-drop control matches a published provenance gate, adopted as a required control in compaction papers; requires the GPT result replicated on M3; probability 0.45 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The section-drop finding generalises to two more public compactors (OpenHands condenser, Pi) and changes the default structured-summary template across harnesses; requires a second benchmark and two more harnesses (another ~$1,500); probability 0.15 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: L4 routes: all compaction and memory groups (control they owe); product teams (a zero-cost prompt edit if section-drop wins); Narasimhan's self-evolving interest only indirectly (what a self-written summary should and should not contain). Industry: harness teams, directly. Jacob's edge (theoretical physics, computer engineering): zero beyond experimental-design discipline.
scorecard.kill_probe: Four arms x 168 tasks x 3 runs on GPT-5.6 Luna; ~$700 API, 0 GPU-hours; kills if SJC beats both controls by >= 5 Pass3 with std < 3; 10 days including a one-week harness build.
scorecard.density_ownership: Occupied: SJC's delete-only gate and census; PAIR/TRACE's per-compaction paired continuations; RECAP 2610.22897 (2026-10-16) keep/compress/remove of a history block at matched states and seeds; The Complexity Trap 2508.21433 (observation masking matches LLM summarization) and Less Context, Better Agents 2606.10209 (last-5 pruning) as cheap-incumbent precedents; restore-counterfactual audit 2609.08279 uses random eviction as a control policy in QA memory. arXiv API: exact-phrase random-deletion/random-pruning + summary/memory + agent = 0 total; random/matched x deletion/pruning/eviction x compaction/summary x agent x control = 16 total, 15 in window, closest RECAP and 2609.08279; paired/counterfactual continuation x compaction x agent = 33 total, 28 in window, closest PAIR, TRACE, 2610.08722. No in-window hit runs a matched-count random control against a provenance or importance gate inside a closed agent loop; the absence of a hit is not evidence, and PAIR's and RECAP's limitation sections must be read before any 'not done' sentence. Kill search owed.
scorecard.why_now: SJC 2026-10-14 (public prompt, census, numbers); PAIR 2026-09-29 and TRACE corpus (public, mined by 2610.08722 on 2026-10-06) establish the matched-state protocol; RECAP 2026-10-16 shows the lane is now running keep/compress/remove comparisons, so the random control will be asked for soon by someone.
scorecard.register: Missing comparison (controlled, dose-matched by entries deleted) in the measurement register; a small recipe consequence (drop two sections) if the control wins. Not a new compaction recipe, not a judge improvement, not a training method.

neighbors_to_check_first: 2609.36526 — PAIR, same authors: read whether any random or section-level deletion control appears in their ablations or limitation text; their harness is the one we would rebuild
2610.22897 — RECAP (2026-10-16): block-level retain/compress/remove at matched environment states and rollout seeds; check whether it includes a random-edit arm and what unit it edits
2508.21433 — The Complexity Trap: observation masking matches LLM summarization; the pre-window cheap-incumbent precedent whose logic our section-drop arm repeats
2606.10209 — Less Context, Better Agents: last-5-tool-call pruning vs summarization with CIs over 5 runs; a second cheap-incumbent precedent
2609.08279 — restore-counterfactual audit: random eviction as a control policy with a matched-accuracy analysis; the closest matched-control design, in QA memory not a closed loop

title: Label the unsourced bullet instead of deleting it
statement: In the same AppWorld harness as the matched-deletion candidate, add a tag-only arm that keeps every summary entry and prefixes each with the judge's verdict ('[observed in environment or prior summary]' vs '[inferred plan or task reading; not confirmed by any output]'), and a delete-plus-tag arm, against Prompting and SJC delete. Measure Pass3 and Acc, the count of the paper's three failure patterns (rewritten constraint, invented deliverable, contradicted state) in failed runs by the paper's annotation protocol, and the fraction of supported entries retained (SJC keeps only 64.2%). The provenance bit the paper computes and throws away is passed forward to the consumer that the card says cannot otherwise tell a kept decision from a kept fact.
claim: Marking unsourced entries recovers at least half of SJC's Pass3 gain over Prompting while retaining 100% of supported entries, so the agent can consume a provenance label and delete-only is the wrong design for a compaction gate.
trick: Keep every summary bullet but stamp each one with whether the environment ever said it, so the agent after compaction can tell a fact from its own earlier plan.
why_now: SJC (2026-10-14) computes the per-entry provenance probability and discards it; its card documents that the agent executes unsourced plans as if observed. Compaction as Epistemic Failure (2607.13071, 2026-07-11) documents the same conflation of observation and persistence in Claude Code summaries; transparent-compact (2610.20116, 2026-10-14) shows that flagging what compaction stripped helps lightweight models avoid confident blunders. The label arm is one prompt-rendering change on top of the matched-deletion harness.

killing_experiment.design: Two added arms (tag-only; delete-plus-tag) x 168 AppWorld test-normal tasks x 3 runs on GPT-5.6 Luna, sharing the matched-deletion candidate's Prompting and SJC arms; failed runs annotated under the paper's written protocol by two LLM annotators with the paper's kappa procedure. Standalone cost if run without the sibling candidate includes the two reference arms.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Tag-only is within 1 Pass3 point of Prompting on GPT and the invented-deliverable and rewritten-constraint pattern counts in failed runs do not fall by at least a third relative to Prompting: the agent ignores provenance labels on its own summary, and only removal works. That negative is itself citable (agents do not read metadata in their own self-messages), so both outcomes are informative.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Tag-only recovers 50-80% of SJC's Pass3 gain on GPT and less on M3, with the invented-deliverable pattern falling most; delete-plus-tag is the best arm by 1-3 points because it also shortens the summary; judgment probability that tag-only recovers at least half: 0.5. Conceded in advance: the section headings Open TODOs and Pending user asks are already a weak provenance label and the paper shows the agent executes those entries anyway, so the explicit per-entry label must do what the heading did not.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper's design assumes unsourced entries must be removed because the agent treats every summary line as established (its three failure patterns); transparent-compact assumes flags help only lightweight models; 21 of 29 surveyed compaction prompts ask for decisions and next steps with no provenance marking.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If tag-only matches delete: compaction schemas should carry per-entry provenance (facts vs plans typed), a default every structured-summary prompt can adopt without a judge's deletion risk, and the 36% of supported entries SJC wrongly deletes are saved. If tag-only does nothing: the agent cannot consume provenance metadata in its own summary, which bounds what any label-based memory scheme (MemTrace anchors, Memory Echo's provenance gating) can expect from the reader and makes deletion or retrieval the only levers.

identifiability: Same as the matched-deletion candidate: randomness is the agent's and compressor's sampling at the provider default and the judge's 2.1% flips; AppWorld is deterministic after the action. The pattern counts are LLM-annotator labels with the paper's kappa (0.86 support, 0.80 pattern), not executable replay, and are reported as such; the Pass3 arm comparison is the executable measurement. The label is a protocol choice (wording and placement), so one fixed wording is pre-registered and a second wording is a robustness arm only if the first moves Pass3.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a controlled comparison of two uses of one computed bit, on public code and data, API-only; a product team (Claude Code, Codex, OpenHands) can run it on its own logs in a day and has more to gain, so the solo result is a published control, not a shipped artifact. Lane L4 permits a mechanism variant only with a controlled comparison; this is one, and it is written as measurement of the consumer, not as a recipe.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2607.13071 names the mechanism as 'a conflation of observation and persistence' in Claude Code compaction summaries and calls for re-verification; SJC's card states the agent 'cannot distinguish the two' after compaction and the paper never passes the bit forward; transparent-compact argues for maximal transparency of the agent's view of its compacted context. Who pays: harness and product teams writing structured-summary prompts; memory-system authors who rely on provenance tags being read.

impact_ceiling.floor: A negative: agents ignore provenance labels in their own summaries; a footnote cited by memory-schema papers; requires the two arms; probability 0.35 (judgment).

title: Per-entry counterfactual value of compaction bullets on TRACE's paired-replay corpus
statement: On TRACE's public corpus of 590 harness-triggered AppWorld compaction boundaries (each with a re-executable prefix state and its committed summary), take the 60 boundaries with the largest post-compaction burden, and for every summary entry b run n=4 paired continuations to task end from the same state with the summary intact and with only b removed, defining V(b) = success rate with b minus success rate without b. Grade three published signals with it: SJC's 83% attribution (fraction of entries that LLM annotators call failure-causing whose removal actually flips success), SJC's judge (the regret distribution over entries it would delete versus keep), and the provenance-predicts-value hypothesis (AUROC of the judge's probability against the sign of V). The ruler replaces LLM annotation of a symptom with executable replay of a cause.
claim: Fewer than 40% of the summary entries that annotators call failure-causing flip task success when removed, and the provenance score predicts an entry's counterfactual value no better than chance, so the harm of compaction lies in what the summary lacks, not in which bullets it contains.
trick: Remove one summary bullet at a time, rerun the agent from the same state, and count how often the outcome actually changes.
why_now: TRACE's paired-replay corpus is public and already mined by an outsider (2610.08722, 2026-10-06: 590 boundaries, re-executed prefix states, continuations under full context and under the summary), so the expensive part, resumable AppWorld states at compaction boundaries, exists; SJC (2026-10-14) supplies the entry-level annotation protocol, the three failure patterns and the judge whose verdicts the ruler grades; PAIR (2026-09-29) stops at the per-compaction level and leaves the entry level open.

killing_experiment.design: 60 positive-burden boundaries x ~15 entries x 2 arms x 4 continuations = ~7,200 continuations of ~10-15 remaining steps, plus 8 intact-summary baselines per boundary, on the corpus's agent model via API (confirm the model is still served; if not, re-run the boundary set with one current model and report the model change); SJC's judge re-implemented from its appendix and scored on every entry; failure-following entries annotated with SJC's written protocol by two LLM annotators. Prefix re-execution relies on AppWorld determinism, which the corpus already exploits.
killing_experiment.kills_if: At least 70% of annotated failure-following entries flip success in at least 2 of 4 continuations when removed, or the judge's probability separates negative-value from non-negative-value entries at AUROC >= 0.7: then entry-level annotation is a good proxy for cause, provenance tracks value, and SJC's design is vindicated; the ruler then becomes a service that confirms the paper. A second kill: prefix re-execution reproduces the corpus's boundary state in fewer than 90% of boundaries (non-deterministic apps), in which case the paired design is not available at this cost and the item is parked with that trigger.

preregistered_surprise.expected: 20-40% of annotated entries flip success on removal; most V(b) sit within the 4-continuation noise band; AUROC of provenance against sign of V is 0.45-0.55, matching the paper's own 0.444 for correctness; the regret of SJC's false deletes (supported entries with V > 0) is non-zero but small, 1-3 entries per 60 boundaries. Judgment probability that the flip fraction is under 40%: 0.6.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Summary entries cause failures (83% of failed runs follow one) and unsourced entries are the harmful ones; annotation-based attribution is treated as causal; per-compaction counterfactuals (PAIR, TRACE) are assumed to localise harm finely enough.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the flip fraction is high: per-entry value is a real control knob and a learnable target in closed loops (what Memory-PRM does for QA memory), and summary editing beats retrieval. If low: the summary's harm is omission, not commission, and the recipe choice moves to retrieval-on-demand and transparency (ACM, MemTrace, transparent-compact) rather than pruning; every attribution number from LLM annotators in this lane then owes a replay check, which is the L1 label-vs-replay gap the card flags.

identifiability: V(b) is random given (boundary state s_t, summary M_t, entry b) only through the agent's sampling at its deployment temperature (T > 0 in the corpus; confirm); AppWorld's apps are deterministic after the action, so there is no environment luck term and the paired difference is a property of the agent-summary pair, not of the protocol. Four continuations per arm resolve only flips of 2 or more; the noise band is reported per entry and the headline is the fraction of entries whose removal clears it. The annotator labels are the thing being graded, so their kappa is reported but does not enter the estimate.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent and solo-feasible because the corpus is public and the compute is API dollars; lab-contested only by the TRACE/PAIR/SJC group, who built the corpus and could run this in a week; 'they have the stack' is a guess, and 2610.08722 shows an outsider already publishes on their corpus, which is the evidence that the position is open. Also serves L1's label-versus-replay gap (the card's L1 fit) and is written so a benchmark owner can rerun it.

scorecard.target_value: In print: PAIR (2609.36526) says whole-trajectory comparisons 'cannot isolate individual compressions and are confounded by agent stochasticity' and that degradation 'concentrates at isolated compression events', leaving the within-summary level open; 2610.08722 ends by stating 'what corpora should ship' for boundary-level questions; SJC's card concedes an entry 'raises the chance of the error rather than determining it'. Who pays: compaction-paper authors who report annotation-based attributions, and the corpus owners (TRACE) whose release this extends.

impact_ceiling.floor: A replication note: executable replay confirms the 83% within 20 points; a footnote; requires the 60-boundary run; probability 0.3 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: Annotation overstates causation by 2x and provenance does not predict value; a required replay check for attribution claims in compaction papers and a per-entry value column added to the TRACE corpus; requires the run plus the regret analysis; probability 0.5 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The entry-level value distribution shows harm is omission not commission across two agents, redirecting the lane from pruning to retrieval and transparency; requires a second agent model and OfficeBench boundaries (another ~$1,000); probability 0.2 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: L4 routes: all compaction groups (a ruler for their attribution claims); product teams (whether to invest in summary editing or in retrieval); Narasimhan's self-evolving interest (value of a self-written line, measured). L1 (secondary): the label-vs-replay gap in failure attribution. Industry: moderate. Jacob's edge: the identification argument (deterministic environment, paired design) is elementary statistics, not physics; zero otherwise.
scorecard.kill_probe: 60 boundaries, leave-one-entry-out, 4 paired continuations each; ~$600 API, 0 GPU-hours; kills if >= 70% of annotated entries flip or provenance AUROC >= 0.7, or if prefix re-execution reproduces < 90% of boundary states; 14 days.
scorecard.density_ownership: Occupied: per-compaction paired continuations (TRACE 2608.06503, PAIR 2609.36526) and the public corpus; per-item deletion-and-reanswer credit in QA memory (Hindsight Memory-PRM 2608.29605: 'one controlled deletion-and-reanswer per probe settles an intervention-calibrated entry-level presence credit'); per-question restore counterfactual for memory eviction (2609.08279, LongMemEval); RECAP 2610.22897 (block-level matched interventions); pre-window: ContextCite 2409.00729 (attribute a response to context parts by ablating them) and leave-one-out influence (Koh and Liang 2017). arXiv API: counterfactual/ablation/leave-one-out x summary/memory/compaction x agent x entry/item x continuation/replay = 9 total, all in window, closest 2609.08279 and 2608.29605, both QA-reader regimes with no closed agent loop; paired/counterfactual continuation x compaction x agent = 33 total, 28 in window, all at the compaction or block level. No in-window hit ablates single summary entries with closed-loop continuations; absence of a hit is not evidence, and PAIR's limitation section plus 2610.08722's 'what corpora should ship' list must be read first. Kill search owed.
scorecard.why_now: TRACE corpus public and mined by 2610.08722 (2026-10-06); SJC's entry-level protocol and judge (2026-10-14); PAIR's per-compaction stopping point (2026-09-29); Memory-PRM's entry-level deletion credit in QA (2026-08-30) shows the design works where a reader can be rerun.
scorecard.register: Ruler (measurement instrument) graded first on a published attribution number and a published judge; not a compaction method, not a training signal (though it is the quantity a training signal would need), not a new benchmark.

neighbors_to_check_first: 2608.06503 and its released corpus — TRACE: confirm the 590 boundaries ship re-executable prefix states, the summary text per boundary, the agent model id and temperature, and task-end success (not only next-action burden)
2610.08722 — uses the corpus; read its 'what corpora should ship' list and whether any entry-level ablation is mentioned as missing

title: Effort notch and fresh restart as control arms for scaffold gains
statement: Grade every scaffold arm in 2610.22289 against two compute-only controls at matched normalized tokens: the plain Baseline agent one effort notch higher (already in Table 1, zero dollars) and a fresh-restart controller that starts a new Codex conversation on the same game whenever Baseline exits stuck, capped at the scaffold's mean spend (new runs, EnvTraverse v0.1, ARC-AGI-3 25 public games, 3 reps). Table 1 already shows the dominance for the lower notch: GPT-5.5 Baseline xhigh (16.08 M tokens, RHAE 50.45) beats Controlled_RESET high (42.19 M, 45.92) and Stop-and-report high (14.19 M, 34.86) on both axes, and GPT-5.6-sol Baseline max (15.34 M, 89.59) beats Stop-and-report xhigh (16.57 M, 77.33) and Controlled_RESET xhigh (18.36 M, 84.59); the open case is the top notch (GPT-5.5 xhigh: Baseline 50.45 vs Controlled_RESET 61.44 at 2.8x tokens), which the restart arm tests. Output is one number per scaffold, the compute-explained share phi = (S_ctrl(c) - S_0) / (s - S_0), where s and c are the scaffold's score and spend, S_0 the plain agent's score and S_ctrl(c) the best compute-only control at spend c.
claim: On ARC-AGI-3 the plain agent given the same normalized tokens through the vendor effort knob or a dumb restart recovers at least half of every environment-agnostic scaffold's gain, so 'control, not new facts' is mostly 'more tokens' at this horizon.
trick: Before crediting a scaffold with organizing the agent, hand the plain agent the same tokens by turning the effort knob or restarting it from scratch, and see how much of the gain the tokens alone buy.
why_now: EnvTraverse v0.1 with the Baseline, Stop-and-report and Controlled_RESET agents and the full run artifacts (Codex agent logs with turn.completed.usage, per-step level metadata) released 2026-10-15 (github.com/astroseger/envtraverse; Dropbox now, Zenodo forthcoming); 2607.12227 (2026-07-14) made matched feedback-and-inference budgets the standard for judging harness search and reported that hand search still wins by 80% on ARC-AGI-3, a result the Table 1 dominance pattern contradicts for hand-written scaffolds; GPT-5.6-sol's nearly flat cost across effort (15.3-18.9 M) makes the effort-knob control cheap.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 (zero dollars): recompute the Table 1 dominance pattern per run from Table 4 and, from the released artifacts, score-at-budget curves by truncating each run at cumulative normalized cost B (join Codex turn.completed.usage events with step_*_metadata.txt level progress by timestamp; replay the truncated action prefix with the repo's generate_scorecards_by_replay.py) to check whether arms separate on the common support B <= 9 M or only beyond Baseline's natural stopping point. Step 2: at GPT-5.5 xhigh (the top notch for that model, where Controlled_RESET 61.44 vs Baseline 50.45 is outside the 3-rep spreads 58.0-64.5 and 48.6-52.5), run Baseline plus a fresh-restart controller (new conversation on exit after the stuck protocol, no rule enforcement, no reread text beyond the main prompt) with the client refusing further actions once cumulative cost reaches 45.5 M, 3 reps of 25 games. Optional step 3: Baseline at GPT-5.6-sol high, 3 reps, to fill the effort curve. Dollar estimate assumes about $12 per M normalized tokens; ARC-AGI-3 only, since Terminal-Bench is wall-clock limited and effort changes wall-clock.
killing_experiment.kills_if: The restart arm at matched spend scores below 53.2 RHAE (recovers under 25% of the 11.0-point Controlled_RESET gap at GPT-5.5 xhigh) in all 3 reps, and the truncation curves show the scaffolded arms above Baseline on the common support B <= 9 M by more than the 3-rep spread: then tokens are not tokens, scripted control is organizational, and the paper's claim stands at matched spend (the kill result is itself the missing comparison the authors asked for in Sec. 9.3).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment p about 0.6: the restart arm recovers at least half of the Controlled_RESET gap at matched spend (RHAE >= 56), the scaffolded arms sit on the Baseline truncation curve for B <= 9 M, and the whole published gain is persistence beyond Baseline's natural stopping point plus one effort notch.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper (Sec. 6.2, 10): 'the intervention supplies control around available information rather than a new game rule'; 2607.12227: harness search beats simple test-time scaling by 80% on ARC-AGI-3; the general reading that scaffolds add organization the model lacks.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If tokens recover >= half: every scaffold or harness paper owes an effort-knob arm and a restart arm, and HAL / ARC Prize cost columns become an effort-equivalent-gain column. If tokens recover < 25%: cheap scripted rules beat compute at the top notch, the 2607.12227 ARC-AGI-3 finding generalizes to hand-written scaffolds, and the right research object is which rules a script should enforce.

identifiability: Random given the Codex sampling only: ARC-AGI-3 is deterministic given the action sequence (the repo replays recorded actions with seed 0 and reproduces scorecards), so all run-to-run variance is the policy's default-temperature sampling plus service nondeterminism, with 3 reps per arm and repetition indices not matched seeds. Temperature is Codex's default, not exposed, and is the deployment protocol. The budget cap, the restart rule and the normalized-token weights (1/60 cached, 1/6 input, 1 output) are protocol choices and are stated; phi is a property of (model, effort, harness variant, game set) under that protocol, and the cap is reported as a signed cost because reaching more levels lets an agent spend more (paper Sec. 9.2).
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a measurement of published scaffold claims with public code and about $2k of API, no artifact or standing needed; frontier labs run effort sweeps internally but do not publish scaffold-vs-effort control arms. A lab would add Terminal-Bench 2.1 and FrontierCode replication at the four effort levels (HAL's 21/36 non-monotone cases) and a per-level decomposition; solo covers ARC-AGI-3 and the ruler definition. Risk solo: the same author (SingularityNET) owns the stack and Sec. 9.3 names the question; the re-open test is asking him whether a matched-cost run is planned.

scorecard.target_value: Asked in print: 2610.22289 Sec. 9.3 'Further analysis is needed to determine their relative contributions and whether they can be meaningfully separated'; 2607.15439 'these gains often exceed variant differences'; HAL 2510.11977 'higher reasoning effort reducing accuracy in the majority of runs'; W41 pressure point #3 Q2 (matched-budget, fixed-scaffold ordering, posed by 2610.00917); 2407.01502 cost-controlled comparisons. Who pays: ARC Prize (cost per task column), HAL, harness builders deciding between prompt engineering and an effort setting.

impact_ceiling.floor: A short note that one effort notch Pareto-dominates both environment-agnostic scaffolds and the ARC-specific reset script on ARC-AGI-3 in both models, from the paper's own Table 1 plus the restart arm; cited as a footnote by harness papers. Requires only steps 1-2. Judgment p 0.5.
impact_ceiling.middle: An effort-equivalent-gain ruler (phi) adopted as a reported number by HAL or the ARC Prize leaderboard, with the finding that phi near 1 on ARC-AGI-3 and phi far from 1 on Terminal-Bench where effort is non-monotone. Requires Terminal-Bench 2.1 replication (another $3-5k) and a leaderboard owner's buy-in. Judgment p 0.25.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: A controlled result that scripted rule enforcement beats compute only at the top effort notch and only via persistence, forcing control arms into harness-paper review across the agent-evaluation community. Requires three benchmarks, two model families, six reps. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan (tau-family): moderate, effort and cost accounting on agent benchmarks, not tau-bench itself. HAL (Narayanan): direct, cost-controlled comparison is their stated line. Evaluators (ARC Prize, Terminal-Bench): direct. Industry: moderate (harness vendors choosing effort vs prompt). Jacob's edge: theoretical physics supplies the control-arm and dose-matching habit; computer engineering relevance is zero.
scorecard.kill_probe: Restart-controller arm at GPT-5.5 xhigh capped at 45.5 M normalized tokens, 3 reps x 25 games, about $1,600 of the $2,200, 0 GPU-hours, 6 days; dead if RHAE < 53.2 in all reps and truncation curves separate on B <= 9 M.
scorecard.density_ownership: Occupied: effort > scaffold stated qualitatively by 2607.15439 (same author); matched-budget harness-search vs test-time scaling by 2607.12227 (Terminal-Bench 2.1 and ARC-AGI-3); score-at-token-budget curves by 2609.15309 Elo-per-token (open-ended tasks with continuous scores); cost-vs-accuracy Pareto by 2407.01502 and HAL; harness-vs-cost by 2610.00917; effort vs tool access by 2607.02436 (observational, one app). arXiv API 2026-10-19: scaffold AND 'reasoning effort' AND agent AND cost = 2 total (1 in window, off-target); harness/scaffold AND agent AND cost-matched/compute-matched/matched budget = 7 total, closest 2607.12227; effort knob AND scaffold AND Pareto/matched = 8 total, closest 2607.02436. Nobody has run the effort-knob or restart control arm on these scaffolds; this week's seeds (Doc2Harness 2610.20344, StateHarness 2610.17616, Probe-and-Resume 2610.21088) are harness recipes, not control arms. Kill search owed, with the two closest papers' (2607.12227, 2609.15309) limitation text quoted.
scorecard.why_now: EnvTraverse v0.1 code, three agents and full run artifacts public since 2026-10-15; matched-budget evaluation standard set by 2607.12227 in July 2026; GPT-5.6-sol's flat cost across effort makes the effort control nearly free.
scorecard.register: Definitive comparison with a ruler consequence (phi per scaffold). It is not a new scaffold, not a harness-search method, and not a benchmark.

title: Timed returns as the shuffled control for Stop-and-report
statement: Replace the agent's self-chosen return points in Stop-and-report with a client-enforced return every N environment actions, with N set from the released logs so the realized return count matches Stop-and-report's, and run it at GPT-5.5 high on ARC-AGI-3 (25 games, 3 reps) beside 3 fresh Stop-and-report reps, in EnvTraverse v0.1. Measure the placement value of self-reported difficulty as gain(triggered) minus gain(timed) over Baseline at matched return count and matched normalized tokens. Zero-dollar first step from the artifacts: per-level return rate in the 12 Stop-and-report runs versus per-level failure rate across all 48 runs, to see whether returns land on the levels agents fail.
claim: A return-of-control on a fixed action schedule with the same goal reminder delivers the same ARC-AGI-3 gain as returning 'when unsure', so the Stop-and-report gain is periodic re-anchoring, not recognized uncertainty.
trick: Interrupt the agent on a timer as often as it interrupts itself, give it the same reminder, and see whether knowing when it is stuck was worth anything.
why_now: The Stop-and-report instruction, controller and the 48 ARC-AGI-3 runs with return events went public on 2026-10-15 (github.com/astroseger/envtraverse, papers/paper03); the environment-agnostic client in EnvTraverse v0.1 is the hook that makes an enforced schedule a 20-line change; the paper's Sec. 9.2 states the mechanism is unresolved ('Asking Codex to report a difficulty may prompt additional reasoning while it formulates the report').

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 (zero dollars): from the controller and server logs count returns per run and per level for Stop-and-report at GPT-5.5 high; compute Spearman correlation between per-level return rate and per-level failure rate across runs and compare with a within-game shuffle. Step 2: implement Timed-return (the client returns 'Return control now' after N accepted actions since the last continuation; the controller resumes with the identical Appendix B.1.2 reminder; no Stop-and-report instruction), N chosen so expected returns per game match the observed Stop-and-report mean; run 3 reps of 25 games at GPT-5.5 high (about 14 M normalized tokens each) and 3 contemporaneous Stop-and-report reps as the triggered arm (Codex version drift since 0.154.0 makes the published numbers a weak reference). Report realized returns per game and tokens per arm; the comparison is valid only if realized return counts match within 30% and tokens within 20%.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Either (a) the fresh Stop-and-report reps show no gain over the published Baseline band (RHAE <= 30.3 in 2 of 3 reps), so there is nothing to attribute, or (b) the timed arm cannot be matched (realized returns off by more than 30% or tokens by more than 20% after one N adjustment), so the shuffled control is not constructible in this harness; in either case the candidate is dead and the record says Stop-and-report's gain is not reproducible or not decomposable by schedule.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment p about 0.55: the timed arm recovers at least 70% of the Stop-and-report gain at matched return count and tokens, and per-level return rate is uncorrelated with per-level failure rate (|rho| < 0.2, within the shuffle band), so the agent's 'unsure' signal is poorly placed and the gain is cadence.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper (Sec. 9.1): returning when stuck lets the reminder 'help it reconsider an unsuccessful approach or revisit neglected information'; the wider assumption that frontier agents know when they are stuck (ask-for-help and abstention literatures).
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If timed >= 70%: self-reported difficulty is a cadence knob, every return-control or 'ask when unsure' scaffold owes a timed control arm, and the right lever is the interval, not the trigger. If timed < 30% of the gain: self-reported difficulty in GPT-5.5 is well placed, the unread report is worth reading, and a measurement of agent metacognition on ARC-AGI-3 exists for the first time.

identifiability: The return decision is the policy's (Codex default sampling, not exposed, the deployment protocol); ARC-AGI-3 is deterministic given actions (replay reproduces scorecards), so run variance is policy sampling plus service nondeterminism over 3 reps with unmatched seeds. The timed schedule is a protocol choice and the quantity gain(triggered) minus gain(timed) is a property of (model, effort, harness) under matched return count and tokens, both reported; the per-level correlation in step 1 is computed over 25 games x levels with a within-game shuffle as its null, and 'failure' is replay-verified level completion, a verifier not a judge.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: an attribution measurement on a published scaffold using public code and about $1k of API. Density in return-of-control placebos is near zero (arXiv API 2026-10-19: agent AND return control / stop and report / ask for help / self-reported uncertainty AND placebo / random / shuffled / matched = 3 total, none on target). A lab adds Terminal-Bench and a second model; solo delivers the ARC-AGI-3 result. The author owns the stack; the re-open test is asking whether a scheduled-return arm is planned.

scorecard.target_value: Asked in print: 2610.22289 Sec. 9.2 (difficulty reports 'may prompt additional reasoning'; mechanism unresolved) and Sec. 4.3 ('instructions request these behaviors rather than enforcing them'); checklist item 'shuffled control for any targeting or placement claim'. Who pays: anyone shipping 'ask when unsure' or stop-and-report behaviors in coding agents (Codex, Claude Code style harnesses) and ARC Prize entrants choosing controller cadence.

impact_ceiling.floor: A note that timed returns match triggered returns on ARC-AGI-3 at GPT-5.5 high, cited by scaffold papers as the control they must run. Requires step 2 only. Judgment p 0.45.

title: Resolvable pairs: the noise ceiling on real-to-sim rank agreement
statement: Change the unit of a real-to-sim validity claim from 'sim agrees with real on k of M policy pairs' to 'sim agrees on k of M_res pairs whose real success-rate gap is resolvable at the trial count used' (a pair is resolvable when |p1-p2| >= 1.96*sqrt(p1(1-p1)/n + p2(1-p2)/n), with p the real success rate and n the real trials per arm), and re-score every published real-to-sim correlation table (SIMPLER 2405.05941, whose real and sim tables are public in simpler_env/utils/metrics.py; PolaRiS 2512.16881; SimFoundry 2606.28276; RoboSnap 2607.06699; the soft-body twin 2511.04665; R2S-Eval 2609.03276; YUBI 2610.17521) by three numbers: the resolvable fraction, sign agreement on resolvable versus unresolvable pairs, and the chance-corrected agreement kappa = (A - 0.5)/(Pbar - 0.5), where A is observed sign agreement and Pbar is the mean over pairs of Phi(|p1-p2|/SE), the agreement a perfect simulator could reach against a real sign that is itself a noisy binomial draw. Deliver with it the sample-size rule: real trials per arm needed to make a gap of d points resolvable at a given success band, and the number of resolvable pairs a validity claim needs for its agreement rate to be distinguishable from chance. This measures neither a visual nor a physics knob; it measures the real criterion's noise floor, which bounds any artifact-injection result (visual or physics) alike.
claim: Published real-to-sim rank-agreement numbers blend near-perfect agreement on resolvable pairs with near-chance agreement on unresolvable ones, so the headline metric (MMRV, Pearson r, k/M) says more about the real trial budget than about the simulator; in SIMPLER's own public tables the sim picks the real winner on 52 of 53 resolvable pairs and 24 of 34 unresolvable pairs (computed 2026-10-19 from REAL_PERF/SIMPLER_PERF, denominators 12-75 inferred from the decimal ratios and flagged for confirmation against the paper appendix).
trick: A proxy test cannot agree with a noisy reference more often than the reference agrees with itself, so split every policy pair by whether the real trials could tell the two policies apart and report simulator agreement only where the answer was knowable.
why_now: Three pieces in 12 months put real-side statistics on the agenda without grading the proxy: PhAIL (2605.29710, 2026-05-28) states that real VLA evaluation 'rests on binary success rate at a fixed timeout with N <= 25 rollouts per condition, almost always without confidence intervals'; AnyRank (2610.14603, 2026-10-10) ranks policies from hardware trials with a sim prior but does not grade the prior; YUBI (2610.17521, 2026-10-13) reports 8/9 with no interval and says so. Seven real-to-sim correlation claims landed in the window (arXiv API, 2026-10-19), which is the sample this ruler grades.

killing_experiment.design: Zero-GPU re-analysis: extract real success rates, trial counts and sim success rates from the tables of the seven real-to-sim papers above (SIMPLER already done for 87 pairs; PhAIL and RoboArena 2506.18123 give real-only pairwise data for the sample-size half); compute resolvable fraction, agreement split, kappa and the Spearman attenuation ceiling r_max = sqrt(rel_real * rel_sim) for each paper's Pearson r, where rel is the binomial test-retest reliability of the success-rate vector; produce the sample-size table.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Across the papers with extractable tables, either the resolvable fraction is >= 85% everywhere (the problem does not exist outside YUBI's near-ties) or raw sign agreement on unresolvable pairs is >= 0.9 (the real estimates carry far more information than their nominal n implies, so the binomial noise model is wrong). Either way the ruler changes no published number by more than 5 points and is dead; the SIMPLER split (98% vs 71%) would then stand as one footnote. If the 2026 papers that compare same-family checkpoints (pi0 vs pi0.5 variants) show resolvable fractions under 40%, the ruler lives.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment: SIMPLER-style cohorts spanning immature to mature policies (real rates 0.0 to 0.92) are ~60% resolvable and their Pearson r survives attenuation correction; the 2025-2026 papers comparing same-family checkpoints with n <= 25 are under 40% resolvable, their agreement on unresolvable pairs sits in 0.5-0.75, and their headline agreement falls by >= 0.15 after chance correction.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: That 8/9 sign agreement, MMRV 0.018 or Pearson 0.911 measures simulator fidelity; MMRV weights a violation by the real gap but not by the gap's uncertainty, so a 0.08 gap at n=12 counts the same as 0.08 at n=75.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If agreement on resolvable pairs is also low (< 0.8) in any 2026 paper, that simulator is broken and the pooled metric hid it; if agreement on unresolvable pairs is near 1.0, the sims are better than the real tests and the field should spend its hardware budget on more real trials per pair rather than on scene fidelity (the sample-size table says how many).

identifiability: Random given: the policy pair, the real scene/initial-condition distribution and the real trial count n per arm; the real sign is a function of two binomial draws, so its reliability is a property of the protocol (n) and of the true gap, not of the simulator. Temperature: RT-1 decodes argmax over discretized actions (deterministic given the observation), Octo samples a diffusion head; real-world variance comes from initial conditions and physical noise in both cases, so the binomial model is the right floor for both. Sim-side noise (GPU batch non-determinism, GPUSimBench 2607.13059) is the companion quantity owned by this week's import seed import:2026-W43-S4xF9 (Gauge R&R: repeatability of the engine as a gauge); this candidate is the real-side half and the two compose as r_max = sqrt(rel_real * rel_sim).
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent. Solo is fully feasible (public tables, zero GPU). A lab with a robot adds what solo lacks: new real trials on the unresolvable pairs to test the sample-size rule directly and to check the binomial model against repeated real batches (R2S-Eval 2609.03276 reports that real evaluation 'may produce different policy rankings across repeated evaluations'). Competitor stacks: Physical Intelligence / PolaRiS group and NVIDIA GEAR / SimFoundry hold paired real-sim data at scale and could run this in a day; 'they have the stack' is a guess about priorities, and the re-open test is asking them. limitation_quotes.quote: Ranking preservation and MMRV [1] need the real reference to order the policies. The bootstrap probability that MolmoAct2 outscores π0.5 on the real robot is 0.36 for bottles, 0.53 for bowls, 0.04 for blocks, 0.98 for latte and 0.36 for clear table. Two of the five tasks are ordered with confidence; both reconstructions agree with real on one of them and disagree on the other. We do not report MMRV on this basis.

We omit MMRV, whether a simulator preserves the real ranking of policies, because with two policies it rests on the real robot's per-task ordering, which is confident on only two of the five tasks (Appendix B); with ten cells the intervals on correlation and failure-stage disagreement are too wide to separate the reconstructions (Table 4).

All results reported in this section are evaluated with 20 simulated rollouts and 5 real-world rollouts for each policy, task, and perturbation dimension. In total, our evaluation includes 11,800 simulated rollouts and 1,115 real-world rollouts.

our empirical analysis is still conducted within a bounded evaluation scope. Specifically, our real-world experiments focus on tabletop manipulation with a fixed embodiment, covering a finite set of policies and task suites. Therefore, the results should not be interpreted as a definitive ranking of existing simulators or policies.

limitation_quotes.section: III-B Metrics for Real-to-Sim Evaluation Pipelines
limitation_quotes.quote: The key point is that we need to take the magnitude of the rank violation into account, measured as the difference in real-world performance between the mis-ranked policies. This provides a clear signal whether rank violations are caused by small real-world performance differences that are often a result of inherent noise in real robot evaluations

The success-rate bars show marginal 95% Wilson score intervals using 20 real or 80 simulated trials per policy. These intervals quantify each success-rate estimate; they are not confidence intervals for ranking accuracy or tests of the difference between policies. Ranking accuracy is reported as a point estimate over the fixed set of eligible scene–task comparisons

the number of hardware evaluations required for statistically reliable policy comparison can be large [47]. One approach to addressing this limitation is the use of proxy evaluations as a substitute for real evaluations [15], which we leave to future work.

Reliability. A reliable evaluator should produce policy conclusions consistent with the target setting. For policy ranking, it should agree with a reference ranking that reflects the actual capabilities of the same set of policies. Stability. As evaluation evidence accumulates, the estimated policy scores or rankings should converge and exhibit low variance across different trials and configurations.

objections.objection: The split's unresolvable half is uninformative about the simulator by construction: sign agreement A = P(R=S) = 1/2 + 2(q_r-1/2)(q_s-1/2) with q_r = P(real sign = true sign), q_s = P(sim sign = true sign) is symmetric; on pairs selected as unresolvable q_r is small by selection. Simulation under the record's own model: a perfect simulator (q_s=1) scored against SIMPLER's rates gets A_unres = 0.895 (the record's 0.9 kill line), and 0.69 / 0.57 on same-family cohorts at n=20 / 5 (the record's 'expected' band); on resolvable pairs a perfect sim with m=25 sim trials scores 0.79 and with n=5, m=20 scores 0.65 (winner's curse), so '<0.8 means the simulator is broken' is false.

title: Does the real winner survive the engine's speed knobs?
statement: Move YUBI's counterfactual-artifact-injection protocol from the visuals to the physics: hold the policies, the visual matching and the real criterion fixed, and vary the PhysX speed knobs that SAPIEN/ManiSkill3 expose (solver_position_iterations default 15, grid 4/8/15/30/60; sim_freq default 500 Hz for the Bridge twins, grid 100/250/500/1000 at fixed control_freq 5; contact_offset default 0.02, grid 0.005/0.02/0.05; TGS versus PGS solver, two PhysX contact-solver schemes; plus a YUBI-style touch-triggered weld grasp as the approximation arm) on SIMPLER's public evaluation twins (Bridge/WidowX tasks GPU-parallel in ManiSkill3, Google-robot tasks in the CPU SAPIEN version) with the public RT-1 (begin/15%/converged), RT-1-X and Octo-base/small checkpoints. Measure, per knob setting: absolute simulated success rates with batch-seed intervals, sign agreement with SIMPLER's public real success rates restricted to the 53 resolvable pairs, and the lane's per-step audit d_t = ||F_ref(x_t,u_t) - x_{t+1}|| with F_ref the finest setting (60 iterations, 1000 Hz), summarised as rho = share of return earned on steps with d_t > kappa, so that each flip is tied to the knob and the step that produced it. This candidate measures physics knobs; the visual artifact axis is held at SIMPLER's visual-matching default throughout.
claim: For frozen real-trained policies, the engine's speed knobs move absolute simulated success rates by more than 10 points on grasp-dominated tasks but flip the real winner on at most 1 of 53 resolvable SIMPLER pairs across the documented range, so ranking validity is cheap and absolute calibration is not; if instead five or more resolvable pairs flip inside the documented range, every real-to-sim validity number needs its physics settings as a reported column.
trick: Keep the robot, the policies and the pictures the same, turn only the knobs that make the physics engine faster, and watch whether the simulator still picks the same winner the real robot picked.
why_now: The SIMPLER Bridge twins run GPU-parallel in ManiSkill3 with editable SceneConfig knobs (docs fetched 2026-10-19; ManiSkill3 2410.00425, 2024-10-01), SAPIEN's own source says 'solver iterations 15 is recommended to balance speed and accuracy. If stable grasps are necessary >= 20 is preferred' (mani_skill/utils/structs/types.py, fetched 2026-10-19), seven real-to-sim validity claims in 12 months each report one physics setting, and RoboSimStudio (2610.18835, 2026-10-13, Newton engine builders) just made 'choices of solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable', so the question of which setting a validity claim depends on is live this month.

killing_experiment.design: Pilot on two tasks (google_robot_pick_coke_can, grasp-dominated, n_real=75; google_robot_open_drawer, contact-dominated, n_real=27) and three policies (rt-1-converged, rt-1-x, octo-base) covering 6 pairs, 5 of them resolvable; 5 knob settings (iterations 4/8/15/30/60 with the rest at default) x 3 batch seeds x 100 episodes each on SIMPLER's pose sweep; record success, d_t against the 60-iteration reference and sign agreement with REAL_PERF. Then the WidowX GPU twins (4 tasks, Octo-base/small, RT-1-X) for the contact_offset and TGS/PGS axes.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Across the whole knob grid, absolute simulated success rates move by less than 5 points for every policy-task cell and no resolvable pair flips: the speed knobs are irrelevant to evaluation of frozen policies on these tasks, which is dead as a paper and alive as one footnote ('evaluate at 4 iterations'). A second kill: if rho does not separate the knob settings that produce flips from those that do not (rho within noise across the grid while flips occur), the lane's audit instrument has failed its first evaluation-side test and that is recorded against L5's first kill test.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment: absolute rates on pick_coke_can fall by >= 10 points at 4 iterations for all three policies together (the engine author's note implies grasps destabilise below 20), rank on resolvable pairs flips in 0-1 of 53, and the weld-grasp arm raises every policy's success and flips 1-2 pairs because it removes the slip failures that separate marginal graspers (octo-base at 0.293 real) from strong ones.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Two things at once: real-to-sim evaluation papers (SIMPLER names 'control and visual disparities' as the key gaps; PolaRiS, SimFoundry, YUBI report one physics setting and never vary it) assume physics settings are second-order for evaluation; L5's own premise assumes iteration caps silently change what policies experience.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: Invariance on resolvable pairs with large absolute shifts tells engine builders and SIMPLER users that evaluation-grade physics is cheaper than training-grade physics and that SureSim-style absolute bias correction is setting-specific while rankings are not; five or more resolvable-pair flips inside the documented range tells the real-to-sim community that a 'digital twin' is a twin at one solver setting only and the setting becomes a mandatory column.

identifiability: Random given: the knob setting, the SIMPLER initial-pose sweep (deterministic grid), the policy's own sampling (Octo diffusion head samples; RT-1 argmax is deterministic given the image), and GPU PhysX batch non-determinism (documented by GPUSimBench 2607.13059), so each setting's success rate carries a batch-seed interval and the sim-side repeatability floor from import:2026-W43-S4xF9 applies; the real criterion is fixed (REAL_PERF, fetched) and its resolvability is the resolvable-pairs candidate's ruler, so only resolvable pairs count toward a flip. The quantity is a property of the engine-setting x policy pair, not of the protocol, provided the pose sweep and visual matching are held fixed across settings.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent to engine builders and robotics RL groups, as the lane says; solo is feasible at 15-100 GPU-hours on public twins and checkpoints with no new real data (the real criterion is SIMPLER's published table). What a lab would add: RoboSimStudio's authors (the Newton engine team) can run the same grid on Newton with force-feedback real data, and a group with a WidowX can add real trials to resolve the 7 unresolvable WidowX pairs. Race flag: RoboSimStudio (2026-10-13) is a tool for exactly these knobs, so the knob-sensitivity measurement is one experiment away for them; 'they have the stack' is a guess about priorities and the re-open test is asking them.

scorecard.target_value: Asked for in print: SAPIEN source note on 15 vs >= 20 iterations for stable grasps (engine author's own text); YUBI 2610.17521 holds physics fixed with a weld grasp and says grasp stability and slip are suppressed by construction (card complaint 3); L5 themes.yaml third kill test demands validation of the audit against real data for at least one task, which SIMPLER's real table supplies. Who pays: every group choosing iteration caps for evaluation twins (ManiSkill/SAPIEN at UCSD, NVIDIA Newton, Genesis), every real-to-sim evaluation paper that reports one setting, and the lane's own audit instrument, which gets its first real-anchored test.

impact_ceiling.floor: A short measurement: absolute shift versus ranking invariance across the iteration axis on two SIMPLER tasks, with intervals; requires only the pilot; p ~0.8 (judgment) that absolute rates move by >= 10 points somewhere on the grid.
impact_ceiling.middle: A measurement paper with a recipe consequence: evaluation-grade settings per task class, the weld-grasp arm quantified, rho tied to flips, adopted as a default or a reported column by the SIMPLER/ManiSkill maintainers; requires the full grid on 9 tasks and the rho separation to hold; p ~0.3 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The physics setting becomes a mandatory column in real-to-sim validity tables and engine builders ship an 'evaluation profile'; requires >= 5 resolvable-pair flips inside the documented range or a clean invariance result replicated on Newton by the RoboSimStudio group; p ~0.1 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: Robotics + learning faculty: direct (evaluation validity). Engine builders (SAPIEN/ManiSkill, Newton, Genesis): direct (which knob matters for evaluation). Robotics RL groups: indirect (bounds the exploit concern to training). Systems/scheduler route: zero in this candidate (no scheduling). Industry: checkpoint-selection teams, direct. Jacob's edge: time step and iteration count are convergence knobs, so the d_t audit and its reference are numerics he can reason about; GPU-scheduling edge is zero here.
scorecard.kill_probe: Pilot: 2 tasks x 3 policies x 5 iteration settings x 3 batch seeds x 100 episodes with d_t against the finest setting; ~15 GPU-hours, $0 on public assets, 5 days; dead if absolute rates move < 5 points everywhere and no resolvable pair flips; audit dead if rho does not separate flipping from non-flipping settings.
scorecard.density_ownership: arXiv API 2026-10-19, 12-month window: (simulat*) AND ('solver iterations' OR 'time step' OR timestep OR 'contact model' OR 'contact parameters' OR 'physics parameters') AND ('policy evaluation' OR 'sim-to-real correlation' OR 'real-to-sim') AND robot = 2 hits: Agentic Real2Sim 2607.19190 (VLM agents infer physical parameters and build an evaluation surrogate; no knob-sensitivity of rankings) and CRISP 2512.14696 (humanoid motion from video; off-topic). Lane neighbors: GPUSimBench 2607.13059 (distribution-level fidelity and non-determinism, not tied to what rankings do), GPUPhysBench 2609.35639 (correctness as matching expert code), SAPU 2305.17110 (interpenetration exploited by sim-trained policies; here policies are real-trained), Erez-Tassa-Todorov ICRA 2015 (CPU-era engine comparison, no policies). This week's seeds: RoboSimStudio 2610.18835 (tool for the knobs, Newton; no sensitivity measurement in the abstract), 2610.17221 (fidelity as a tunable dose for PDE surrogates, same error sources, different object). Occupied: building twins, inferring parameters, visual-artifact injection (YUBI). Not found: holding policies and visuals fixed and varying solver knobs against a published real criterion. Kill search owed; read SIMPLER's section on control disparities and RoboSimStudio's experiments before any 'not done' sentence.
scorecard.why_now: GPU-parallel SIMPLER twins with editable SceneConfig (ManiSkill3, docs fetched 2026-10-19); the engine's own source naming the iteration trade-off; RoboSimStudio (2026-10-13) exposing the knobs; seven one-setting real-to-sim validity claims in 12 months.
scorecard.register: Measurement (knob sensitivity of a validity metric) with a recipe consequence (evaluation-grade settings), using the lane's audit instrument as the mechanism probe. It is not a new simulator or contact model, not system identification, and not a training-time exploit study.

neighbors_to_check_first: 2610.18835 — RoboSimStudio: Newton-based tool making solver and contact knobs editable; read its experiments for any ranking-sensitivity result and record the group's stack and date

2405.05941 — SIMPLER: the section on control disparities and system identification says what physics was tuned once and held fixed; also confirm Google-robot envs' solver settings in ManiSkill2_real2sim

2510.04354 — SureSim: absolute bias correction is the quantity the expected result says is setting-specific

title: Convergence law of the capped contact solve along policy-visited states
statement: Roll out the public MuJoCo Playground checkpoints (Go1 joystick, trained at Newton iterations=1 and ls_iterations=5 at timestep 0.004; Leap-hand cube reorientation at iterations=5; cheetah at 4; MuJoCo's own default is 100 iterations with tolerance 1e-8, all values read from the shipped XML and the XML reference on 2026-10-19) in MJX, and at every visited state-action pair (x_t, u_t) re-run the single step with the solver cap K in {1,2,3,5,10,20,50,100 with tolerance 1e-8 as the reference} and separately with substeps h0/{1,2,4,8} inside a fixed control period so the task is unchanged. Record e_t(K) = ||x_{t+1}^{(K)} - x_{t+1}^{ref}|| in a mass-weighted norm (velocities scaled by the square root of the inertia matrix), the number of active contacts n_t, and whether the active contact set changed at t; fit per state the geometric law e_t(K) = a_t * rho_t^K that 2610.17221 assumes for its solver axis (rho = contraction factor, the ratio by which error shrinks per iteration). Measured how: the spread of rho_t across visited states, the fraction of contact steps where a single-rho fit has R^2 < 0.9, the knee of e_t(K) against n_t, and the lane's exploit share rho_L5 = sum_t r_t 1[e_t(K_default) > kappa] / sum_t r_t with kappa set on the converged-trained policy.
claim: Along policy-visited states the capped Newton contact solve has no single convergence rate: the per-state contraction factor spreads over more than an order of magnitude and tracks the number of active contacts and contact-set changes, so the scalar fidelity tag xi_hat that 2610.17221's mixture recipe needs cannot be written down for GPU rigid-body RL and any fidelity schedule there has to be per state.
trick: Take the states a trained policy actually visits, re-step each one with more solver iterations, and plot how fast the error falls per iteration: that curve is the dose-response law of the simulator's fidelity knob, and whether it is one curve or a thousand decides whether fidelity is a dial or a lottery.
why_now: MJX (2023) and MuJoCo Warp (2025) made the capped Newton solve the production path, with per-task caps shipped in model files (Playground go1_mjx_feetonly.xml: iterations=1, Feb 2025); Warp exposes solver_niter per world (mujoco_warp/_src/types.py, read 2026-10-19), so cap-hit is observable; 2610.17221 (Oct 2026) supplies the compute-optimal recipe that consumes exactly this law and declines any axis whose law is unknown.

killing_experiment.design: 4 Playground tasks x 50 episodes x up to 1000 steps = about 200k visited states; re-step each at 8 caps and 4 substep levels in MJX (embarrassingly parallel across states); fit e_t(K) per state; compute rho_L5 for the coarse-trained and a converged-trained (cap 100) policy on Go1.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Either (a) a single-rho geometric fit reaches R^2 >= 0.95 on >= 90% of contact steps for every task, so the law exists and fidelity is a scalar dose (the card's recipe ports directly; this candidate dies and the mixture candidate inherits a free tag), or (b) e_t(K_default) < kappa on >= 99% of steps and rho_L5 does not separate the iterations=1 policy from the cap-100 policy on Go1 (lane kill test 1), so the cap is not a silent trade on MJX Playground tasks and the lane's premise is refuted for this engine.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Bimodal, not geometric: on more than 70% of steps (free flight or persistent contact with a good warm start) e_t(1) is already below 1e-4 of the per-step state change and K is irrelevant; on contact-set-change steps e_t(1) is of the order of the per-step velocity change and falls slower than geometric until the active set is identified, with the knee at roughly n_t iterations; those steps carry a share of return (touchdowns, grasp onsets) several times their count share, and rho_L5 separates the iterations=1 Go1 policy from the cap-100 one.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: One warm-started Newton iteration is accurate: the MuJoCo XML reference says 'accurate results are obtained with fewer iterations' when warmstart is on, and Playground ships iterations=1 for Go1 and reports zero-shot transfer; 2610.17221 assumes a single contraction factor per solver axis (rho = 0.99994 SSOR, 0.95 chord Newton).
preregistered_surprise.would_change: A single-rho law per task (kill a) means the fidelity knob is a scalar dose and the compute-optimal mixture recipe applies to RL without modification; e_t(K_default) below kappa everywhere (kill b) means the iteration cap is not where the sim-to-sim gap lives and the lane moves to the time-step axis or to PhysX/Isaac; the expected bimodal result means the fidelity tag must be per state (from n_t and the residual), which is the ingredient every fidelity schedule in GPU RL is missing.

identifiability: e_t(K) is deterministic given (x_t, u_t, engine build, cap, batch position); the only randomness is GPU-batch non-determinism (documented by GPUSimBench), reported as a repeat-step spread. Whose temperature: the policy's action sampling only chooses which states are visited; the audit uses the deterministic mean action and states the visited-state distribution (policy, task, episode count) as the conditioning set. The law is a property of the engine at a state, not of the protocol; kappa and the norm are protocol choices and are reported with a sensitivity sweep.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent. Solo is feasible: public checkpoints, free engine, 10 GPU-hours. A lab (DeepMind MuJoCo, NVIDIA Newton) has the engine internals and the production task set but has not published the along-visited-states law; GPUSimBench measures distribution-level fidelity, not the per-knob dose-response. The operator-4 'regret when the optimum jumps' hint is folded in here rather than written as its own candidate: the discontinuity of the fidelity axis is read directly from the knee of e_t(K) at active-set identification, while the regret of a calibration recipe measures the recipe and needs a full lambda x budget sweep in RL (hundreds of GPU-hours, over the solo bar).
