limitation_quotes.quote: This work has several limitations. First, GPUSimBench currently covers only a limited set of tasks and metrics, and the conclusions should be interpreted within this benchmark scope. Specifically, we evaluate two scalability scenes and one contact-rich real-world-matched experiment, all on a single hardware and software stack. As a result, the reported performance and variability may change across different GPUs, drivers, and simulator versions.

a primary source is the algorithmic path taken by iterative numerical solvers: small floating-point perturbations can change contact ordering, activation of constraints, projection decisions, and early-termination conditions, leading to different sequences of intermediate iterates even with identical nominal settings.

MuJoCo Playground inherits the limitations of MJX due to constraints imposed by JAX. First, just-in-time (JIT) compilation can be slow (1-3 minutes on Playground's tasks). Second, computation time related to contacts does not scale like the number of active contacts in the scene, but like the number of possible contacts in the scene.

limitation_quotes.section: Appendix A.1 and Table III caption
limitation_quotes.quote: Certain XMLs were modified for performance and are shown in the table. [...] Where specified, XML modifications were made to the solver iterations, line search iterations, as well as contact custom parameters for MJX.

At large h the Newton iterates can overshoot, so instead of a line search we run a fixed budget and return the iterate with the smallest residual from index k_min onward; the floor k_min blocks early acceptance of under-converged states. On mesh terrain the final iterate overshoots an earlier, lower-residual one by up to three orders of magnitude on a third of steps.

PRDP is limited to settings that involve iterative linear solvers. [...] Our work opens up many interesting directions for future investigations, such as smoother relations between the achieved plateau ratio r and the conducted iterations/prescribed tolerance in the physics solver.
The LF simulation simplifies the robot collision model, coarsens the physics time step, reduces the number of physics solver iterations, and disables self-collisions.

The resulting convergence is non-monotonic in the outer iteration count and depends on multiple knobs that interact non-trivially. We therefore run all simulations to a fixed iteration count and study fidelity along the spatial discretization axis only.

title: Compute-matched fidelity mixture versus fixed solver cap in GPU RL
statement: Train PPO in MJX Playground on Go1 joystick (default Newton cap K=1) and Leap-hand cube reorientation (default K=5) under four arms that consume the same total number of solver iterations summed over worlds and steps, I: fixed K=1 for N steps; fixed K=2 for N/2 steps; a stationary batch-wide mixture that runs the whole batch at K=1 with probability 8/9 and at K=10 with probability 1/9 (expected K = 2) for N/2 steps; fixed converged K=100 with tolerance 1e-8 for N/100 steps; plus one tag-conditioned mixture arm where the policy sees the per-step fidelity tag during training and is deployed with the tag set to 'converged', the card's own conditioning trick moved from regressor to policy. Evaluate every arm with deterministic actions under the converged engine (return R_conv), under its own training fidelity (R_train), the sim-to-sim gap G = R_train - R_conv, and the lane's exploit share rho_L5 with the converged step as reference; report wall-clock beside I because collision detection and kinematics do not scale with K.
claim: At equal solver-iteration budget a 1-in-9 converged-step mixture reaches the return under the converged engine of fixed K=2 and halves the exploit share of fixed K=1, so rare accurate steps are to a policy what the few accurate samples in 2610.17221 are to a surrogate: the correction term that makes the cheap majority safe to use.
trick: Spend the same number of solver iterations either evenly (a fixed cap) or lumpily (mostly one cheap iteration, now and then a fully converged step), and measure which policy performs better once the simulator is run converged: lumpy wins if the exploits a policy learns on cheap steps stop paying when any step can be the accurate one.
why_now: MFPG-PPO (2610.02505, 1 Oct 2026, fetched) made budget-aware high/low-fidelity PPO in GPU-parallel simulation a live topic and did it on a modeling axis ('a simplified simulator') with a control-variate mechanism, leaving the solver-cap axis of a single engine and the exploit question untouched; Playground ships K=1 for Go1 (Feb 2025); 2610.17221 (Oct 2026) measured the regressor case and never a consumer that optimizes.

killing_experiment.design: 5 arms x 2 tasks x 3 paired seeds = 30 PPO runs at equal I (Playground trains Go1 in minutes at K=1; equal-iteration arms have similar Newton cost, more fixed overhead), each evaluated for 100 episodes under the converged engine and under training fidelity, with the per-step audit for rho_L5.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Either (a) the mixture arm's R_conv is not above fixed K=1's by more than the paired-seed spread and its rho_L5 is not lower, on both tasks, so fidelity mixing does nothing for an optimizer and the card's result does not transfer from regression to control (an informative negative: the regressor/optimizer distinction is real); or (b) fixed K=1 already matches fixed K=100 in R_conv with G within seed spread and rho_L5 near zero on both tasks, so the cap is not where the sim-to-sim gap lives on Playground tasks and the comparison moves to PhysX/Isaac Lab or harder contact.

preregistered_surprise.expected: On Go1 the mixture arm equals fixed K=2 in R_conv within seed spread and cuts rho_L5 by at least half relative to fixed K=1, with G shrinking from a positive value (the K=1 policy scores higher in its own engine than in the converged one) toward zero; on Leap-hand the mixture's advantage over fixed K=5 is larger because contact-set changes are more frequent; the tag-conditioned arm does not beat the blind mixture, because a policy cannot act on a tag it will never see at deployment.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Either a low cap is fine (Playground: K=1 Go1 transfers zero-shot) or fidelity should be ramped monotonically during training (PRDP refines coarse to fine; curricula), and multi-fidelity RL means two simulators of different modeling fidelity (MFPG, 1712.06489), not two caps of one engine; nobody has reported the compute-matched fixed-versus-mixture frontier for a policy.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If only the tag-conditioned arm helps, a policy needs the fidelity information the engine discards (card point b) and engine teams gain a reason to expose solver_niter or the residual as an observation during training; if the mixture hurts (non-stationary dynamics confuse the critic), the recipe for RL is monotone refinement, not mixing, and PRDP's shape wins over the card's; if kill (b) holds, the lane's exploit premise is refuted on MJX Playground and must be re-tested on PhysX.

identifiability: Return is random given (seed: policy init, resets, PPO action sampling) and GPU-batch non-determinism; arms are compared on paired seeds, medians with spread over 3 seeds. Whose temperature: PPO's sampling policy is the training protocol by construction; R_conv and rho_L5 are measured with the deterministic mean action so the evaluation adds no decision variance. The matched quantity is named: total solver iterations I; wall-clock is reported separately and will differ because per-step cost has a K-independent part. Property of the engine-plus-algorithm pair at a task, not of the evaluation protocol.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent to engine builders and robotics RL groups; solo is feasible with public configs and about 50 GPU-hours. Lab-contested only in the narrow sense that the MFPG authors (2503.05696, 2610.02505) have a working budget-aware multi-fidelity PPO stack; 'they have the stack' is a guess about their priorities and the re-open test is asking them whether the solver-cap axis and exploit share are on their list. A lab would add the per-world mixture arm, which needs iteration-level scheduling to save wall-clock (the lane's scheduler), and Isaac Lab/PhysX arms.

scorecard.target_value: Asked in print: 2610.17221 tests its surrogate only at the top fidelity against top-fidelity labels and never a consumer that optimizes (card, information asymmetry c); MFPG-PPO 2610.02505 introduces 'a budget-aware MFPG-PPO to divide a fixed sampling budget among high- and low-fidelity data sources' and evaluates only return, not exploitation. Who pays: every group training in MJX/Warp/Isaac that picks a cap, and the engine teams that ship defaults.

impact_ceiling.floor: A compute-matched table on two tasks stating whether the solver cap changes return under the converged engine and exploit share; the first fixed-versus-mixture frontier for a policy. Requires the 50 GPU-hour probe. p = 0.8 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: Mixture dominates fixed caps at equal compute on the contact-rich task and the recipe 'run every n-th step converged' is adopted by Playground users as a default; the exploit-share drop is the mechanism. Requires the expected result on Leap-hand. p = 0.3 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The tag-conditioned arm wins, establishing that policies need per-step fidelity information, and an engine exposes it; this plus the convergence-law candidate gives a compute-optimal fidelity schedule for RL, the policy-side analogue of the card's frontier. Requires both the bimodal law and the conditioning result. p = 0.08 (judgment).

Systems route: the per-world mixture is the scheduler's use case, and this comparison gives the scheduler its payoff number (what fidelity buys at equal compute). Engine builders: consumers for defaults. Industry: GPU-simulator RL shops. Jacob's edge: GPU batch behavior and numerics, load-bearing for the compute matching. Zero for L1-L4 routes and for any LLM-agent consumer.
scorecard.kill_probe: 30 PPO runs at equal solver-iteration budget across 5 arms, 2 tasks, 3 seeds, evaluated under the converged engine with the per-step audit; 50 GPU-hours, about $150, 7 days; dead if the mixture is no better than fixed K=1 in R_conv and rho_L5 on both tasks, or if fixed K=1 already matches K=100 under the converged engine on both.

Pre-window precedents: 1712.06489 (simulator chain with Gaussian processes, fewer samples in higher simulators), PRDP 2502.19611 (coarse-to-fine iteration refinement during differentiable-physics training), Erez-Tassa-Todorov ICRA 2015 (CPU-era accuracy-versus-speed frontier across engines, from the lane block). None uses the solver cap of one engine as the axis, none measures exploitation, none reports the fixed-versus-mixture frontier at equal solver compute. 'Fidelity schedule'/'fidelity curriculum' AND RL query = 52 hits, all noise from 'progressive refinement' phrasing. It is not a new estimator, not a control variate, not a new simulator, and not a sim-to-real claim: the reference is the converged engine, not reality (lane kill test 3 applies before any real-robot sentence).

title: The solver's own stopping statistic as a free per-step fidelity flag
statement: MuJoCo's Newton solver computes, at every iteration, the gradient norm and cost improvement it uses for its tolerance test (mjSolverStat.gradient and .improvement in mjdata.h; MuJoCo Warp computes them for the same test but exposes only solver_niter per world, read 2026-10-19), then discards them before the policy sees the state. On the visited states from the convergence-law candidate, record the residual g_t after the capped iteration (re-stepped in CPU MuJoCo, which keeps the statistic) and test whether it predicts the re-simulation error d_t = e_t(K_default): Spearman rank correlation per task on contact steps, precision and recall of the flag g_t > tau for d_t > kappa, and the same for g_t scaled by the engine's own constraint-stiffness estimate (efc_D, the diagonal of the constraint-space inverse inertia, which strong convexity says converts a gradient norm into a state-error bound: ||x - x*|| <= ||grad f(x)|| / mu, mu the strong-convexity constant).
claim: The gradient norm the solver already computes at the cap, scaled by the engine's constraint-stiffness estimate, rank-correlates above 0.8 with the one-step re-simulation error, so the lane's per-step physics audit can be produced for free at training time without a second converged step, and exposing one number per world from Warp is the whole systems change.
trick: The solver stops when its own residual is small enough; read that residual out instead of throwing it away, and check whether it tells you how wrong each step was without ever running the expensive reference step.
why_now: MuJoCo Warp's Data exposes solver_niter and efc_force per world but not the gradient or improvement statistic (mujoco_warp/_src/types.py, read 2026-10-19), so the gap is one field in a young codebase; the lane's audit (d_t with a re-simulated reference) was specified in the 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-16 sessions and costs a second solve per step; the convergence-law candidate's rollouts make this test nearly free.

killing_experiment.design: Reuse the convergence-law candidate's 200k visited states; re-step each at K_default in CPU MuJoCo recording mjSolverStat after the capped iteration (or one extra zero-step evaluation if the recorded statistic precedes the update); compute Spearman(g_t, d_t) and Spearman(g_t * sqrt(efc_D-scaling), d_t) per task on contact steps; sweep tau for precision/recall against d_t > kappa.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Spearman(g_t, d_t) < 0.3 and the stiffness-scaled version < 0.5 on contact steps for every task: the solver's stopping statistic does not track the state error it is meant to bound, the free flag is dead, the audit keeps its re-simulated reference, and the finding becomes a footnote on the tolerance criterion itself (an informative negative).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Raw g_t predicts d_t within a task only up to a state-dependent factor spanning about two orders of magnitude (precision of a fixed tau below 0.5), because the same gradient means a different state error at different contact stiffness; the stiffness-scaled residual lifts rank correlation above 0.8 on contact steps; steps with g_t near zero and d_t above kappa are under 5% (the problem is convex, so a small gradient is a true certificate).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: A gradient tolerance (MuJoCo: 'the smaller of the cost improvement and the gradient norm' against tolerance=1e-8) is a sufficient convergence criterion for every state, and fidelity is a property of the setting, not of the step; GPUSimBench and the lane's own audit both assume a reference re-simulation is required to measure per-step error.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If raw g_t alone rank-correlates above 0.8, every engine can ship a per-step fidelity flag for free and the audit needs no reference solve; if neither version works, the Kalman import's observability concern stands (iteration-cap errors are not visible from what the engine reports) and the audit must keep its re-simulation; if only the scaled version works, the engine's tolerance criterion is mis-scaled across states and a stiffness-normalized tolerance is the recipe consequence.

identifiability: g_t and d_t are deterministic given (x_t, u_t, engine build, cap); the CPU re-step removes GPU-batch non-determinism, and the CPU-versus-MJX step difference is reported as a floor. No temperature enters: the visited-state distribution is fixed by the convergence-law candidate's rollouts with deterministic actions and stated as the conditioning set. The correlation is a property of the engine's solver at a state; kappa and tau are protocol choices with a sweep.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent to engine builders: the shippable artifact is a one-field change to Warp's Data plus a validation table, which an outside contributor can submit and which the engine team has not published. Solo is feasible at 6 GPU-hours on the convergence-law candidate's data. It depends on that candidate running first and inherits its kill (b): if e_t(K_default) is below kappa almost everywhere there is nothing to flag.

neighbors.limitation_quote: docs, Inverse dynamics: 'When the flag fwdinv in mjModel.opt.enableflags is on, the forward and inverse dynamics are automatically compared at the end of each time step, and the difference is recorded in mjData.solver_fwdinv. title: Cross the builder's effort with the player's effort on the released self-written harnesses
statement: In 2610.30499 the same model at the same reasoning effort both writes the harness and plays with it, so the +13.4 RHAE (Sol high 28.58 to xhigh 41.94) and +24.5 RHAE (Opus 5 high 15.43 to xhigh 39.95) gaps between conditions confound a better-written harness with a harder-thinking player; we take the three revision-2 harnesses of each Opus 5 condition from the released snapshots and play each at the other effort, filling the two off-diagonal cells of a builder-effort by player-effort 2x2 whose diagonal the paper already measured on the same 20 held-out games. Each cell is 3 harnesses x 20 games with the paper's per-game dollar ledger kept, so the builder main effect (does the xhigh-written harness win at both player efforts) and the player main effect (does xhigh play win with both harness sets) are read in RHAE and at matched dollars per game. Zero-dollar step first: from the released ledgers, regress held-out RHAE change on dollar-per-game change over the 54 revision transitions and report the spend-explained share of score change.
claim: On ARC-AGI-3, the harnesses a model wrote for itself at xhigh reasoning effort score no better than the ones it wrote at high effort once both are played at the same effort, so the condition ranking in harness self-improvement studies is the player's effort knob and not better harness design.
trick: Swap the effort knob between the model that wrote the harness and the model that plays with it, and see whether the higher score followed the writer or the player.
why_now: 2610.30499 (October 2026) released all 81 harness source snapshots with per-game dollar ledgers at a frozen 2026-09-13 price list and single held-out evaluations of every snapshot, so two of the four cells and the harness code exist for free; the vendor effort knob is an API parameter on both families, so the crossed cell is a one-line configuration change in the harness; 2607.12227 (July 2026) made matched feedback-and-inference budgets the standard for judging harness evolution and compared evolution against test-time scaling, but never crossed the effort of the model that writes with the effort of the model that plays.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 ($0, 1 day): from the released ledgers and scores, regress per-lineage held-out RHAE change $\Delta J$ on dollar-per-game change $\Delta C$ over the 54 revision transitions ($H_0 \to H_1$, $H_1 \to H_2$), where $J$ is the 20-game mean RHAE and $C$ the mean inference dollars per held-out game; report the slope and the share of variance in $\Delta J$ explained by $\Delta C$, and read each harness's configured sampling temperature from its source. Step 2 ($1,700 at an assumed $8 per game at high and $20 per game at xhigh, judgment from the card's $7.57 all-condition mean; step 1 reprices it from the per-condition ledgers; 4 days): take the three Opus 5 high $H_2$ harnesses and play each on the 20 held-out games at xhigh, and the three Opus 5 xhigh $H_2$ harnesses at high, changing only the effort parameter; with the paper's diagonal cells this gives the 2x2 with cell means $\bar{J}_{bp}$, builder effort $b \in \{\mathrm{high}, \mathrm{xhigh}\}$, player effort $p \in \{\mathrm{high}, \mathrm{xhigh}\}$. Builder main effect $\beta = \tfrac{1}{2}[(\bar{J}_{\mathrm{xhigh},\mathrm{high}} - \bar{J}_{\mathrm{high},\mathrm{high}}) + (\bar{J}_{\mathrm{xhigh},\mathrm{xhigh}} - \bar{J}_{\mathrm{high},\mathrm{xhigh}})]$; player main effect $\pi$ by the same form with the roles swapped; the diagonal gap is $\beta + \pi$ plus the interaction. Noise reference is the paper's one measured within-harness suite SD of 3.99 RHAE over 20 games, so a cell mean of 3 harnesses carries roughly $3.99/\sqrt{3} \approx 2.3$ RHAE of run noise plus harness-to-harness spread. Each cell is also a (RHAE, dollars per game) point, so the builder effect is read a second time at matched spend. If $\beta$ lands within 4 RHAE of the decision line, replicate the one decisive cell (high-built harnesses at xhigh, 60 games, about $1,200 more) before deciding. Sol family is the replication if the budget allows, not part of the kill.
killing_experiment.kills_if: The builder main effect $\beta$ is at least half of the player main effect $\pi$ (on Opus 5 at least 12 RHAE against the 24.5-point diagonal gap), with the xhigh-written harnesses ahead in both player cells by more than the 3-harness spread: then a harder-thinking builder writes a harness that transfers its advantage at fixed play effort, harness design carries the condition gap, and CL-W43-03 is refuted for self-written harnesses. That negative is itself the first builder-versus-player decomposition of a harness-optimization result and is citable as such, so both outcomes are informative.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.55: $|\beta| < 4$ RHAE (inside the single-evaluation noise floor) and $\pi$ carries at least 80% of the 24.5-point diagonal gap, so the high-built harnesses played at xhigh land near 40 RHAE and the xhigh-built harnesses played at high land near 15; and step 1 shows a positive $\Delta J$ on $\Delta C$ slope with the 9 cheaper-and-worse lineages on it. Conceded in advance: an xhigh-written harness can carry a larger internal action or call budget, which raises dollars at any play effort; the dollar-matched reading of the cell points is what separates that from play effort, and if the two readings disagree the record says so.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2610.30499 presents per-condition held-out means as the model-effort setting's capacity for 'autonomous harness adaptation' and frames the gap as 'a capability of general intelligence' (card, framing_stripped); its Sec. 8 concedes it 'cannot separate model capability, harness design and spending into independent effects'. The card's neighbor 2607.12227 reports harness evolution beating simple test-time scaling by 80% on ARC-AGI-3 games under matched budgets; Meta-Harness, HarnessCompass and RRSI report harness-design gains with the player's effort never varied.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If $\beta$ is within noise: every harness-optimization result owes a crossed-effort control, the harness adaptation gap $G_t$ should be measured at fixed play effort, ARC Prize and HAL harness comparisons report the player effort beside the harness, and the self-improvement conditions in 2610.30499 reorder by cost per game rather than by harness. If $\beta \geq \pi/2$: builder reasoning effort buys design that transfers across play efforts, the right research object is what the xhigh builder wrote differently (the released source lets the diff be read), and CL-W43-03 loses its self-written-harness branch while keeping the hand-written one that C-W43-11 tests.

identifiability: Random given the player model's sampling at the temperature each harness's source configures (read and reported per harness in step 1; a harness at temperature 0 has provider batch arithmetic as its only run noise, the CL-W43-J01 case) plus any harness-internal randomness; ARC-AGI-3 is deterministic given the action sequence in our records (C-W43-11: the replay reproduces scorecards), so held-out variance is the player's. 'high' and 'xhigh' are the vendor's protocol labels, ordered within one vendor and not comparable across vendors, so the design stays inside one family and the quantity $\beta$ is a property of (harness set, player model, effort pair) under that protocol, not of the harness alone. The noise floor is borrowed from one harness measured ten times (SD 3.99 suite, 18.78 per game) and is a stated assumption until the replicate cell measures it on these harnesses.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: public harness source and ledgers, API-only, about $1,700, no artifact or standing needed; the authors or any harness-optimization group could run the two crossed cells in a day, and the re-open test before spending is asking them whether crossed-effort runs exist. Solo delivers the Opus 2x2 and the ledger regression; a lab adds the Sol family, the 27 lineages' $H_0$ cells and a second benchmark (Terminal-Bench 2.1 via 2607.12227's setup). Written as a controlled measurement of a published result, not a harness recipe, so lane L1 positioning holds.

Who pays: ARC Prize (cost-per-task column beside harness entries), HAL, harness-optimization authors (Meta-Harness, HarnessOpt-Bench, HarnessCompass, RRSI) deciding whether to spend on the builder or on play-time effort.

title: Second run or second model: matched-run accumulation curves for multi-model coverage
statement: Re-read the paper's 265-root-cause by 48-cell response matrix (sec. 14, reported only as marginals) as a capture-recapture study: at a matched number of runs $k$, compare the union of the best model's $k$ runs against the union of one run each from the $k$ best models, for $k = 2$ from the matrix and $k = 1, \ldots, 4$ from new runs of three open models (Gemma-4-31B, GLM-5.1, Qwen 3.8 27B on mini-SWE-agent, the paper's OpenRouter runner, at a fixed stated temperature) scored as recall of the known root causes, falling back to 100 CyberGym Level-0 instances with their one known vulnerability each if the Conduit corpus is not released. Readouts: the run-accumulation curve $U_m(k) = |\bigcup_{r \le k} R_{m,r}|$ per model against the model-accumulation curve $U^{\times}(k) = |\bigcup_{m \le k} R_{m,1}|$ at equal $k$ and at equal dollars; the share of 'found by exactly one model' identities that a second run of another model recovers; and the Chao lower bound on undiscovered root causes $\hat S = S_{\mathrm{obs}} + f_1^2 / (2 f_2)$ from per-run singletons $f_1$ and doubletons $f_2$, which turns the reported '60.4% of the union' into a coverage of what is there.
claim: In agentic vulnerability scanning, re-running the best model recovers the union as fast as adding the next model does, so the coverage gained by combining models is a restart effect and 'found by exactly one model' at two runs per model is a run count, not a model property.
trick: Before buying a second model for coverage, run the first one again as many times and count whether the new findings come from the model being different or from the dice being rolled again.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-20, CAMLIS 2026) is the first multi-model scan with an open harness (DeepSec), two runs per cell and a per-finding record of which cells found it, so the matched comparison is computable from an existing table; CyberGym (2506.02548, 2025-06) supplies a public oracle set with one known vulnerability per instance for the replicated arm. The capture-recapture estimator itself is decades old; the enabling piece is the response matrix, and the flag is that nothing else is new.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, 2 days): obtain the per-identity cell record (sec. 14 'models: multiple' field; ask the authors if the corpus is not in the DeepSec release) and compute, for the best model, $U_{\mathrm{best}}(2)$ against $|R_{\mathrm{best},1} \cup R_{\mathrm{next},1}|$ and $|R_{\mathrm{best},2} \cup R_{\mathrm{next},2}|$ (two matched pairings, giving a spread), the same for the top five models, the per-run singleton and doubleton counts and the Chao bound. Step 1 (replicated arm): three open models at the engineered prompt A1, $k = 4$ runs each, on Conduit at the pinned commit scored as recall of the 265 known root causes by canonical mapping with an LLM matcher and a manual check of every unmatched report; if the corpus is unavailable, 100 CyberGym Level-0 instances per model and run (recall per instance is the paper's own transfer metric). Compute $U_m(k)$ for each model and $U^{\times}(k)$ over models at $k = 1 \ldots 3$ with all orderings, each with its bootstrap band over run subsets; report the comparison at matched run count and at matched dollars (per-run cost logged). Served locally on 2 H100s, about 30 whole-repo runs or 1,200 instance runs.
killing_experiment.kills_if: In both the matrix and the replicated arm, at $k = 2$ and $k = 3$ the model-accumulation union exceeds the best model's run-accumulation union by more than the bootstrap run-to-run band, and fewer than half of the 'found by exactly one model' identities are recovered by a further run of any other model: model diversity is real complementarity with a measured coverage premium, the paper's 'combining configurations for broader coverage' stands, and the result is the first number on that premium (citable either way).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.55: the best model's run-accumulation curve matches the model-accumulation curve within the run-to-run band for $k \le 3$, at least half of the 38 single-model identities are recovered by a further run of another model, and the Chao bound says the 48 runs found under 80% of the discoverable root causes, so the published 60.4% is coverage of a moving union.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper's abstract: 'the largest two-run configuration covers 60.4%, while 14.3% are found by exactly one model. No single configuration covers all observed findings' and 'These results support ... combining configurations for broader coverage'; the same paper reports run-to-run Jaccard of 0.35-0.83 and that an A0 yield 'can shift by a third between runs' (sec. 7) without connecting the two.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If restarts match models: coverage claims in agent benchmarks must report run-accumulation curves before stating complementarity, 'found by exactly one model' is retired as a statistic, and a security team's budget goes to repeated runs of one strong cheap model (GLM-5.3 at 121 findings per cell) rather than a model portfolio. If models beat restarts: the complementarity premium per dollar is measured for the first time, and the next question is which model pairs are complementary (an item-by-model interaction on the matrix).

identifiability: Random given: the repository at one pinned commit (static-analysis agents, no execution, so the environment is deterministic after the action and all run-to-run variance is the policy's sampling plus provider nondeterminism), one runner, one prompt arm and the model's served temperature, which the paper leaves unstated for the OpenRouter lane and this probe fixes and reports. The union over $k$ runs is a property of (model, runner, prompt, temperature, $k$); 'found by exactly one model' is a property of the protocol's $k$, which is the Gate 0 point. On Conduit, matching a new report to a known identity is an LLM-matcher step with a manual check and its disagreement rate is reported; on CyberGym the oracle is one known vulnerability per instance, a verifier not a judge. The Chao bound assumes findings are sampled with heterogeneous but run-independent catchability and is reported as a lower bound.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a re-analysis of a published table plus a replicated arm on public code with open models; no frontier lab owns this question. Solo covers step 0 and the open-model arm. The paper's authors hold the corpus and the 48 runs and can run step 0 in an afternoon; the re-open test is asking whether the per-identity cell record is released. Dropped operators: operator 1 (replace the self-judge with a fixed external judge) is the paper's own stated future work and a service; operator 2 (a forward predictor of harness sensitivity from a cheap baseline run) rests on four points and is the shape of C-W43-06, not re-proposed; this week's import import:2026-W43-S8xF1 covers the run-residual versus interaction decomposition for effort and is not duplicated here, since this probe matches run count against model count rather than fitting variance components.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card paper's abstract recommends 'combining configurations for broader coverage' and reports 14.3% single-model findings while its sec. 7 says a yield 'can shift by a third between runs'; CyberGym and BountyBench report per-agent recall and never a run-accumulation curve (card neighbors). Who pays: security teams deciding whether a scan budget buys models or runs; benchmark owners (CyberGym, BountyBench, ZeroDayBench) who report coverage per agent; harness builders (DeepSec, AgentFlow) whose multi-model designs rest on complementarity.

impact_ceiling.floor: A re-analysis note on one matrix: run-versus-model marginal coverage at matched $k = 2$ and the Chao bound on the 265; cited by the next multi-model scanning paper. Requires step 0 only. Judgment p 0.45.
impact_ceiling.middle: A replicated result with accumulation curves on open models and a reporting rule (run-accumulation curve before any complementarity claim) adopted by one security-agent benchmark. Requires step 1. Judgment p 0.35.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: A general ruler, the run-equivalent of model diversity, measured on two more agent domains (coding-agent union coverage on SWE-bench-style tasks, where pass@k across models is reported the same way), changing how ensembles are justified across agent evaluation. Requires two more domains, about 200 GPU-hours. Judgment p 0.15.

scorecard.relevance: HAL (Narayanan): direct, cost-controlled comparison and multi-run reliability. Narasimhan (tau-family): moderate, the union over runs is the complement of pass^k and the same run-variance question. Evaluators (CyberGym, BountyBench owners): direct. Industry: direct for security scanning spend. Jacob's edge: the capture-recapture statistics and the matched comparison are evaluable from his background; theoretical physics zero; computer engineering small (serving three open models).
scorecard.kill_probe: Step 0 on the matrix (zero dollars, 2 days) then three open models times four runs at A1 (about 80 GPU-hours, about $100, 7 days); dead if the model-accumulation union beats the best model's run-accumulation union beyond the run-to-run band at $k = 2, 3$ in both arms.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: From the card's fetched neighbors: CyberGym (2506.02548) scores per-agent proof-of-concept success over 1,507 vulnerabilities and gives no run-accumulation statistic in its abstract; ZeroDayBench (2603.02297) three frontier models, fixed harness, no runs-per-cell statement; BountyBench (2505.15216) 10 agents in dollars of finding; IRIS (2405.17238) and AgentFlow (2604.20801) are methods, not coverage measurements. Occupied by the card: the 60.4% and 14.3% marginals and the per-model Jaccard. The kill search must use the neighbors' words (ensemble, union coverage, complementary, pass@k across models, repeated runs, capture-recapture, species accumulation, unseen species) and quote the card paper's and CyberGym's limitation text; density is counted on the day of writing, not here.
scorecard.why_now: Card paper 2026-10-20 (open harness, two runs per cell, per-finding cell record); CyberGym 2025-06 (public oracle instances). The estimator is old; the flag is recorded.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement (a matched comparison and a ruler on a published table) with a recipe consequence (spend on runs or on models). It is not a new scanner, not an ensemble or routing method, not a benchmark, and not a variance-components fit.

neighbors_to_check_first: 2610.28802 sec. 14 and Table 9 — whether the per-identity cell record is in the DeepSec release and how the two-run union per model is defined; the matched pairing needs per-run sets
2506.02548 — CyberGym: whether any table reports recall over repeated runs or over agent unions; its Level-0 instances are the fallback oracle
2505.15216 — BountyBench: how ten agents' Detect coverage is aggregated and whether any union-over-agents figure exists
2603.02297 — ZeroDayBench: three frontier models on 22 vulnerabilities; whether coverage per model and overlap are reported
2604.20801 — AgentFlow: whether the multi-agent harness synthesis reports gains against repeated runs of the single-agent baseline
headline_test: The coverage gained by combining models in agent benchmarks is a restart effect: re-running one model recovers the union as fast as adding another.
claim_attachment_note: tests the restart clause of CL-W43-03 on a non-scaffold harness choice (which models to run); the claims stage detaches it to orphan if 'combining configurations' is read as outside scaffold design

title: Wrong repository's call graph as the placebo for pasted static-analysis context
statement: On the engineered prompt A1, add a placebo arm that pastes a CodeQL call-graph block of identical format and rendered length (about 2,415 tokens per batch) generated from a different TypeScript repository, beside the true CodeQL block and A1 alone, for three open models (Gemma-4-31B, GLM-5.1, Qwen 3.8 27B on mini-SWE-agent) at $k = 4$ runs per cell, scored as recall of the 265 known root causes (fallback: 100 CyberGym Level-0 instances). Log dose taken per batch (graph-query calls where the arm exposes a query tool; the card's Table 6 has GPT-5.5 at 144 calls in 38 of 38 batches with a context increment of $-6.5$ and Gemma at 9 calls in 3 of 32 batches with $+4.5$). Primary contrast: the placebo increment $\Delta_{\mathrm{pl}} = Y_{\mathrm{A1+pl}} - Y_{\mathrm{A1}}$ as a fraction of the true increment $\Delta_{\mathrm{cg}} = Y_{\mathrm{cpg}} - Y_{\mathrm{A1}}$, each with its four-run standard error, per model.
claim: A same-length call-graph block from the wrong repository changes a scanning agent's yield as much as the right one does, so the paper's targeted-context effect is the presence of an authoritative block in the prompt, not its content.
trick: Paste a confident-looking analysis of some other codebase into the agent's prompt and see whether its yield moves the same way it does with the real one.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-20) decomposed its headline and found the context increment negative for three of four models while naming a length-matched control and auditable tool use as future work (sec. 7, 10.2); its open harness renders the block from a deterministic CodeQL export, so a wrong-repository block is a one-line change; its Table 6 is the first per-batch record of dose taken next to a context effect, and the two models it reports are inverted (most reading, least gain).

killing_experiment.design: Three arms (A1; A1 plus true CodeQL block; A1 plus placebo block from another repository, shuffled so no batch sees its own files described) times three open models times $k = 4$ whole-repo runs on Conduit, each run scored as recall of known root causes by canonical mapping with a manual check of unmatched reports; fallback 100 CyberGym Level-0 instances per cell with the instance's oracle file and a placebo call graph from a different instance. Readouts per cell: yield with its four-run SE, dose taken where observable, and per-batch class of finding (the card says the block steers the class). Served locally on 2 H100s; 36 whole-repo runs or 3,600 instance runs.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Either (a) at $k = 4$ the true increment $\Delta_{\mathrm{cg}}$ is within two standard errors of zero for every model, so there is no context effect to attribute and the paper's 'for whom' ordering is run noise (citable: two runs per cell did not identify it); or (b) $\Delta_{\mathrm{cg}}$ clears two SE for at least two models and the placebo increment is under one third of it and within two SE of zero for each: content is the mechanism, the form hypothesis is dead, and the surviving result is that the agent uses the right call graph and ignores a wrong one.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.5 for the form result: the placebo reproduces at least half of the true increment for the two smaller models (both signs allowed; the card's increments are $+4.5$ for Gemma and $-29.5$ for GLM-5.1), and dose taken does not order the models by benefit; probability 0.35 that outcome (a) fires and nothing clears two SE at $k = 4$.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper: 'adding CodeQL context beyond that prompt improves yield only for the smallest model' (abstract), read as the content filling a capability gap; it rules out 'more tokens' from the untargeted context-gathering arm lowering yield (sec. 7) without a same-length irrelevant block. The wider assumption, shared with the semantic-layer paper behind C-W43-07, is that pasted context acts through what it says.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If form: every context-injection result in agent scanning owes a placebo-block arm, 'who needs context' is a prompt-form question answered by block presence not call-graph quality, and static-analysis integration is better served as a queryable tool than as pasted text. If content: the right block is read and the wrong one is ignored, which bounds the placebo-form claim to the semantic-layer domain and makes the paper's negative increments for frontier and mid-tier models a content-misdirection effect worth its own mechanism.

identifiability: Random given the pinned repository (deterministic after the action; static analysis, no execution) and each model's served temperature, fixed and reported here, unstated in the paper's OpenRouter lane. The increment is a property of (model, runner, prompt, block, temperature) under the stated protocol; the placebo content is shuffled across batches so the result is not a property of one wrong repository. Dose taken is observable only where the arm exposes a query tool, so for pasted-only arms the probe measures dose offered and says so; the matcher that maps reports to known identities is an LLM-judge step with a manual check and a reported disagreement rate.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a control arm on an open harness with open models; solo under 60 GPU-hours. The paper's authors own the corpus and the frontier-model arms, where the negative increments were reported; open models are a proxy and the record says so. This is the second probe, after C-W43-07 (placebo semantic layer for data agents), of the same latent headline that pasted context steers agents by form; it is written so the claims stage can lift the two into a claim, and it is not a duplicate of C-W43-07 (different domain, different scaffold, the paper's effect has the opposite sign for three of four models). Not duplicated: import:2026-W43-S8xF1 (variance components of effort by task) and C-W43-06 (habit predicts scaffold sign).

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card paper's sec. 7 and 10.2 name a length-matched control and auditable tool use across runners as future work, and its sec. 17 decomposition shows the context increment negative for three of four models; 2604.25149 (via C-W43-07) attributes a layer's gain to content. Who pays: teams integrating static analysis into scanning agents (DeepSec, IRIS-style pipelines), security benchmark owners deciding whether to ship context, and anyone evaluating a context-engineering claim without a placebo arm.

impact_ceiling.floor: A control-arm result on one harness and three open models saying how much of the context effect survives a wrong block, with the first four-run intervals on the paper's cells. Judgment p 0.5.
impact_ceiling.middle: With C-W43-07, a two-domain claim that pasted context steers agents by form, and a placebo-context arm becomes a standard control in context-engineering evaluations; requires both probes and one frontier model arm (about $500 of API). Judgment p 0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: Static-analysis integration moves from pasted text to queryable tools as a default in one public scanning harness, with the dose-taken log as the audit. Requires replication on the paper's own frontier arms. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: HAL and evaluators: the placebo-context control as a standard arm for scaffold and context claims. Narasimhan (tau-family): low, no simulated user. Industry: direct for security tooling vendors. Jacob's edge: the control-arm habit from physics; computer engineering small (serving models, generating the placebo export).
scorecard.kill_probe: Three arms times three open models times four runs (about 60 GPU-hours, about $100, 7 days); dead if nothing clears two SE at $k = 4$ or if the placebo moves yield by under a third of the true block while the true block clears two SE.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: From the card: the paper itself (untargeted context arm, no length-matched block), IRIS (2405.17238, the arrow reversed: LLM feeds CodeQL), AgentFlow (2604.20801, harness search with runtime signals). From C-W43-07's record: 2604.25149 (layer document helps three frontier models equally), 2601.07226 (contextual distractors degrade reasoning models), 2609.37153 (blind compliance with poisoned tool outputs). None in those records pastes a wrong-content analysis block into a scanning agent. title: Omission of irrecoverable state versus commission of unsourced bullets: which predicts the compaction penalty on the same boundaries
statement: On the TRACE corpus of AppWorld compaction boundaries (per C-W43-10's record: re-executable prefix state, committed summary, and continuations under full context and under the summary, so the per-boundary success penalty already exists), compute for every boundary two counts from the trace alone: (a) irrecoverable omissions, the values (ids, names, amounts) the full-context continuation uses after the boundary that appear in a pre-boundary observation, are absent from the summary, and cannot be re-fetched because the producing call was a one-shot output (a mutating call, a user turn) or because the agent never re-issued the read that would show them; and (b) unsourced entries, SJC's judge verdict on each summary bullet (the count CL-W43-05's probes use). Regress the paired penalty on both counts, and report the summary's retention rate for observed versus derived values (the card measured 38.5% versus 92% on its toy). The matched quantity is the boundary: both mechanisms are measured on the same compaction event and the same continuations.
claim: At a compaction boundary the success penalty tracks the count of later-needed values the summary dropped and no tool call re-fetched, not the count of unsourced entries it kept, and summaries drop observed values far more often than derived ones.
trick: For each compaction, count the facts the agent later needed that the summary dropped and nothing re-fetched, count the unsourced bullets it kept, and see which count predicts failure on the same boundaries.
why_now: Card 2610.26632 (October 2026) shows on a controlled toy that the recoverability label is the whole truncation effect (penalty 0 versus 92.5 points) and that model-written summaries retained derived facts in 92% of episodes but observed facts in 38.5%, and its own limitation says it claims nothing about real agents and dropped the state component for cost; SJC (2610.20927, 2026-10-14, per C-W43-08) supplies the unsourced-entry judge and the competing mechanism; the TRACE corpus is public and already mined by an outsider (2610.08722, 2026-10-06, per C-W43-10), so the paired penalties exist and only the two counts have to be computed.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 ($0, 2 days): load the TRACE boundaries; for each, parse pre-boundary observations into a value set, find values used by the full-context continuation after the boundary, mark each as re-fetched (an identical read call re-issued after the boundary in the summary continuation), re-fetchable-but-not (a read on unmutated state the agent never re-issued) or one-shot (produced by a mutating call or a user turn); compute irrecoverable omissions = one-shot plus re-fetchable-but-not values absent from the summary. Step 2 (~$60 API, 2 days): re-implement SJC's judge from its appendix prompt and score every bullet of every summary. Step 3 (1 day): per-boundary penalty $P_j = S^{\text{full}}_j - S^{\text{sum}}_j$ (success rates over the corpus's continuations) regressed on both counts with task fixed effects; partial correlations and a leave-one-count-out comparison; retention rates of observed versus derived values. Optional step 4 (~$300, 5 days): 40 new boundaries on a task family whose observations are one-shot (tau-bench user turns or ARC-AGI-3 frames) to test the cross-benchmark prediction that the omission count, and the penalty, rise when observations cannot be re-read.
killing_experiment.kills_if: The unsourced-entry count explains at least twice the penalty variance of the irrecoverable-omission count (partial $R^2$), or the omission count's coefficient is not distinguishable from zero at the corpus size while the unsourced count's is: then compaction fails by commission as CL-W43-05 says and this probe is a confirming footnote. A second kill: fewer than 90% of the boundaries' continuations reproduce (corpus parsing or app determinism fails), in which case the probe is parked with that trigger.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Irrecoverable omissions carry more of the penalty variance than unsourced entries (partial $R^2$ ratio above 1.5; judgment probability 0.55); the retention split replicates in direction, observed values retained under 60% and derived values above 85% (judgment 0.6); most omitted observed values were re-fetchable and the agent did not re-issue the read, matching 2609.20804's finding that recovery machinery is rarely used.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: SJC: the harmful content is what the summary asserts without support (83% of failed runs follow an entry; 22 of 29 failure-following entries unsourced), so the gate is a deletion judge; the card's paper calls its own omission penalty 'expected by construction' and confines it to a toy; 2609.29875 states reasoning becomes safe to forget once written into code, files or tool outputs, which is the recoverability idea applied to derived state only.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If omission dominates: CL-W43-05's mechanism is secondary and the fix is recoverability, not deletion: summarizers are told which observations cannot be re-observed (the card's asymmetry 1), harnesses keep an index of observed values, and every compaction paper reports an irrecoverable-omission count beside its length and provenance numbers. If commission dominates: CL-W43-05 stands with a matched-mechanism control behind it, and recoverability work (2609.20804's machinery, VISTA's lossless store) is confirmed as low-value for this task family.

identifiability: The penalty $P_j$ is random given (boundary state, summary) only through the agent's sampling at the corpus's temperature (confirm from the corpus metadata); AppWorld's apps are deterministic after the action, so there is no environment luck term. The omission count is a deterministic function of the trace plus one protocol choice, the value-matching rule (exact string match on ids, emails, amounts; a fuzzy rule is a robustness arm). The unsourced count carries the judge's answer flips (2.1% in SJC). Both counts are properties of the boundary, not of the protocol, once the matching rule is fixed and pre-registered.
positioning_note: Solo-feasible on a public corpus with API dollars; lab-adjacent to the TRACE/PAIR/SJC group, who built the corpus and could run this in a week ('they have the stack' is a guess; the re-open test is asking them whether any omission count exists in their unpublished analyses). Written as the omission-side test of CL-W43-05, which its probes C-W43-08/09/10 do not measure: 08 varies how much is deleted, 09 labels kept entries, 10 ablates kept entries; none counts what was dropped and could not be recovered. Shares SJC's re-implemented judge with C-W43-08/09 and the corpus with C-W43-10.

scorecard.target_value: In print: card 2610.26632's own limitation ('I claim nothing about real agents or tasks; the registered state component that would have used the recoverability label was dropped for cost'); PAIR (2609.36526, per C-W43-10's record) says degradation 'concentrates at isolated compression events' and stops above the entry level; 2609.20804 reports that recoverability machinery is rarely used and asks nothing about why. Who pays: compaction-paper authors who report a mechanism, harness teams choosing between a deletion judge and a recoverability index, and the corpus owners whose release this extends.

impact_ceiling.floor: A confirming footnote that unsourced entries predict the penalty better than omissions on AppWorld; requires steps 1-3; probability 0.35 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: Omission of irrecoverable state carries more of the penalty on one corpus and the observed-versus-derived retention bias replicates on real summaries; an omission count becomes a required column in compaction evaluations and CL-W43-05 is rewritten; requires steps 1-3; probability 0.45 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The cross-benchmark prediction holds (penalty rises where observations are one-shot), redirecting compaction work from deletion gates to recoverability and summarizer-side recoverability labels across two task families; requires step 4 plus one more task family (another ~$600); probability 0.2 (judgment).

None of these counts irrecoverable omissions against unsourced commissions on the same boundaries; the kill search does the 12-month count with the neighbours' words (recoverable, irreversible, re-observe, restore, omission, provenance, unsupported).

title: Re-price context management under prefix-cache billing: when does trimming cost more than keeping everything
statement: Write the per-turn billing identity for an agent whose context is either kept whole (prefix cached) or trimmed every turn (prefix broken) and re-price published context-management results with it: $$\frac{D^{\text{trim}}_t}{D^{\text{full}}_t} = \frac{s_t}{r + \delta_t}, \qquad s_t = \frac{n^{\text{trim}}_t}{n_t},\ \ \delta_t = \frac{\Delta_t}{n_t},$$ where $D_t$ is the input-token bill at turn $t$, $n_t$ the full-history context length in tokens, $n^{\text{trim}}_t$ the trimmed length, $\Delta_t$ the tokens appended since turn $t-1$, and $r$ the provider's cached-to-uncached input price ratio, under the assumptions that the full-history prefix is served from cache and the trimmed prefix is not (per-turn eviction moves the edit point every turn). Trimming saves money only when $s_t < r + \delta_t$; the card's own numbers ($s = 0.84$-$0.90$ tokens, $2.9$-$4.0\times$ dollars) satisfy the identity with $r + \delta \approx 0.22$-$0.30$. Grade with it, first analytically on released trajectories (longest-common-prefix token counts per turn under each policy) and then by temperature-0 replay on SGLang with prefix caching logging computed-prefill tokens and prefill time: full history, per-turn observation masking (the Complexity Trap policy), last-$N$ pruning, threshold summarization (Pi-style), and boundary-batched masking, on 50 SWE-bench Verified tasks with one open model, at three price ratios $r \in \{0.1, 0.25, 0.5\}$.
claim: Under prefix-cache pricing, per-turn context trimming on coding-agent trajectories costs more than full history until the trimmed context is smaller than the cache discount ratio times the full context, so the cost savings published for observation masking and sliding windows are token counts with the wrong sign at the lengths where they were reported.
trick: Evicting a turn moves the edit point of the prompt, so everything after it is re-prefilled at full price; count the tokens actually recomputed, not the tokens sent, and the saving reverses unless the trim removes more than the cache discount.
why_now: Card 2610.26632 (October 2026) measured the reversal in the wild: a 24k-token window sent 0.84-0.90x the tokens of full history and cost 2.9-4.0x the dollars because the cached share fell from 94% to 48%; AKV (2610.28577, October 2026, this week's L3 card) reports that a text-level trim 'costs 1.85x the full-context baseline' on 100 BrowseComp-Plus tasks and that KV-cache reads are 82.4% of API cost, while the Complexity Trap (2508.21433, 2025-08-29, abstract fetched) reports observation masking 'halves cost relative to the raw agent' and 2609.20804 (2026-09-17, abstract fetched) ranks five context-management strategies by efficiency across 176 settings; three papers in fourteen months give opposite signs for the same operation, and the identity says which pricing model each used. TokenPilot (2606.17016, June 2026) and SmoothAgent (2607.00151, July 2026) already engineer around the invalidation, so the systems side knows; the measurement lane's cost columns do not.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 ($0, 2 days): for each context-management paper that released trajectories (the Complexity Trap releases code and data per its abstract; check 2609.20804 and AKV), reconstruct per-turn prompts under the paper's own policy, compute $n_t$, $n^{\text{trim}}_t$ and the longest common token prefix with the previous turn's prompt, and re-price every reported cost column at $r \in \{0.1, 0.25, 0.5\}$ with and without a cached prefix; report the sign of the saving per paper per $r$. Step 2 (30 GPU-hours, ~$100, 4 days): replay 50 SWE-bench Verified trajectories per policy at temperature 0 with recorded tool responses (the protocol AKV's card describes) on SGLang with radix prefix caching, one ~20-30B open model (GPT-OSS-20B or MiroThinker-1.7-Mini, both in AKV's regime) on one 80 GB GPU, logging cache-hit tokens, computed-prefill tokens and prefill wall-clock per turn for five policies at a matched window budget; this measures the identity's two assumptions (full prefix cached; trimmed prefix missed) instead of assuming them. Step 3 (1 day): the break-even table, $s_t$ against $r + \delta_t$ per turn and per policy, and the fraction of turns on which trimming saves.
killing_experiment.kills_if: On SWE-bench-length trajectories, per-turn observation masking computes fewer prefill tokens than full history on a majority of turns at $r = 0.1$ and $r = 0.25$ (that is, $s_t < r + \delta_t$ holds: the trim removes enough that even uncached it is cheaper), and the re-priced published savings keep their sign at those ratios: then the token-count cost columns are right and the card's and AKV's reversals are artifacts of short windows. The negative is still a footnote: it bounds the window lengths at which cache invalidation matters.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Per-turn observation masking on SWE-bench trajectories leaves $s_t$ in 0.4-0.7 (observations are most of the tokens but not nine tenths), which exceeds $r + \delta_t$ at $r \le 0.25$, so masking costs 1.5-3x full history in computed prefill and in dollars, and the Complexity Trap's halving flips sign under cache pricing (judgment probability 0.6); threshold summarization is within 20% of full history because its prefix is stable between triggers; boundary-batched masking recovers most of the token saving at near-full cache hit. At $r = 0.5$ the sign depends on $\delta_t$ and roughly half the published savings survive.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The Complexity Trap abstract: observation masking 'halves cost relative to the raw agent'; 2609.20804 abstract: rule-based elision before summarization gives 'the strongest overall efficiency' across 176 settings; AKV's motivation (per its card) that text trimming costs 1.85x is stated on one model and one benchmark with no accuracy, and AKV's own 27.7% saving is API-equivalent arithmetic at a fixed price ratio (hit = half of miss), so even the systems paper that knows the mechanism did not report the break-even.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the reversal holds: every context-management paper reports computed-prefill tokens or dollars under a stated $r$, not tokens sent (a ruler change for L1/L4 evaluations), harness defaults move from per-turn masking to boundary-batched eviction or threshold summarization, and the AKV-style server-side drop has a quantified text-level competitor (batched masking) to beat. If it fails: cache invalidation is a short-window problem, the published savings stand, and the card's 2.9-4.0x is a 24k-window artifact.

identifiability: For a fixed trajectory text and a fixed cache policy, computed-prefill tokens are a deterministic function (longest common prefix per turn plus radix-tree eviction state), so the step-1 and step-2 numbers have no sampling randomness; the trajectory itself is random given the agent's sampling, and replaying recorded trajectories (AKV's protocol) holds it fixed, which also means the policy's effect on behaviour is not measured here and is not claimed. The dollar figure is a property of the protocol (the provider's $r$ and whether the prefix is cached across turns), which is the point: the claim is about the pricing model, and $r$ is reported as a parameter, never assumed. Temperature is irrelevant to the cost count; it enters only through which trajectories exist.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent in the systems register: measurement of published artifacts plus a napkin identity, with GPU-side verification a solo first-year can run on one node. Not head-to-head with AKV/TokenPilot/SmoothAgent, who build fixes; this grades the measurement lane's cost columns that motivate them and names the text-level policy (boundary-batched eviction) that closes most of the gap without a server fork. Jacob's edge applies: the identity is prefill arithmetic and the measurement is cache-hit accounting on a GPU server. A lab position adds provider-side cache-hit logs; solo is sufficient with an open-weight server.

Who pays: every harness team choosing a context-management default on a cache-priced API, every paper reporting an agent cost column, and the systems groups (AKV, TokenPilot, SmoothAgent) whose motivation this quantifies.

title: Omitted, never fetched, or overridden: a judge-free stage split of post-compaction failures
statement: On a public corpus of AppWorld trajectories with harness-triggered compaction boundaries (the record of C-W43-10 names TRACE's 590 re-executable boundaries with committed summaries; if that corpus lacks full trajectories, the Prompting arm of C-W43-08, 168 tasks x 3 runs, supplies them), take every failed task with at least one boundary and extract its needed values: the argument values of the task's reference solution's state-changing API calls that the agent's post-compaction state-changing calls got wrong or never made. Label each needed value by exact normalized match against two sets built from the logs with no judge, $P$ (every value in any environment output the agent received over the whole trajectory) and $S$ (every value in the post-compaction context: the summary plus tool results after the boundary and before the divergent action), and label the wrong value the agent emitted as unsourced if no environment output ever contained it. The three cells and the unsourced share are the card's build / exposure / closure decomposition moved from a retrieval index to the agent's own summary, computable because AppWorld is deterministic after the action and the facts a correct action needs are literal values.
claim: In post-compaction failures the fact the correct action needed was still in the agent's view or was never fetched at all in at least two thirds of cases, and the value the agent acted on instead came from no environment output in at least 40% of cases, so compaction fails by unsourced persistence and never-fetched facts, not by the summary dropping facts the environment had produced.
trick: Replay the logs to list every value the environment ever printed and every value that survived into the summary, then check for each failed task whether the needed value was dropped, never fetched, or still in view and overridden by a value nobody printed.
why_now: The card's paper (2610.26836, 2026-W43) shows the three-stage label is exact without a judge whenever the tool is deterministic and the needed fact is a literal value, and states in its own text that the same question for compaction summaries 'has no such oracle'. AppWorld is deterministic after the action (C-W43-09's record) and its needed facts are IDs, amounts, dates and addresses that match literally. C-W43-10's record names a public corpus of 590 re-executable compaction boundaries, so the data exists without a new run. CL-W43-05 (opened 2026-10-20) has three probes, all interventions or counterfactual replays; none reads the existing logs for the cell the headline's noun names.

killing_experiment.design: Parse every failed trajectory with a boundary in the corpus; build $P$ and $S$ per trajectory by exact normalized matching (lowercase, whitespace stripped, numbers in canonical form, dates in ISO) with a pre-registered exclusion list of high-base-rate values (0, 1, booleans, empty strings, single common words) whose count is reported; needed values come from the benchmark's reference solution program, or, if none ships, from the state-changing calls of a successful run of the same task in the same corpus. Report $\pi_{\mathrm{build}} = \Pr[v^\star \notin P]$, $\pi_{\mathrm{exp}} = \Pr[v^\star \in P \setminus S]$, $\pi_{\mathrm{clo}} = \Pr[v^\star \in S]$ over classified needed values $v^\star$ (they sum to one), the unsourced share $\upsilon = \Pr[w \notin P]$ over emitted wrong values $w$, the unclassified count, and task-level bootstrap intervals (1,000 resamples). Audit 50 automatic labels by two annotators as the card's paper did on 58 trajectories and report agreement. If the Prompting arm must be re-run, it is the same arm C-W43-08 needs and the cost is shared.
killing_experiment.kills_if: $\pi_{\mathrm{exp}} \geq 0.5$ with the interval's lower end above 0.4: the summary dropped a fact the environment had produced in most failures, compaction fails by omission, and the noun in CL-W43-05 is wrong; that result is itself citable because it says the length knob and re-fetch policies are the lever and provenance gating works on the minority cell. Protocol kill: more than 25% of needed values unclassifiable (ambiguous matches or multiple valid solution forms), in which case the oracle does not transfer from a scalar-matching simulator to AppWorld at this cost and the probe is parked with that trigger. If the Prompting arm is re-run instead, the dollar figure rises to about 300 (C-W43-08's per-arm estimate).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Build 35-50% (the needed fact was never fetched, before or after the boundary), closure 25-45% (the fact was in the summary or a later tool result and the agent acted on something else), exposure 15-30% (the summary dropped it); among closure-and-build failures the emitted wrong value is unsourced in at least 60% of cases. Judgment probability that $\pi_{\mathrm{exp}} < 1/3$: 0.6. Conceded in advance: the card's paper found 15 of 24 item-level losses were build failures that churn between runs, so build is likely to be the largest cell here too, which would re-scope the claim rather than confirm it.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: ACON (2510.00615) rewrites compression guidelines 'from analyses of the agent's failures', treating post-compaction failures as compression losses to be repaired by keeping more of the right content; The Complexity Trap (2508.21433) frames context management as a trade of observations for cost, where dropping old observations costs nothing measurable; CL-W43-05's own headline asserts persistence over length without a judge-free count; the card's paper states the compaction version of the exposure/closure question 'has no such oracle'.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If exposure dominates: compaction recipes should keep or re-fetch raw observations (masking plus retrieval), and the provenance-gate thread (C-W43-08, C-W43-09) is optimizing the minority cell. If closure with unsourced values dominates: summary length is the wrong lever, per-entry provenance typing (C-W43-09) is the right one, and every compaction paper owes a three-cell table in place of an LLM-annotated failure taxonomy. If build dominates: compaction is a minority cause of post-compaction failure and the lane's claim is re-scoped to say so, which is also news for a lane whose papers attribute post-compaction failures to the summary.

identifiability: The labels are deterministic functions of the logs, the matcher and the reference solution: no sampling, no judge, no temperature. The randomness is in which trajectories failed (the agent's and compressor's sampling at the provider default) and is handled by task-level bootstrap intervals; the cell shares are properties of the (agent, compressor, benchmark) triple and are reported as such, not as properties of compaction in general until a second environment agrees. Protocol dependence is in three fixed choices: the normalization rules, the exclusion list, and the definition of needed values from the reference solution; all three are written before labelling and the unclassified count is reported, so a reader can see how much of the result the protocol decided. A value present in $S$ for a different entity (the card's paper's 'matching number printed for a different reaction step') is the known failure of the matcher and is what the 50-label audit measures.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a judge-free ruler run on public logs, API cost near zero. A product team with its own compaction logs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenHands) can run the same three cells in a day and has the larger corpus, which is both the risk and the adoption surface; the solo contribution is the ruler's definition, the first public table, and the standard the lane's papers would then owe. Lane L4 permits measurement register only; this is measurement with a lever consequence and no new compressor.

scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement of shipped compaction behaviour by executable labels, with a lever consequence (length and re-fetch versus provenance gating). Not a compressor, not a judge, not a memory system, not a training method, and not the card's method on a new benchmark: the object measured is the agent's own self-message, which the card's paper says it cannot grade.

neighbors.title: Prune the Summary, Not the History: Source-Judged Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents (SJC)
neighbors.trick: After the compressor writes a summary, ask a non-generative decision model whether each entry has a source in the environment outputs or the previous summary, and delete the entries that do not.
neighbors.difference: Its failure analysis already does two of the candidate's three cells on natural AppWorld failures (OpenClaw compressor, GPT-5.6 Luna, 90 training tasks x 3 runs): 29 of 35 analyzed failed runs carry out a summary entry, 22 of those entries are supported by no environment output and 3 contradict one, so the candidate's unsourced share (claim: at least 40%) is already in print at about 71% of analyzed failures. The labels are LLM annotations (support kappa 0.86, pattern kappa 0.80) with every quoted entry 'verified by script against the logs'; the 6 of 35 failures that follow no entry are not split into never-fetched versus dropped, and no judge-free label exists. The candidate adds the executable label and the build/exposure split, nothing else.
neighbors.limitation_quote: SJC filters by provenance, not correctness, and the two are largely independent: supported and unsupported entries are correct at similar rates (92.2% against 90.6%; Appendix G). [...] Finally, the failure analysis in Section 3 relies on annotations produced by LLM annotators under a written protocol. (Sec. Limitations.) Protocol, App. D: 'All 44 failed runs of the Prompting baseline on the training split were traced by LLM annotators following a fixed written protocol. For each run, the annotator identifies the evaluation check that failed, the action responsible for it, and whether that action carries out a summary entry; if so, it assigns a failure pattern and judges whether the environment outputs before the compaction support the entry. [...] Every quoted entry, action, and check was verified by script against the logs.'

neighbors.title: Towards Reliable Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents (TRACE), its frozen 590-boundary cohort and causal annotation; Does an Agent's History Tell You When Compaction Will Hurt? (the outsider paper on the same corpus)
neighbors.trick: Rebuild the AppWorld state at each real compaction boundary twice, continue once with raw history and once with the summary, and score the summary by how many of the next actions error or repeat an earlier call; a side annotation treats a summary defect as causal only when the state existed pre-compaction, the summary lost or corrupted it, a later action used the corrupted state and that use entered a failed requirement.
neighbors.difference: The corpus does not carry what the probe needs: the repository's own words are 'data/ ships the derived boundaries and rollouts, not these source trajectories' (docs/COLLECTION.md) and 2610.08722 App. A lists what is released: 'Sorted sets of prior calls and functions, prefix step count, compaction index, task identifier and difficulty, and the last three observations, but not the ordered action sequence, token counts, compression ratio or summary text'. So neither the summary set S nor the produced set P is computable from the release, and the $50 arm of the probe does not exist. The corpus's own human annotation (data/causal_annotation, 14 failure trajectories, 46 compactions, W4096) already splits defects by mechanism (token_rewrite, collection_to_prose_or_count, call_signature_corruption, live_state_not_addressable, false_execution_model_lesson) and effect (LATENT 7, EXECUTION_TAX 4, STATE_CORRUPTION 2) and finds 'No trajectory in W4096 is caused by compression alone' (12 POLICY, 2 HYBRID): a small-n human version of the candidate's build-dominates expectation. Candidate differs by executable labels and n, not by question.

neighbors.limitation_quote: 2610.08722, Sec. 5: 'One agent model, one compressor and one window (4,096 tokens, deliberately tight); harness-triggered boundaries on AppWorld only [...] coarse released observables; [...] no data redistribution (the source carries no licence file)—we cite the release'; and 'corpora should ship ordered actions, token counts, summary text and more replays.' neighbors.title: Reclaim Evaluation: A Lossy Memory Is Worse Than an Empty One
neighbors.trick: Plant a known wrong conclusion, compress at a fixed budget keeping either the answer or the work behind it, deliver a correction, and score exact recovery without a judge; a memory that kept the stale value and dropped its source makes the model re-emit the stale value where an empty memory abstains.
neighbors.difference: Judge-free exact-match scoring of a compaction's unsourced-persistence failure, replicated on tau-bench by database-state hash, but on induced drift with the source present by construction; it names the naturalistic agent-log case as untested and says a judge would be needed there. The candidate is that case with a judge-free label.
neighbors.limitation_quote: Sec. 10 Ecological validity: 'Arithmetic and constraint-logic trajectories are the regime where the answer-determining source is compact, identifiable, and mechanically checkable, which is exactly what buys the judge-free exact-match scoring the paper rests on; a naturalistic corpus would reintroduce the judge model we deliberately avoid. [...] What stays untested is a genuine long-running assistant or agent memory in the wild, where identifying the re-derivation basis at write time is itself the hard, unfiltered problem; the locating study is a first probe of it, not a deployment census.'

neighbors.title: AI Guardrail Survival under Single-Cycle Agentic Self-Summarization
neighbors.trick: Compact once with a planted safety rule in context, then check whether the rule is dropped, degraded to a residue, or intact, and replay behaviour to see whether each state still prevents the prohibited action; textual presence is not a safety check because residues and even intact rules fail to fire.
neighbors.difference: A dropped / degraded / present-but-not-acted-on split (the exposure and closure cells) measured by behavioural replay for one planted fact type on synthetic sessions; the candidate labels natural failures and adds the never-fetched cell.

neighbors.title: Governance Decay: How Context Compaction Silently Erases Safety Constraints in Long-Horizon LLM Agents
neighbors.trick: Place a governance constraint in context, compact, grade tool calls deterministically, and split episodes by whether the constraint survived the summary: violation is 0% when it survives and 38% when it is dropped.
neighbors.difference: A judge-free exposure split (fact kept vs dropped) with deterministic tool-call grading, for an injected constraint on 1,323 synthetic episodes; no natural failures, no never-fetched or unsourced cell.

neighbors.title: What Does Context Compression Cost an Agent? Interaction Costs Unrevealed by Task-Completion Metrics
neighbors.trick: In a deterministic planning environment, vary compression severity and restore dropped state by oracle intervention, then count retrieval calls separately from execution calls to show compression's cost is re-acquisition of dropped state, not completion.
neighbors.difference: Interventional and judge-free; measures the re-fetch cost of the exposure cell and separates state quantity, type and validity, but never labels a natural failure by which cell it fell in.
