kill_search.summary: Two papers sit closest. Source-Judged Compaction (2610.20927, 2026-10-14; trick: a decision model scores each summary entry for having a source in the environment outputs and deletes the unsourced ones) already traced every failed run of the same OpenClaw compressor on AppWorld: 29 of 35 analyzed failures carry out a summary entry, 22 of those entries are supported by no environment output and 3 contradict one, with LLM annotators at kappa 0.86 and 'every quoted entry, action, and check [...] verified by script against the logs'; its limitation section says 'the failure analysis in Section 3 relies on annotations produced by LLM annotators under a written protocol.' TRACE (2608.06503, with its public cohort; trick: rebuild the AppWorld state at each real compaction boundary and continue once with raw history and once with the summary, scoring the next actions' errors and repeats) ships a human causal annotation on 14 failure trajectories that finds 'No trajectory in W4096 is caused by compression alone', and its outsider paper 2610.08722 records that the release exposes 'the last three observations, but not the ordered action sequence, token counts, compression ratio or summary text', while the repository says 'data/ ships the derived boundaries and rollouts, not these source trajectories.' Reclaim Evaluation (2606.25449; trick: plant a wrong conclusion, compress keeping the answer or its source, score exact recovery judge-free) names the gap in its own words: 'a naturalistic corpus would reintroduce the judge model we deliberately avoid.' One-line difference: the candidate labels natural failures with executable set membership and adds the never-fetched and dropped cells; the unsourced share it predicts is already published by LLM annotation, and the $50 TRACE arm does not exist because the corpus carries no summaries or full trajectories, so the probe is the $300 re-run of SJC's Prompting arm, shared with C-W43-08.
incumbents: TRACE repository docs/DATA.md: rollouts.jsonl holds 4,641 post-boundary rollouts with 'every executed action, its signatures, the real observation (4000-char cap)'; boundaries.jsonl holds metadata and four identity hashes; causal_annotation/ holds 14 trajectories, 46 compactions, mechanisms token_rewrite, collection_to_prose_or_count, call_signature_corruption, live_state_not_addressable, false_execution_model_lesson; effects LATENT 7, EXECUTION_TAX 4, STATE_CORRUPTION 2; 'pure_compression_caused: 0'. README: 'This repository does not yet carry a license file'.

SJC repository (GuanghuiMin/sjc): runners write <run>/trajectories/<task_id>.json 'with the steps and the compaction events', each compaction event holding 'the summary the agent saw'; the harness is ACON's agent with a patch; no run logs listed as shipped.
2610.26836 sec. 2.3 / App. C: the produced-corpus / seen-corpus / matcher oracle, 52 of 58 trajectories confirmed by hand audit.

redteam.protocol: three attacker personas (systems, theory, professor + checklist) as parallel agents; a separate defender agent answered every objection in writing before conceding; the operator graded

objections.objection: No matched uncompressed control: the claim concludes 'compaction fails by X' from a census of post-compaction failures, but in the same harness the No-compression arm fails 15.9% of runs (acc 84.1%) against Prompting's 23.2% (acc 76.8%), so under nesting about two thirds of the Prompting arm's failures are failures the agent has with no summary at all, and TRACE's annotators found none of 14 compression-caused. The three cells must be differenced against the No-compression arm's failures (where exposure is zero by construction and the cells reduce to build versus closure); without that arm the census measures the agent's baseline failure anatomy, and the 'build dominates' outcome the record half-expects says nothing about compaction. The control costs a second arm of 441 runs at roughly the same token count.
objections.answer: conceded: the arithmetic is verified from SJC Table 3 (GPT-5.6 Luna, 168 tasks x 3 runs): $504 \times 0.232 = 116.9$ Prompting failures against $504 \times 0.159 = 80.1$ No-compression failures, an excess of $36.8$, which is $31.5\%$ of post-compaction failures (easy 44%, medium 34%, hard 30%); TRACE's protocol_summary.json records 'POLICY 11, HYBRID 1' on 12 trajectories and w4096.json 'pure_compression_caused: 0', and its byhand_infoloss_reaudit retained 0 of 3 presence-based INFO-LOSS labels. Two things in the objection are wrong and I state them before conceding the rest. First, the kill clause is satisfiable: $\pi_{\mathrm{exp}}$ is a census share over failed runs with a boundary, and nothing in the base-rate arithmetic prevents a dropped needed value from co-occurring with a failure the agent has anyway, so '$\pi_{\mathrm{exp}} \geq 0.5$' is a well-defined event with a real probability under the pre-registered protocol. Second, 'nesting' (that the 80 base failures are a subset of the 117) is an assumption, not a measurement: runs differ only by sampling (SJC App. F), so the difference in failure counts is the net excess, not the identity of the excess runs. What I concede is the inference: the three cells are presence labels conditional on failure, and the claim's 'so compaction fails by unsourced persistence and never-fetched facts' is a statement about what compaction does, which a census without the uncompressed arm cannot carry; a perfect compressor ($S \supseteq P_{\mathrm{pre}}$) and a compressor that causes nothing both yield the record's 'confirming' cells. The compelled correction is the one all four objections name: run the No-compression arm (SJC harness, no `--method`, same 441 runs) and report the cells as a difference in composition between the two arms' failures, with exposure defined only on the compacted arm. The claim and the pre-registered kill stay as written; the control is in the narrowest surviving version.
objections.merged: theory #1 (compaction-attributable failures at most 31.5%, kill unsatisfiable on a causal reading), theory #2 (presence statistic vs causal verb; perfect compressor and null compressor both confirm), professor #3 (no control arm; TRACE retracted presence labels; cells attribute POLICY failures to compaction) merged here: one objection, one answer.

objections.objection: The scalar-matching oracle does not cover the failures it is meant to label: on the only natural-failure corpus in print (SJC's 35 adjudicated Prompting failures, AppWorld train split), 19 of 35 (54%) come from scenarios whose failing action's needed value is a composed or task-given value that no environment output ever prints (29caf6f: a comma-joined movie-title subset, 9 failures; 6104387: CSV file content and a path from the instruction, 3; 60d0b5b: a payment description, 1; 76f2c72 and d0b1f43: summed totals as the answer, 6), so exact matching labels $v^\star \notin P$ ('build') and $w \notin P$ ('unsourced') by construction and the record's pre-registered protocol kill (>25% unclassifiable) fires before any run — while the record's unclassified count, which covers only 'ambiguous matches or multiple valid solution forms', would not even detect it. Over all 147 train+dev reference solutions, 23.3% of the 1,984 classifiable state-changing argument values are composed text (destination_file_path, message, content, description) and 2.4% appear only in the instruction; 29 of 103 tasks with state-changing calls have at least one such value.
objections.answer: conceded: I re-read the attackers' script (rt_scripts/oracle_coverage.py) and outputs (rt_fetch/oracle_coverage_v2.txt, oracle_sjc_scenarios.txt) against the decrypted AppWorld bundle: the classification is sound (auth tokens excluded, 1,409 of 3,536; high-base-rate values excluded, 143; the remaining 1,984 values split env_literal 1,472 / composed_text 463 / task_given 47 / composed numeric 2), the pooled composed-or-task-given share is $(463+47)/1984 = 25.7\%$, and the SJC-scenario join is correct: 29caf6f's needed message is 'Fight Club, The Social Network' (composed from titles the environment printed separately), 6104387's content is a CSV body plus a path from the instruction, d0b1f43's and 76f2c72's needed value is a sum the environment never prints. One correction to the objection: a composed value the agent's own code prints (a sum, a joined string) is in $P$ under the record's definition, because AppWorld's observation is the stdout of the agent's cell, exactly as the card's paper counts the agent's own simulator output as produced; so 'by construction' is too strong for correct runs. It is not too strong for failed runs, where the correct composite was never computed, and that is what the probe labels. The decisive point stands: under the pre-registered matcher a composed needed value is silently labelled build, the record's unclassified count does not catch it, and once the category is added (it must be) the protocol kill's threshold is met at the value level (25.7%) and exceeded at the failure level on the only published failure set ($19/35 = 54\%$). The probe as written parks on its own protocol kill. What survives is an atomic matcher: composed values are decomposed into their constituents (titles, addends, path segments), each constituent is matched as a typed value, and the composite is labelled by its constituents; theory #3's point that SJC's unsupported mass sits in plans (Open TODOs 67.7%, Pending user asks 86.1%) while exact identifiers are 3.4% unsupported is the same fact seen from the summary side and is conceded with it.
objections.merged: theory #3 (estimator does not estimate the claim's noun; 20 of 35 failures have no literal needed value; protocol kill fires on Table 11) merged here.

objections.persona: checklist:2026-10-20 zero-cost probe runs its first step; theory
objections.objection: Applying the candidate's own labelling rule (the wrong literal value the agent acted on has no source in any environment output) to SJC's published failure table for the same compressor and benchmark gives $3/35 = 8.6\%$ (the three 'contradicted state' runs; upper bound $9/35 = 26\%$ if every 'other' run also counts), against the claim's pre-registered 'at least 40%'; the published table fires the kill before any log is parsed. SJC's Table 2 says why: literal values ('Exact identifiers', 14,444 entries) are 3.4% unsupported, while the unsupported mass sits in Open TODOs (67.7%) and Pending user asks (86.1%), which are plans, and a value matcher has nothing to match in a plan.
objections.answer:
conceded: Table 11 (re-read in 2610.20927.txt lines 1768-1800) totals RC 15, ID 5, CS 3, Other 6, Unrelated 6, support Unsupported 22 / Contradicted 3 / Supported 4. Walking the patterns with the record's rule: the 6 non-29caf6f rewritten-constraint runs act on the wrong ids (transactions, requests, songs) that the environment printed, so $w \in P$; the 5 invented deliverables emit an environment-returned id (complete_task(answer=8217)), so $w \in P$ and no $v^\star$ exists; the 3 contradicted-state runs emit a value no output contained ('Jennifer Powell: \$531.00'), $w 
otin P$. That gives $3/35 = 8.6\%$ as a floor and $9/35 = 25.7\%$ with every 'other' run counted. The theory reviewer's companion point is what settles it: the 9 runs of 29caf6f emit a comma-joined string that no output printed, so under whole-string matching they are 'unsourced' ($12/35 = 34\%$; $18/35 = 51\%$ with 'other'), and under atomic matching they are sourced. Two attackers derive 8.6% and 51% from the same protocol, which proves the record's quantifier is set by a normalization rule the record never wrote. Under the atomic reading, which is the only one on which 'came from no environment output' means what the claim says, the published table puts the share at 9-26%, under the claim's 40%. I also concede theory #5's structural point: $\upsilon = \Pr[w 
otin P]$ has no membership test on the summary, so a value invented after the boundary counts as persistence, and in the build cell $w 
otin P$ is near-certain, so $\upsilon \geq 0.4$ is close to entailed by the record's own expected build share of 35-50%. The quantity CL-W43-05 names is $\Pr[w \in M \wedge w 
otin P]$ with $M$ the summary text, reported with build-cell runs excluded. That is a different estimator from the candidate's and belongs to the narrowest surviving version, not to this claim.
objections.merged: theory #5 (upsilon is not persistence; no summary-membership test; build cell entails w not in P; 40% line set by normalization) merged here.

objections.objection: The Prompting-arm fallback has no needed-value oracle on the corpus the record names: AppWorld withholds solutions for test_normal (the 168-task split SJC's main table and C-W43-08's arm use), so 'the argument values of the task's reference solution's state-changing API calls' are undefined there, and the record's second fallback (a successful run of the same task) does not exist for the tasks that fail in every run, which in SJC's own corpus supplied 18 of 44 failed runs (29caf6f 9 of 9 and b0a8eae 9 of 9). Only train and dev (90 + 57 tasks) ship ground_truth/api_calls.json; the arm has to be re-pointed there, where SJC's failure analysis and TRACE's 147-task corpus already live, and the record's 168 x 3 run count, failure count and cost are for the wrong split.
objections.answer: The fact is verified on the decrypted bundle: tasks/3d9a636_1/ground_truth (test_normal) has no api_calls.json or solution.py; tasks/82e2fac_1/ground_truth (train) has both; the AppWorld README states 'only evaluation programs for test_normal and test_challenge'. The consequence is a re-pointing, not a kill: the probe's primary oracle is the reference solution, and the record names the 168-task arm only as a source of trajectories if TRACE's corpus lacks them. On train+dev (147 tasks, 441 runs) every task carries api_calls.json, so the sibling-run fallback is never needed and the all-runs-fail problem (18 of 44 in SJC) disappears; this is the split where SJC's own failure analysis (90 train tasks) and TRACE's corpus (147 tasks) live, so the comparison with both incumbents becomes same-split. Cost falls, not rises: $441 \times 112.8\mathrm{K} = 49.7\mathrm{M}$ tokens against 56.9M for test-normal. The record's run count and cost line are corrected accordingly; nothing in the claim or the kill changes.

objections.objection: The lab-position verdict and the Gate 3 adoption surface are false as written: on an owned compaction log (Claude Code, Codex, OpenHands) there is no reference solution and no guaranteed successful sibling run, so the needed-value set $\{v^\star\}$ is undefined and the three cells cannot be computed 'in a day' or on 'any deterministic-environment log a harness team already stores'; the ruler runs only on a benchmark that ships solutions (AppWorld train/dev, 147 tasks), which is the opposite of the claimed transfer to production logs.
objections.answer: conceded: the record's own definition of $v^\star$ requires a reference program or a successful sibling, and production logs carry neither; the lab verdict 'the three cells are a day's audit' and the scorecard line 'computable on any deterministic-environment log a harness team already stores' are false for the needed-value cells. What transfers to an owned log is the emitted-value label alone: whether the value the agent acted on after a boundary appears in any tool output it received, and whether it appears in the summary, needs no reference and is what SJC's gate already computes per entry. So the adoption surface is clause 2 (once its estimator is corrected, see the unsourced-share entry), not the three-cell split; the lab verdict is rewritten to say that.

objections.persona: checklist:shuffled control / placebo for a privileged signal
objections.objection: Exact normalized matching of untyped scalars makes $v^\star \in P$ true by chance for a third of needed values: 34.6% of the 1,984 classifiable state-changing argument values in the train+dev reference solutions are integers of at most three digits (song, playlist, transaction and contact ids such as 5, 16, 231) and another 11.1% are four-digit integers; over a 20-50 step AppWorld trajectory whose outputs are JSON lists of ids, counts, page sizes and amounts, some output contains any given small integer with probability near one, so the build cell is deflated and the exposure/closure split for those values is noise. The record's exclusion list (0, 1, booleans, empty strings, single words) does not reach this, and no shuffled-$S$ control (the summary of a different trajectory, or a wrong task's $P$) is pre-registered to measure the chance membership rate; the card's own paper reports 5 of 6 matcher disagreements were 'a matching number printed for a different reaction step'.
objections.answer: The value-shape counts are verified (rt_fetch/oracle_value_shapes.txt: int<=3 digits 687 = 34.6%, int 4 digits 221 = 11.1%). The remedy is inside the record's protocol, which fixes the normalization rules 'before labelling' without stating them: match typed pairs, not bare strings. AppWorld responses and reference calls are JSON with field names, so the needed value is $(\texttt{field}, v^\star)$ (for example (transaction_id, 8246), (song_id, 16)) and membership in $P$ or $S$ requires the same field, or for the summary the same section and entity line of OpenClaw's structured 'Exact identifiers' entries. A bare 16 in a page count no longer matches song_id 16. The residual chance rate is then measured, not assumed, by the placebo the checklist asks for: build $S'$ from the summary of a different run of the same scenario and a wrong task's $P'$, and report $\Pr[v^\star \in S']$ and $\Pr[v^\star \in P']$ beside the real cells; the placebo costs nothing because it reuses the same logs. The card's five-of-six 'different reaction step' disagreements are the untyped failure this fixes. The build cell, the exposure/closure split and the audit are all defined on typed matches; the claim and kill are unchanged.

objections.objection: The sets $P$ and $S$ are built from printed environment outputs, but in the SJC/ACON harness the agent acts through a stateful Python shell: an API result bound to a variable (`transactions = apis.venmo.show_transactions(...)`) and passed into a state-changing call (`apis.venmo.like(t.id)`) is never printed, and the interpreter state survives compaction because compaction rewrites the LLM context, not the shell. A needed value can therefore be fetched, used correctly and absent from $P$ (labelled 'build'), and a value present in $S$ can be irrelevant to an agent that acts through a variable, so the cells do not measure what the agent 'had in view'. The matcher must read the executed code's call arguments and the API responses (the environment's request log), not the printed observation strings.
objections.answer: The harness facts are verified (acon env.py: `output = self.world.execute(code)` is the observation; AppWorld's shell is stateful). The objection's own last sentence is the answer, and AppWorld already supplies it: `appworld/requester.py` RequestTracker.add_request deep-copies every call's method, url and resolved data into `logs/api_calls.jsonl` ('all API/HTTP calls made by agent', README), which is also how `ground_truth/api_calls.json` was produced. So emitted values $w$ are literal and resolved at the API layer whatever the Python text says (`apis.venmo.like(t.id)` logs the integer), and the professor's premise objection ('neither the emitted value nor the needed value is a literal in the action text') is answered at that layer: the action text is not where the probe reads. Responses are not stored by the tracker; the fresh arm logs them with a one-line wrapper on the requester, which is why the fresh run (not TRACE's release) is the corpus. With $P$ defined as the union of typed values in API responses received by the agent's code plus its stdout, the three cases sort correctly: a value fetched into a variable and used correctly is in $P$ and the action is not wrong, so there is nothing to label; a value fetched into a variable, described by name in the summary and lost at the boundary (TRACE's live_state_not_addressable, 4 of 13 defect records in w4096.json, the NameError at 2610.08722 line 74) has $v^\star \in P$ and $v^\star \notin S$, which is the exposure cell, where it belongs, and theory #4's charge that build absorbs it holds only under the stdout-only $P$ the objection rejects; TRACE's two causal mechanisms both show at the API layer, call_signature_corruption as a logged create_file call missing the content field, collection_to_prose_or_count as page_index values that are in $P$ and absent from $S$. One limit is conceded inside this answer: a variable that survives the boundary is a channel the LLM's view does not show, so 'in view' means 'in the LLM context or in a live binding', and the would_change text's lever for the exposure cell must read 'carry the value, by observation or by binding', not only 'keep raw observations'.
objections.merged: professor #5 (premise 'needed facts are literal values' false; args are variables; TRACE mechanisms invisible to a value matcher) and theory #4 (build cell absorbs live_state_not_addressable) merged here.

objections.persona: checklist:A first measurement that names a benchmark confirms it is runnable (public code and data) or budgets the re-implementation; 'Dollar-matched' needs the unit
objections.objection: The ~$300 / 2 weeks is borrowed from C-W43-08, not derived: SJC Table 5 gives Prompting on AppWorld with GPT-5.6 Luna at 112.8K cumulative agent-plus-compressor tokens per task (inputs and outputs), so 441 runs (train+dev x 3) are 49.7M tokens and 504 runs (test-normal) 56.9M; the judge costs nothing in this arm (the safeguard arm never calls Jev), and the dollar figure depends on GPT-5.6 Luna's list price, which the record never states — at $1.25/$10 per million with a 90/10 input/output split the arm is about $125, at twice that about $250, and medium-effort reasoning tokens are billed as output whether or not the paper's count includes them. The arm is runnable: `python -m sjc.benchmarks.appworld.run --method safeguard --window 4096` on ACON commit d63f9ae plus `third_party/acon.patch`, AppWorld 0.1.x data public as a 34 MB encrypted bundle, OPENAI_API_KEY only; but the shipped tasklist is test-normal, the train/dev list has to be built, no seed controls API sampling, and the MiniMax-M3 arm costs 142.6K tokens per task.
objections.answer: Recomputed: $441 \times 112.8\mathrm{K} = 49.7\mathrm{M}$ tokens; at \$1.25 / \$10 per million with a 90/10 input/output split the arm is \$106, at 80/20 it is \$149; the two-arm design (Prompting plus No-compression, conceded above) is 99.5M tokens, \$211-298 at that price. So the record's \$300 is an upper bound that holds at list price for both arms or at twice list for one, and the unit the checklist asks for is 'tokens per task at the model's list price', which the record now states. The runnability facts are accepted and two items are added to the plan: build the train+dev tasklist from `datasets/train.txt` and `datasets/dev.txt` (the shipped list is test-normal), and patch the requester to log responses (see the stateful-shell entry). The first step is cheaper than any arm: ask SJC's authors for their Prompting-arm run logs (`<run>/trajectories/<task_id>.json` holds the steps and 'the summary the agent saw'), which makes the compacted arm free and leaves only the response log to recover by deterministic replay of the logged calls.

objections.objection: The 'two existing annotations disagree and the probe adjudicates' framing compares two different agent-compressor models, not two labelling methods: SJC's 29-of-35 figure is GPT-5.6 Luna on the train split, TRACE's 0-of-14 is MiniMax-M3 on the 147 train+dev tasks, both at a 4,096-token window. A probe on one model cannot adjudicate; matched adjudication needs the Prompting arm on both models (SJC ran both: 112.8K and 142.6K tokens per task), which doubles the arm.
objections.answer: conceded: 2610.08722 Sec. 2 names TRACE's agent and compressor as minimax-m3 and SJC Sec. 5.1 names GPT-5.6 Luna for its training-split analysis; one arm on one model compares with one incumbent only. The compelled correction: the probe's comparison partner is SJC's Table 11 on the same (model, compressor, window, split), run by run where the authors share logs; TRACE's figure is a second model and is not adjudicated by this arm. The pre-registered surprise is reworded to drop 'adjudicates'. The MiniMax-M3 arm is the ceiling scenario's second model, not part of the kill probe.

objections.objection: The pre-registered surprise ('the two existing annotations disagree and the probe adjudicates') is false because SJC and TRACE measure different quantities and already agree: SJC's 29/35 counts whether the failing action carries out a summary entry and SJC itself says the entry 'raises the chance of the error rather than determining it', with its interventional check tracing 4 of 10 recovered tasks to an unsupported entry; TRACE's 2 of 14 HYBRID counts a four-part causal chain; 4/10 and 2/14 are consistent, and the probe's set-membership label is a third quantity that is neither. Under standards.md Gate 2 Route B the candidate's own expected result (build dominates, 'conceded in advance') equals the field's assumption (TRACE: POLICY dominates; the card's own 15 of 24 build failures), which the standards call a service, not a paper.
objections.answer: Half conceded inside the answer, half answered. Conceded: SJC Sec. 5.5 ('raises the chance of the error rather than determining it'; 4 of 10) and TRACE's 2 of 14 HYBRID are compatible once read as a conditional and a causal count, and the probe's set-membership label is a third quantity; the word 'adjudicates' goes (see the previous entry). Answered on Route B: the field's assumption, as this lane has written it down, is SJC's headline framing, which CL-W43-05 carries verbatim as its current_belief ('83% of failures follow one unsourced bullet') and which ACON operationalizes by rewriting compression guidelines from failure analyses; the probe's expected result (the summary's dropped or asserted content is the minority of post-compaction failures; the agent's never-fetched values the majority) contradicts that belief and agrees with TRACE's n = 14 human annotation. A field whose two incumbents point opposite ways at n = 35 and n = 14 has no single assumption for the expected result to equal; a judge-free count at n of about 90 that lands on one side is not a service under Route B's wording. What makes it a thin paper rather than a service is conceded elsewhere: without the uncompressed control the count does not speak to compaction.

objections.persona: checklist:Pairs share policies; curves share tasks (2026-10-20); theory; professor
objections.objection: Failures cluster by scenario, not task: AppWorld tasks are three variants of one template, and SJC's 35 failures sit in 10 scenarios with one scenario holding 9, so the record's task-level bootstrap is the wrong cluster. A scenario-cluster bootstrap with Table 11's sizes gives a 95% half-width of 0.25-0.32 at $n = 35$ (clusters half to fully homogeneous in cell) and 0.21-0.26 at the train+dev scale (~49 failures in ~16 scenarios), so the pre-registered kill 'lower end above 0.4' needs a point estimate of about 0.65-0.70, not the 0.56 the record computes, and the 50-label audit must sample across scenarios, not runs.
objections.answer: conceded: SJC App. D states 'a single scenario accounts for 9 of them, so per-run counts are not independent', and I reproduced the width: with cluster sizes [3,9,2,1,3,3,4,5,2,3] the analytic SE under full within-scenario correlation at $p = 0.5$ is $\sqrt{0.25 \sum_i w_i^2} = 0.185$ and the scenario bootstrap half-width is 0.31 at $n = 35$; at train+dev scale (about 90 failed runs in about 18 scenarios) it is about 0.25 under full correlation, so the kill's lower bound above 0.4 needs a point estimate near 0.65, and the kill search's 'half-width about 0.15 at n = 40' is the task-level number and is wrong. The kill remains satisfiable and the result remains reportable at any value, but 'informative either way' overstates it: an exposure share between 0.4 and 0.65 ends in an interval that neither kills nor clears. The compelled changes: the bootstrap unit is the scenario; the audit samples across scenarios; the Kish design effect (4.8 at ICC 1 on SJC's sizes, $n_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 7$) is reported. Professor #6's two extras are also conceded: an action the reference never makes (SJC's 5 invented deliverables) has no $v^\star$ and needs an 'extra action' category labelled by $w$ alone, and a boolean needed value (the habit case) is classifiable only under typed matching (field 'meditate', value no), which the untyped exclusion list drops.
objections.merged: theory #6 (three units mixed; Kish design effect 4.8; Wilson bounds; 'at least 40%' not resolvable at this n) and professor #6 (scenario bootstrap half-width 0.31; kill near-unsatisfiable; 5 of 35 have no needed value; boolean on exclusion list) merged here.

objections.objection: The production baseline is absent: the corpus's compaction fires at a 4,096-token window 'set well below the models' limits so that compaction occurs within each task', giving several compactions per 20-step task and 5.8 extra steps, whereas deployed harnesses compact once near a 200K-1M limit; the cell shares are properties of the (agent, compressor, window) triple and the claim's sentence 'compaction fails by unsourced persistence' carries no window. Two bookkeeping items follow from the data: access tokens are 1,409 of the 3,536 state-changing argument values in the reference solutions and must be excluded (a summary that drops a token costs one re-login, not a failure) or exposure is inflated; and 42.8% of values are file paths from a few file_system scenarios (one task moves hundreds of files), so cell shares must be reported per failure, never per value.
objections.answer: Accepted as scope, all three parts, none of which touches the claim's truth. The record's identifiability text already states the cells are 'properties of the (agent, compressor, benchmark) triple'; the window joins that list, and the sentence reported carries '$B = 4096$ tokens, harness-triggered, about 2.5 compactions per run (SJC: 667 summaries over 270 runs)'. A second window is the price of saying anything about deployed harnesses and is a second arm, not part of the kill probe. Auth tokens are excluded (the attackers' own script excluded them and the count, 1,409 of 3,536, is verified); the 850 path values are composed (directory plus filename) and fall into the composed category conceded above, where their constituents are matched. The unit of every reported share is the failed run, clustered by scenario, as the previous entry fixes; theory #8's point that agent and compressor are one model, so exposure versus closure separates two draws of one disposition rather than two parties, is accepted as a reading note for the lane, not a defect of the labels.
objections.merged: theory #8 (conditioning set; window as part of the quantity's definition; agent and compressor one model) merged here.

objections.objection: 'Judge-free' hides a judgment step: locating the divergent action and choosing which boundary's summary is $S$ (about 2.5 compactions per run: 667 summaries over 270 runs) requires aligning the agent's path to a reference program that the benchmark does not privilege, since AppWorld grades by state and admits different solution paths; SJC needed LLM annotators for exactly this alignment. The alignment rule must be written and audited as a label, or the probe has a judge.
objections.answer: The rule is written here and is deterministic. AppWorld's evaluation report names the failed state checks per task (evaluation.py assertions; the report.md the harness writes); each failed check reads one or more database rows that the reference's state-changing calls wrote, so the needed values are the arguments of exactly those reference calls, which is a join on the check's rows, not an alignment of paths. The divergent action is the first post-boundary state-changing call in the agent's api_calls.jsonl whose (url, resolved data) matches no reference call for that task and whose effect a failed check reads, or, when no such call exists, the needed call is 'never made'. Path freedom does not disturb this: a different path with the same final state passes every check and produces no failed run; a failed run's state differs from the reference's on the checked rows, and the row identifies the value. $S$ is the summary of the last boundary before the divergent action plus the tool results between them. SJC's annotators also had to judge whether an action 'carries out a summary entry', which is a semantic question about a plan; the probe asks only whether a typed value is present, which is why it needs no judge. The rule is pre-registered and falls under the 50-label audit as the objection asks.

objections.objection: Exact matching reads a corrupted value as a dropped one: TRACE's token_rewrite and call_signature_corruption records (4 of 13) are values present in the summary with altered digits or signatures, which the matcher assigns to the exposure cell whose recipe consequence ('keep or re-fetch raw observations') is the wrong lever for corruption. A 50-label audit at 85% agreement has a Wilson interval of $[0.72, 0.93]$ and cannot separate this matcher error from the acceptable rate.
objections.answer: Accepted and fixed inside the protocol. With typed matching, the exposure cell splits into two sub-labels that the matcher computes without a judge: 'dropped' (no value for the typed field in $S$) and 'corrupted' (a different value for the same typed field in $S$, including OpenClaw's structured 'Exact identifiers' lines), and the Jennifer Powell \$531.00 case and TRACE's token_rewrite records land in 'corrupted'. The lever reading is then per sub-label, and the objection's premise that keeping raw observations is the wrong lever for corruption is only half right: with the raw observation retained beside the corrupted entry the agent has both values in view and the case becomes closure, so retention changes the cell even for corruption, which is itself a result worth reporting. On the audit: the Wilson interval at 85% agreement with $n = 50$ is $[0.71, 0.92]$ (recomputed), so 50 labels cannot separate 85% from 75%; the audit grows to about 150 labels stratified by cell and scenario, which costs annotator hours and no API spend.

objections.persona: checklist:2026-10-09 premise numbers verbatim; checklist:premise numbers carry the source's category name and denominator verbatim
objections.objection: The claim record's premise misquotes its source: '2610.20927 reports 83% of failures follow one unsourced bullet' conflates two numbers; SJC's 83% is 29 of 35 failures that follow any summary entry, of which 22 are unsupported and 3 contradicted, so the unsourced share is $25/35 = 71\%$ (or $22/35 = 63\%$ strictly unsupported), on 35 runs from 10 scenarios after excluding 9 runs of one broken scenario.
objections.answer: conceded: SJC Sec. 3.2 reads 'In 29 of the 35 failed runs, the failing action carries out a specific summary entry [...] 22 of these entries are supported by no output and 3 contradict one; only 4 are supported', and App. D excludes b0a8eae's 9 runs from 44. CL-W43-05's current_belief must read: '2610.20927: 29 of 35 analysed Prompting failures (83%) follow a summary entry; 25 of those entries (71% of failures) are unsupported or contradicted by the environment outputs; 35 runs from 10 scenarios, GPT-5.6 Luna, 90 training tasks x 3 runs, 4,096-token window'. The correction is to the claim record, not to the candidate.
objections.merged: theory #10 and professor #8 (the same misquote, the same correct figures) merged into one entry.

objections.objection: The 'why now' and the 'who asked for it in print' both rest on a sentence the card's paper does not contain: the record says 2610.26836 'states in its own text that the same question for compaction summaries has no such oracle', and the paper's full text has zero occurrences of 'oracle', 'compaction', 'memory file' or 'sub-agent'; the quotation is the card-writer's inference (card field information_asymmetry (4)) promoted to a limitation quote. Gate 0 fails, the target value has no requester in print, and the only remaining 'why now' is 'a paper showed exact matching works on a deterministic tool', which TRACE (deterministic prefix re-execution with PRE and POST arms, August 2026) and Reclaim (June 2026) had already shown for compaction.
objections.answer: conceded: I grepped the stripped full text (scratchpad/cards/2610.26836/paper.txt, 73,669 characters): 'oracle' 0 hits; 'compact' occurs once, in a reference title; 'memory' once, in the agent prompt ('not memory'); 'summar' once, in the same reference title; Sec. 9's four paragraphs (Models, Decoding and prompts, Runs, What verification establishes) and Sec. 6 say nothing about compaction summaries, memory files or sub-agent briefs. The sentence in why_now and target_value is the card's information_asymmetry (4) inference written as a quotation, and the record's density_and_ownership repeats it. What the gate re-grounds on, from the kill search's fetched texts: Reclaim 2606.25449 Sec. 10 ('a naturalistic corpus would reintroduce the judge model we deliberately avoid [...] What stays untested is a genuine long-running assistant or agent memory in the wild') and SJC's Limitations ('the failure analysis in Section 3 relies on annotations produced by LLM annotators under a written protocol'); those are requesters in print for a judge-free label on natural compaction failures. The why-now is then the SJC harness release (2026-10-14) that makes the Prompting arm re-runnable, not the card's paper; and the professor is right that TRACE's PRE/POST replay and Reclaim's exact-match scoring had shown deterministic labelling for compaction on planted or replayed facts before the card's paper, so the card's paper contributes the three-stage decomposition shape, not the enabling piece. Gate 0 is re-passed on the corrected sentences; the record's wording failed it.

objections.persona: checklist:2026-10-20 headline is the sentence the probe tests; one claim per sentence; quantifiers pre-registered
objections.objection: The candidate's claim sentence carries two quantified claims (exposure at most one third; unsourced at least 40%) and a causal conclusion, and its kill does not match its quantifier: the kill fires only at $\pi_{\mathrm{exp}} \geq 0.5$ with lower bound above 0.4, so any exposure share in $(1/3, 1/2)$ falsifies the stated claim and fires nothing. CL-W43-05's headline 'not by length' is tested by no cell: no length knob is varied, and the gate1 text equates the exposure cell with length although a summary of any length can drop a value.
objections.answer: conceded: the claim sentence contains three statements (exposure at most $1/3$, unsourced at least $0.4$, and the 'so' conclusion) and the kill is pinned to $0.5$, so an exposure share in $(1/3, 1/2)$ refutes the first statement and fires nothing; the record's 'informative either way' is false in that band. 'Not by length' is tested by no cell: the probe varies no length knob and a short summary drops values as easily as a long one; the gate1 line in CL-W43-05 that equates the exposure cell with length is an operator inference, not a measurement. I cannot rewrite the claim; the narrowest surviving version states one sentence with its kill at the same number and leaves 'length' to the probes that vary it (C-W43-08's matched-deletion arm).

objections.objection: Known idea with new words: exact-match membership of summary content in the source corpus is extractive-fragment coverage (Newsroom, 2018: summaries 'borrowing words and phrases from articles at varying rates') applied at value granularity, and 'unsourced' is Maynez et al.'s extrinsic hallucination ('hallucinate content that is unfaithful to the input document'); the record presents the cells as the card's build/exposure/closure decomposition 'moved' to the summary, so the lineage, the baselines (coverage, faithfulness metrics such as entailment) and the one genuinely new cell (never-fetched, which the card already owns as 'build') are mis-stated. Reframed in the summarization field's words, the deliverable is a coverage/faithfulness table on one compressor's summaries, a footnote in that literature.
objections.answer: The lineage is accepted and the density_and_ownership text is corrected to name Maynez et al. (2005.00661, extrinsic hallucination) and Newsroom coverage as the incumbent rulers, which the kill search listed as pre-window precedents without promoting them. The deliverable is not their table, for one reason the objection passes over: coverage and faithfulness measure the summary's content against its source, while the probe measures the needed content (what the next correct action required, fixed by a reference program) against the summary and against the whole produced corpus, which is why it has a never-fetched cell and a closure cell at all; a summary with perfect coverage of its source and zero hallucination still scores exposure if the source never held the value and build if nobody fetched it. The register is measurement, as the record says, and a three-column table on one compressor's natural failures is the intended size of the result; the professor's 'footnote' is a judgment about reach that the lab-verdict concession above already lowers.

objections.objection: What I would tell a first-year student: the group that holds the logs already runs the judge-free step as a verification pass ('every quoted entry, action, and check was verified by script against the logs'), published the judge-labelled version because the entries that matter are plans with nothing to exact-match, and can emit the three-cell table in a day; the one experiment that would convince me is interventional and partly in print, SJC's delete-unsourced arm (+5.3 accuracy, Pass3 +8.9) against an omission-repair arm that re-inserts dropped values verbatim at the same boundaries (the arm 2608.16370 ran in a planning environment: 'restore dropped state through controlled oracle interventions'), compute-matched, on TRACE's PRE/POST replay; nobody has run that pair on AppWorld because the two groups each hold half the stack. An observational three-cell count adjudicating two annotations that do not disagree is a service to Min and Chen, and the re-open test is an email asking them for the run logs, which the record has not sent.
objections.answer: Three parts. The email is accepted as the first step and the cheapest: it is the standards' re-open test and it turns the compacted arm's cost to zero if answered; the record's why_not_done named SJC's authors as first movers without asking them, which the checklist forbids. The interventional pair (delete unsourced entries versus re-insert dropped typed values verbatim at the same boundaries, compute-matched on PRE/POST replay) is the convincing experiment and is the territory of C-W43-08 and C-W43-09 on this claim; the census is their prerequisite only in one way, which is also its defence: the re-insertion arm needs the list of dropped needed values per boundary, and that list is this probe's exposure cell computed per boundary, so the census is the first half of the professor's own experiment, not a substitute for it. On 'service': SJC's script verified quoted entries after the annotators chose them; it did not enumerate needed values from the reference or label failures no entry explains (6 of 35 'unrelated' and the 29caf6f block), so the day's table the professor imagines is not a pass they have run. The reach conceded above (no control, the lab verdict, the clause-2 estimator) is what keeps this a probe and not a paper.

redteam.narrowest_surviving_version: What survives is a redesigned census with a control, run after one email, and it tests one sentence of CL-W43-05, not two. Corpus: first ask SJC's authors (Min, Chen) for the Prompting-arm run logs; failing that, re-run the OpenClaw safeguard arm through SJC's harness on AppWorld train+dev (147 tasks x 3 seeds, 441 runs, the only split with ground_truth/api_calls.json) with the requester patched to log API responses, plus the No-compression arm (441 runs) as the control; about $110-150 per arm at GPT-5.6 Luna list price (112.8K tokens per task), $0 GPU, about 3 weeks. Oracle: needed values are typed (field, value) pairs from the reference's state-changing calls joined to the failed evaluation checks; auth tokens excluded; composed values (paths, messages, sums, CSV bodies) decomposed into constituents and labelled by them, with the composed share and an 'extra action' category (no $v^\star$) reported; $P$ is the union of typed values in API responses received by the agent's code plus its stdout over the whole run; $S$ is the last pre-divergence summary plus the tool results after it; the divergent action is the first post-boundary state-changing call matching no reference call whose effect a failed check reads. Cells per failed run, clustered by scenario: build ($v^\star \notin P$), exposure split into dropped (no value for the field in $S$) and corrupted (a different value for the field in $S$), closure ($v^\star \in S$); the same build and closure cells on No-compression failures, and the result reported as the difference in composition between the arms. Controls: a placebo $S'$ from another run of the same scenario and a wrong task's $P'$ for the chance-membership rate; a 150-label two-annotator audit stratified by cell and scenario. The sentence tested: 'Among post-compaction failures at $B = 4096$ on AppWorld with the OpenClaw compressor and GPT-5.6 Luna, the needed typed value was produced by the environment and absent from the post-boundary view (dropped or corrupted) in under one third of runs, and the excess of such runs over the uncompressed arm's failures is the compaction-attributable omission share.' Its kill is the candidate's pre-registered one unchanged, $\pi_{\mathrm{exp}} \geq 0.5$ with the scenario-cluster lower bound above 0.4, which at about 90 failed runs needs a point estimate near 0.65 and otherwise ends in an interval the digest reports as such. What does not survive: the claim's second clause (unsourced at least 40%) under the atomic reading is already at 9-26% on SJC's Table 11, and its corrected estimator $\Pr[w \in M \wedge w \notin P]$ is a new candidate, not this one; the claim's 'so compaction fails by' conclusion, which needs the control arm's difference and not the census; the $50 / 6-day cost and the TRACE-corpus arm; the lab-position verdict's 'day's audit', since production logs carry no reference; and any test of CL-W43-05's 'not by length', which no cell touches.
redteam.verdict_reason: killed as a probe of CL-W43-05 as written: four killing objections conceded with evidence — (1) no uncompressed control, so 'compaction fails by X' does not follow from a census of post-compaction failures (SJC Table 3: 116.9 vs 80.1 failures of 504 runs, excess 31.5%; TRACE's re-audit retained 0 of 3 presence-based labels); (2) the scalar-matching oracle does not cover the failures it must label (25.7% of AppWorld reference values are composed or task-given; 19 of SJC's 35 adjudicated failures sit in composed-value scenarios), so the record's own >25%-unclassifiable protocol kill fires before any run; (3) the 40% unsourced quantifier is set by an unwritten normalization rule and the published table gives 8.6-26% under atomic matching, firing the pre-registered kill; (4) the 'who asked in print' quote attributed to 2610.26836 does not exist in the paper (Gate 0). The narrowest surviving version — a census with the No-compression arm as control on AppWorld train+dev, typed matcher pre-registered, scenario clusters, one sentence (exposure share under one third, differenced) — is a new candidate owed with its own scorecard, not this one.

title: Ghost information: KV drop versus the same drop done as text
statement: On the released AKV engine (SGLang fork, github.com/thu-nics/AKV) run two arms that show the model the identical visible text at identical positions and differ in one bit: arm KV keeps the retained entries' KV as computed while the old tool responses were still visible (drop the KV of every tool response older than the latest $K = 12$, then repos immediately so positions are $0, \ldots, r-1$); arm TEXT removes the same tool responses from the text and re-prefills the retained text contiguously (the observation-masking recipe of 2508.21433 at the same $K$). Measure paired pass rate on 300 SWE-bench Verified tasks x 2 runs with GPT-OSS-120B (mini-SWE-agent, 250-step limit, official tests), plus the cost of each arm under the paper's hit/miss price arithmetic, under a flat per-token price, and in measured GPU-seconds on the same build. The pre-step is zero agent runs: teacher-forced next-token divergence between the two states on the paper's or our recorded trajectories.
claim: A transformer agent keeps using information from tool outputs it can no longer see, through the cache entries that were computed while those outputs were visible, and that ghost information is worth a measurable pass-rate margin over re-reading the identical visible text.
trick: Give the model the same words at the same positions twice, once with a cache that remembers the deleted tool outputs and once freshly computed without them, and see whether the memory of the deleted text changes what it solves.
why_now: AKV (2610.28577, October 2026) ships the drop and repos operations and a segment-batch attention that restores any operation history in one prefill, so arm KV and arm TEXT are two configurations of one released engine, not new kernels; the paper's own Table 1 compares only against threshold summarization and its text-trim number (1.85x cost on 100 BrowseComp-Plus tasks, sec. 3.2) carries no accuracy; the text arm's recipe and its accuracy claim are in print since 2508.21433 (August 2025). The import import:2026-W43-S6xF7 (2026-10-25) predicts KV residency is the binding station in agentic RL, which makes the KV-level drop a training lever and the answer to 'is the gain the drop or the cache' a recipe decision for trainers as well as servers.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (no agent runs, ~10 GPU-h): on 50 recorded AKV trajectories (GPT-OSS-120B, SWE-bench Verified), teacher-force each turn under the arm-KV state and the arm-TEXT state and record the per-token divergence $\delta_t = D_{\mathrm{KL}}\big(\pi(\cdot \mid \mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{KV}}_t) \,\|\, \pi(\cdot \mid \mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{TEXT}}_t)\big)$, where $\pi$ is the model's next-token distribution and $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{KV}}_t$, $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{TEXT}}_t$ are the two active caches holding the same tokens at the same positions; if the median $\delta_t$ is below the bf16 run-to-run noise of the engine itself, stop (the states are the same and there is nothing to find). Step 1 (~110 GPU-h on 4 H100-class GPUs): the two arms on a fixed random 300-task subset of SWE-bench Verified, 2 runs each at the paper's sampling settings, paired by (task, run); outcome $\Delta$ = pass(KV) - pass(TEXT) with a paired bootstrap 90% interval over 600 pairs (standard error about 1.8 points at a 20% discordance rate); secondary: token logs per arm converted to cost under the paper's price table, under a flat price, and in measured GPU-seconds, and the hit/miss price ratio $p_{\mathrm{hit}}/p_{\mathrm{miss}}$ at which the arms cost the same.
killing_experiment.kills_if: The paired 90% interval for $\Delta$ lies inside $[-3, +3]$ pass-rate points: ghost information is worth less than 3 points on this model and benchmark, the accuracy claim of cache engineering over summarization is the drop policy's and belongs to the observation-masking literature, and the paper's contribution reduces to a cost line whose sign depends on the hit/miss price ratio (reported). That negative is citable on its own (KV eviction and text trimming are interchangeable for accuracy; choose by price model), so both outcomes are informative. A positive $\Delta \geq 3$ with the interval excluding zero establishes the claim; a negative $\Delta \leq -3$ shows off-distribution retained KV hurts and that text trimming plus background re-prefill (2607.00151) is the better recipe.

preregistered_surprise.expected: $\Delta$ within $\pm 3$ points (judgment probability 0.55); $\Delta \geq +3$, ghost information consumed (0.25); $\Delta \leq -3$, off-distribution cache hurts (0.20). Step 0 is expected to show $\delta_t$ well above engine noise in the first turn after a drop and decaying over later turns (0.7), so a null in step 1 would mean the states differ and the difference carries no task value.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper treats ghost information as a feature without a test: 'retained KV can still carry information from dropped history' (Figure 1, sec. 3.2), supported by a citation to attention-sink work; its App. A.4.4 says a weaker model is 'more sensitive to cache modifications'. The text-trimming camp (2508.21433: omitting older observations matches LLM summarization on SWE-bench Verified across five model configurations) implicitly treats the visible text as the whole state. The two camps cannot both be right about the value of the retained entries' history, so either outcome moves one of them.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If $\Delta \geq +3$: a model reads task-relevant information from cache entries whose source tokens are gone, so every compaction, memory and trimming method that re-prefills from text discards information it could keep for free, and any trainer that recomputes the policy from text trains a different policy than the one that acted. If within $\pm 3$: cache engineering's accuracy gain is the drop choice; the decision between KV drop and text trim is a price-model question with a reported crossover ratio, and leaderboard cost columns built on list prices should state which model they assume. If $\Delta \leq -3$: holes in the cache are a liability, and SmoothAgent-style hidden re-prefill of trimmed text is the recipe.

identifiability: Random given: fixed checkpoint (GPT-OSS-120B), fixed engine build and precision (BF16, SGLang v0.5.20 fork), fixed task subset, the agent's sampling at the paper's settings. SWE-bench is deterministic after the action (tests run in a container), so the only randomness is the policy's sampling, which is the same object in both arms; the paired design cancels task difficulty. Repos after every drop makes positions identical across arms, so the measured difference is a property of the model's state (what the retained entries encode), not of position gaps or the price protocol; the paper's own policy (repos only at $\tau = 96$K) is an optional third arm that separates the position-gap effect and is not needed for the kill. The cost numbers are protocol quantities (a price table), so they are reported as a crossover ratio and as measured GPU-seconds, never as one percentage.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent systems measurement: two configurations of a released open engine on a public benchmark with an open-weight model, under one GPU-week; no serving stack to own. A serving team (SGLang, an API provider with cache pricing) can run it on its own logs faster, so the solo output is the published controlled comparison and the crossover ratio, which is the artifact L3 asks for (a definitive comparison). L4 secondary: it is the controlled comparison the lane requires before any compaction mechanism is admitted, written as measurement, not as a recipe.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2610.28577 claims the gain over summarization without the matched text arm and names 'training agents under this scheme' as future work; 2508.21433 claims text masking matches summarization; the two camps disagree about whether retained cache history has value and neither has run the one-bit test. Who pays: serving teams deciding whether to ship cache-level eviction (SGLang fork maintenance versus a prompt-level trim); API buyers whose cost depends on the hit/miss price ratio; agentic-RL teams deciding whether a trainer must reproduce the cache state (the import S6xF7 makes the drop a training lever).

impact_ceiling.floor: A null: KV drop and text trim are interchangeable for accuracy and the choice is a price-model question with a published crossover ratio; a footnote cited by compaction and serving papers; requires only step 1; probability 0.55 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: A positive margin on one model and benchmark: ghost information is real and consumed; replicated on GPT-OSS-20B (the paper says weaker models are more sensitive) and on BrowseComp-Plus (another ~$300); changes the default of harness builders from text trim to cache-level drop where the engine supports it; probability 0.3 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The margin holds across three models and two task families and is paired with the per-token divergence curve, giving a mechanism (which layers and heads carry it) and a trainer consequence; every compaction and memory paper that re-prefills must report what it loses; requires attention readouts on the engine (another ~60 GPU-h); probability 0.15 (judgment).

relevance.routes: L3 systems route (Lloyd / Netravali / Tri Dao): direct, a serving-level controlled comparison with a cost model consequence. L4 (all; product teams): the controlled comparison the lane demands. L2 (Narasimhan, RL groups): indirect, through the trainer consequence. L1: the price-model dependence of cost columns.
relevance.industry: Direct: API providers price cache hits and misses; harness builders (mini-SWE-agent, Pi, OpenHands) choose between trim and cache-level drop.
relevance.jacobs_edge: Moderate: the state-versus-text distinction is an identity question (same tokens, same positions, different state), and the RoPE re-rotation $K \leftarrow R(q) R(p)^{-1} K$ in finite precision is a numerics check he can run; no physics content.

scorecard.kill_probe: Step 0 teacher-forced divergence (~10 GPU-h) then two arms x 300 SWE-bench Verified tasks x 2 runs on GPT-OSS-120B (~110 GPU-h, ~$420 at $3.50 per GPU-hour, 10 days); kills if the paired 90% interval for the pass-rate difference lies inside $\pm 3$ points.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: From the card's neighbors only (the kill search does the count): SideQuest 2602.22603 (a trained side branch decides which retrieved tokens to delete from the cache; no text-matched arm), Context Language Models 2609.37725 (text edits with suffix-cache reuse; the edit is to text, so it is the TEXT arm's family), TokenPilot 2606.17016 (text-level cleaning and batched eviction to keep the prefix cache; TEXT family), SmoothAgent 2607.00151 (background re-prefill of trimmed or summarized prefixes; hides the TEXT arm's cost), Complexity Trap 2508.21433 (text masking matches summarization on SWE-bench Verified; the TEXT arm's accuracy claim). None of these, by the card's reading, compares KV-level drop against the identical drop done as text. The paper itself owns the drop/repos formalization and the engine; the one-bit comparison is unclaimed in the card's text. Kill-search queries in the neighbors' words: 'KV cache eviction', 'observation masking', 'attention sink', 'retained tokens', 'tool output', 'agent', 're-prefill'.
scorecard.why_now: AKV engine and code, October 2026 (2610.28577); Complexity Trap, August 2025 (2508.21433); import S6xF7, 2026-10-25 (KV residency as the binding station turns the drop into a training lever).
scorecard.register_and_not: A controlled comparison in the measurement register with a cost-model consequence and a trainer consequence. Not a new eviction policy, not a learned drop model, not a serving engine, not a compaction recipe, not a frontier recipe fight.

neighbors_to_check_first: 2508.21433 — Complexity Trap: observation masking matches LLM summarization on SWE-bench Verified; the TEXT arm's recipe; read its cost accounting (flat tokens or cache-aware) to settle the 1.85x versus halving discrepancy before any run
2607.00151 — SmoothAgent: background re-prefill of transformed prefixes; the recipe that wins if the TEXT arm wins; check whether it reports accuracy of trimmed versus full prefixes
2606.17016 — TokenPilot: text-level eviction aligned to prefix caching; check whether it ever compares against cache-level eviction
2602.22603 — SideQuest: model-driven cache deletion; check whether it reports accuracy against a text-deletion control at matched retained content
2609.37725 — Context Language Models: context as an editable file with suffix-cache reuse; the TEXT family with learned editing; check for any cache-versus-text ablation
headline_test: A transformer agent keeps using tool outputs it can no longer see, through cache entries computed while they were visible, and that memory of deleted text is worth at least 3 pass-rate points over re-reading the identical visible context.

title: Off-policy by cache: how far the served policy under KV eviction departs from its own text
statement: For agent trajectories sampled under harness-controlled KV eviction (AKV drop and repos), define per token the served distribution $\pi_{\mathrm{serve}}(\cdot \mid \mathcal{C}_t)$, with $\mathcal{C}_t$ the active cache produced by the operation sequence $o_{1:t}$, and the text-recomputed distribution $\pi_{\mathrm{text}}(\cdot \mid \tilde{x}_{1:t})$, with $\tilde{x}_{1:t}$ the retained visible tokens prefilled contiguously, which is what a trainer's recompute path sees; measure $\delta_t = D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi_{\mathrm{serve}} \,\|\, \pi_{\mathrm{text}})$ and the sampled-token log-ratio $\rho_t = \log \pi_{\mathrm{text}}(x_t) - \log \pi_{\mathrm{serve}}(x_t)$ by turn offset since the last drop, against the in-run baseline $\delta^{\mathrm{num}}_t$ (serving engine with full cache versus a trainer-style BF16 recompute of the same full text), which is the engine-trainer numerical mismatch that RL frameworks already correct with importance-ratio truncation. Teacher-forced replays only, on recorded AKV trajectories from GPT-OSS-20B and GPT-OSS-120B on SWE-bench Verified; the quantity is a ruler for any cache-editing method used during RL rollouts.
claim: An agent served under KV eviction samples from a policy that its trainer, recomputing log-probabilities from the visible text, does not reproduce: in the turns after a drop the divergence between the two is at least ten times the engine-trainer numerical mismatch trainers already correct for.
trick: Replay the agent's own words under the cache it actually had and under the fresh cache a trainer would build from the text, and measure how differently the model would have bet on each next token.
why_now: 2610.28577 (October 2026) formalizes that the cache state depends on the operation sequence $o_{1:m}$, not on the token sequence (sec. 3.4, Figure 5), names training under the scheme as future work (sec. 6), and ships the segment-batch attention that reconstructs any operation history in one prefill, which is exactly the teacher-forcing tool this ruler needs; import:2026-W43-S6xF7 (2026-10-25) predicts KV residency binds agentic RL throughput, so eviction during rollouts is the next lever systems teams will ship, and the trainer-side distribution question lands with it. Nothing in the card's text or neighbors reports this divergence.

killing_experiment.design: Generate 60 SWE-bench Verified trajectories under the paper's policy (drop all but the latest 12 tool responses; repos at the paper's threshold) with GPT-OSS-20B on one 80 GB GPU and 30 with GPT-OSS-120B on four, recording the operation sequence per turn. Teacher-force each trajectory three ways: (i) under the recorded operation sequence on the AKV engine (served state), (ii) under contiguous re-prefill of the retained text on the same engine (text state), (iii) full text with no drops on the engine and on a trainer-style BF16 HF forward pass (numerical baseline). Report $\delta_t$ and $\rho_t$ per token binned by turn offset since the last drop and since the last repos, as multiples of the median $\delta^{\mathrm{num}}_t$, plus the fraction of tokens whose $|\rho_t|$ exceeds the truncation threshold a trainer would apply. Also report the finite-precision error of the repos re-rotation, $\|R(q) R(p)^{-1} K - K_{\mathrm{recomputed}}\|$, which the paper leaves unmeasured.
killing_experiment.kills_if: The 90th percentile of $\delta_t$ over all tokens in the two turns after a drop is below 2x the median numerical baseline $\delta^{\mathrm{num}}_t$ on both models, and the fraction of tokens with $|\rho_t|$ above a trainer's truncation threshold is within 1 percentage point of the full-cache baseline: cache engineering is free for trainers, text recompute is the right path, and the result is a citable footnote (no operation-aware recompute needed). The claim is established if the median $\delta_t$ in the first post-drop turn is at least 10x the baseline median on both models; between 2x and 10x the claim's quantifier is rewritten to the measured number before any report.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Median post-drop $\delta_t$ at least 10x the numerical baseline in the first turn after a drop on both models, decaying over later turns, larger on GPT-OSS-20B (the paper reports it 'more sensitive to cache modifications'); judgment probability 0.6. Probability 0.25 that the ratio lands between 2x and 10x; 0.15 that it is under 2x and the probe kills the claim.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2610.28577 formalizes the history dependence (sec. 3.4) and stops before the trainer consequence, naming 'training agents under this scheme' as future work (sec. 6). The agentic-RL systems named in import:2026-W43-S6xF7 (prime-rl, veRL, AReaL, ROLL, SkyRL, VenusRL, Heddle, FlashNext-RL) record token sequences, not cache-operation sequences, as the trajectory (to be verified against their code at the kill search; stated here as the shape of every recompute path that takes tokens as input). The trainer's truncation threshold is a protocol constant and is reported as a curve over thresholds, not a single number. No judge, verifier or critic enters.

A lab training agents under eviction would run it on its own trajectories in a day and has more to gain; the solo output is the ruler and the first numbers, published as a note that trainers cite when they decide whether to reproduce cache state. title: Hack-seeding prompts are readable from the base model's rollouts
statement: Replace SimHack's fitted high-risk-prompt ranking (the learned sender coefficient $\beta$, which needs ten reference RL runs) with the quantity its own update rule uses at step zero: for prompt $i$, with pre-RL correct probability $c_{i,0}$, hack probability $h_{i,0}$ and proxy-success probability $s_{i,0} = c_{i,0} + h_{i,0}$ estimated from base-model rollouts at the training temperature, the expected GRPO advantage mass landing on hacking rollouts is $w_i = h_{i,0}\sqrt{(1 - s_{i,0})/s_{i,0}}$ (binary pass/fail reward; the exact value is read off the empirical reward histogram when a partial compile reward exists). Run the removal experiment the paper describes but does not report: GRPO on Qwen3-0.6B in a separable-reward coding environment (the Overwrite hook if released, else the Countdown-Code testbed 2603.07084) with three prompt pools — the full pool, the pool minus the top 5% of prompts by $w_i$, and the pool minus a random 5% matched to the removed set on $c_{i,0}$ — four seeds each, measuring the onset step $t_{50}$ (first step at which half the rollouts are flagged as hacks) and the hack share curve $H_t$. The matched-random arm separates 'the base model already hacks here' from 'the base model cannot solve this', which is the distinction the paper's Sec. 5.2 examples do not control.
claim: Which prompts seed reward hacking under GRPO is readable from the untrained model's rollouts alone: removing the 5% of prompts with the largest step-zero hack advantage mass $w_i$ delays onset by more than removing difficulty-matched random prompts, with no fitted simulator.
trick: Count, per prompt, how often the untrained model passes only by hacking, weight it by how much GRPO rewards a rare success, drop the top prompts, and see whether hacking comes later than when you drop equally hard prompts at random.
why_now: SimHack (2610.28707, 2026-10-20) computes the pre-RL state $S_0$ from 1,024 rollouts per prompt and then ranks hack-seeding prompts by a fitted $\beta$ instead, shows three code examples and runs no removal test; its abstract states that 'the initial hacking rate alone does not determine onset', which is the belief this probe is scoped against. Countdown-Code (2603.07084, March 2026) gives a public environment where proxy and true reward are separable, so the hack label is a deterministic check rather than a judge. A 0.6B GRPO run on 992 prompts costs about 13 GPU-hours (133 GPU-hours for the paper's ten reference runs, App. C), which makes a 12-run removal matrix affordable from the solo position.

killing_experiment.design: Pre-RL: 256 rollouts per prompt at temperature 0.7 on Qwen3-0.6B over the 992-prompt pool (the paper's Lazy-suite count; estimated 8-12 GPU-hours with vLLM), labelled by the environment's deterministic loophole check, giving $c_{i,0}, h_{i,0}, w_i$. RL: three arms (full pool; minus top 5% by $w_i$, about 50 prompts; minus 50 prompts drawn at random from the same $c_{i,0}$ deciles as the removed set) x 4 seeds, paired by seed (same LoRA init and sampling seed across arms), the paper's default recipe (16 prompts per step, 16 rollouts per prompt, learning rate 7e-5, 400 steps, GRPO with LoRA rank 32, VeRL), about 13 GPU-hours per run. Outcome: per arm the median and interquartile range of $t_{50}$ over seeds, the full $H_t$ curve, and the clean-pass rate on a held-out set. Zero-GPU pre-step if the SimHack dataset is released: Spearman correlation of $w_i$ against the per-prompt first-hack step and against the paper's $\beta$ on the existing 325 runs.
killing_experiment.kills_if: The $w_i$-removal arm's median $t_{50}$ lies inside the matched-random arm's seed interquartile range (the two removals are indistinguishable), or both removal arms lie inside the full pool's interquartile range (removing 5% of any prompts does nothing). The first outcome says the pre-RL hack rate carries no information beyond difficulty, so the lever is verifier hardening, not prompt selection; the second says hacking is diffuse across the pool and not seeded by a few prompts, which contradicts the spread-from-seeds reading of 2603.07084 at pool scale. Either negative is a citable control on SimHack's Sec. 5.2 and on the paper's abstract claim, so both outcomes are informative.

preregistered_surprise.expected: The $w_i$-removal arm delays median $t_{50}$ by at least 30% over the full pool and by at least twice the delay of the matched-random arm, with a clean-pass rate within 1 point of the full pool; judgment probability 0.4. Conceded in advance: the paper's abstract says 'the initial hacking rate alone does not determine onset' across recipes, and this probe does not contest that — it holds the recipe fixed and tests whether a step-zero quantity (not the raw hack rate, but the advantage-weighted hack-only-success mass) ranks the seeding prompts; the two statements are compatible if $w_i$ ranks prompts well while the learning rate sets the clock.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: SimHack's text: the initial hacking rate alone does not determine onset (abstract), and the high-risk prompts are those with large fitted sender coefficients $\beta$ after ten reference runs (Sec. 5.2); the three Overwrite rules define 'hack'. Countdown-Code (2603.07084, neighbor abstract): 1% hacked trajectories in SFT data make hacking resurface and spread under RL, i.e. hacking is seeded and spreads, with the seed located in the data the model was taught on rather than in the prompt pool. 2511.18397 (neighbor abstract): hacking is taught as strategies and then generalises; no prompt-pool structure is named.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the $w_i$ arm wins: every verifier-based RL team gains a zero-fit data step — screen the prompt pool with base-model rollouts and drop or re-verify the top-$w_i$ prompts — and SimHack's fitted $\beta$ ranking is replaced by its own step-zero input; the ranking then also predicts the seed spread of onset as a first-passage time started from few prompts, which is the follow-on measurement. If matched-random ties: hacking onset is set by the unsolvable mass of the pool, prompt selection cannot separate hackable from hard, and verifier hardening is the only data-side lever. If neither removal moves onset: hacking is not seeded by a small prompt set under GRPO at this scale, and any per-prompt ranking (fitted or not) is cosmetic.

identifiability: Random given the seed: LoRA initialisation, the sampler at temperature 0.7 / top-p 0.95, and prompt order; the environment's loophole check is deterministic after the rollout, so there is no judge noise and no luck term in the label. $t_{50}$ is a first-passage time of a stochastic training process, so its seed spread is part of the quantity, and the kill criterion is stated against that spread (four seeds give a coarse interquartile range; this is the probe's thinnest point and is said so). $w_i$ is a property of the base policy, the prompt and the verifier at the training temperature — whose temperature: the training sampler's, held equal to the pre-RL rollouts — and not of the protocol, except that 'hack' is whatever the detector's rules flag, so every statement is about detectable hacking (the paper's own scope). The removed set and the matched set are fixed before any RL run.
positioning_note: Lane L2 is lab-contested and admits a candidate only as a measurement or a controlled comparison; this is a controlled comparison of two prompt removals with a data-step consequence, not a recipe, a monitor or a simulator. Solo is feasible (0.6B, a public testbed, under one GPU-week). The race risk is real and named: reward hacking in verifier RL is a frontier-lab topic (2511.18397 is a lab paper) and the SimHack authors hold 325 runs on which the $w_i$-versus-$\beta$ correlation is a zero-GPU afternoon; the solo defence is that the shipped artifact is the removal result and the screen, which they did not run and which anyone can reproduce.

scorecard.target_value: In print: SimHack's abstract asks for ways to 'select lower-risk recipes in advance' and names environment hardening as 'increasingly difficult'; its Sec. 5.2 ranks hack-seeding prompts and its introduction claims 'subsequent RL runs' confirm the ranking, with no such experiment in the text (card, weakest_component). Who pays: every team training coding models with verifiers that have loopholes; the SimHack authors themselves (a cheaper ranking); curriculum designers for RLVR (reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards — the setting where the reward is a programmatic check).

impact_ceiling.floor: A negative: the step-zero quantity carries nothing beyond difficulty, or 5% removal moves nothing; a control cited by SimHack follow-ups and by anyone proposing prompt-level hack screens; requires the 12 runs; probability 0.4 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: The $w_i$ screen works at 0.6B on one suite: a zero-fit prompt-pool screen proposed as a data step, with the identity that justifies it; requires a 4B replication (about 50 GPU-hours per run, outside the solo week) to be believed; probability 0.4 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The screen replaces fitted simulators for finding seeding prompts, predicts the seed spread of onset as a first-passage time from the top-$w_i$ prompts, and becomes a default step in RLVR data pipelines; requires two suites, 4B, and the released SimHack dataset; probability 0.2 (judgment).

relevance.routes: Narasimhan (Odysseus, EasyPPO) and any RL group: moderate — a credit-signal fact about GRPO's advantage at step zero, validated against a ground-truth hack label; L1 evaluators: weak (a verifier-validity measurement); L3/L4/L5: none.
relevance.industry: Direct: a data step for verifier-based RL on code.
relevance.jacobs_edge: The identity is an elementary moment computation on the group-normalised advantage, the kind of napkin check he favours; the LLM-RL stack itself is not his edge.
relevance.zero_where: Physics, GPU numerics, scheduling, robotics (L5); the whole L5 register is absent here.

scorecard.kill_probe: Pre-RL rollouts (8-12 GPU-hours) plus 3 arms x 4 seeds of 0.6B GRPO (about 156 GPU-hours), about $500 at A100 rates, 10 days including environment setup; kills if the $w_i$ arm's median $t_{50}$ falls inside the matched-random arm's seed interquartile range, or both removal arms fall inside the full pool's.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: From the card's neighbors only: Simfluence 2303.08114 (influence via simulated loss curves; the parent method, no RL, no hack label); CoT monitoring 2503.11926 (a training-time monitor that induces obfuscation; a different lever); Countdown-Code 2603.07084 (the separable-reward testbed; seeds located in SFT data, not in the prompt pool); 2511.18397 (hacking taught then generalising; no prompt-pool structure); Wong, Engels and Nanda (monitor-based interventions; unfetched, must be read to see whether prompt removal is among them). Not in the card and owed to the kill search: the RLVR data-selection literature that filters prompts by pass rate (zero-variance prompts give zero GRPO advantage, so difficulty filtering is common) — search in its words: 'zero-variance prompts', 'pass rate filtering', 'online difficulty filtering', 'exploitable prompts', 'test-case hacking', 'verifier loophole'. The hack-rate weighting is the new bit; whether it already exists as a filter rule inside a data-pipeline paper is unknown until the kill search runs, and density is measured on the day of writing.
scorecard.why_now: SimHack 2026-10-20 (the $S_0$ data exists and is bypassed for a fitted ranking; the removal experiment is claimed and not shown); Countdown-Code March 2026 (public separable-reward environment); 13-GPU-hour 0.6B runs make the matrix solo-affordable.
scorecard.register_and_not: A controlled comparison of two prompt removals, in the measurement register, with a data-step consequence and a one-line identity behind the ranked quantity. Not a new simulator, not a monitor, not a reward design, not a curriculum method, not a claim about onset prediction across recipes, and not a claim about undetectable hacking.

headline_test: Reward hacking in verifier-based RL is seeded by the prompts the base model can already hack but cannot solve, and a base-model rollout screen finds them before training without any fitted simulator.
